name: Aaron
description: The eldest son of Amram and Jochebed, a daughter of Levi (Ex. 6:20). Some explain the name as meaning mountaineer, others mountain of strength, illuminator.

name: Abagtha
description: One of the seven eunuchs in Ahasuerus’s court (Esther 1:10; 2:21).

name: Abda
description: The father of Adoniram, whom Solomon set over the tribute (1 Kings 4:6); i.e., the forced labour (R.V., “levy”).

name: Abdeel
description: Servant of God, (Jer. 36:26), the father of Shelemiah.

name: Abdiel
description: Servant of God, (1 Chr. 5:15), a Gadite chief.

name: Abdon
title: Abdon (son of Hillel)
description: The son of Hillel, a Pirathonite, the tenth judge of Israel (Judg. 12:13-15). He is probably the Bedan of 1 Sam. 12:11.

name: Abdon
title: Abdon (son of Shashak)
description: One of the “sons” of Shashak (1 Chr. 8:23). This is the name also of a Levitical town of the Gershonites, in the tribe of Asher (Josh. 21:30; 1 Chr. 6:74).

name: Abdon
title: Abdon (son of Abiel)
description: The first-born of Gibeon of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chr. 8:30; 9:36).

name: Abel
description: (Heb. Hebhel), a breath, or vanity, the second son of Adam and Eve. He was put to death by his brother Cain (Gen. 4:1-16).

name: Abiah
title: Abiah (son of Samuel)
description: The second son of Samuel (1 Sam. 8:2; 1 Chr. 6:28). His conduct, along with that of his brother, as a judge in Beer-sheba, to which office his father had appointed him, led to popular discontent, and ultimately provoked the people to demand a royal form of government.

name: Abiah
title: Abiah (son of Becher)
description: One of the sons of Becher, the son of Benjamin (1 Chr. 7:8). “Abiah,” A.V.

name: Abiathar
description: Father of abundance, or my father excels, the son of Ahimelech the high priest. He was the tenth high priest, and the fourth in descent from Eli.

name: Abida
description: Or Abi’dah, father of knowledge; knowing, one of the five sons of Midian, who was the son of Abraham by Keturah (1 Chr. 1:33), and apparently the chief of an Arab tribe.

name: Abidan
description: Father of judgment; judge, head of the tribe of Benjamin at the Exodus (Num. 1:11; 2:22).

name: Abiel
title: Abiel (Arbathite)
description: An Arbathite, one of David’s warriors (1 Chr. 11:32); called also Abi-albon (2 Sam. 23:31).

name: Abiel
description: The son of Zeror and father of Ner, who was the grandfather of Saul (1 Sam. 14:51; 1 Chr. 8:33; 9:39). In 1 Sam. 9:1, he is called the “father,” probably meaning the grandfather, of Kish.

name: Abiezer
title: Abiezer (2 Samuel 23:27)
description: One of David’s thirty warriors (2 Sam. 23:27; comp. 1 Chr. 27:12).

name: Abiezer
title: Abiezer (son of Gilead)
description: The second of the three sons of Hammoleketh, the sister of Gilead. He was the grandson of Manasseh (1 Chr. 7:18). From his family Gideon sprang (Josh. 17:2; comp. Judg. 6:34; 8:2).

name: Abigail
description: The wife of the churlish Nabal, who dwelt in the district of Carmel (1 Sam. 25:3). She showed great prudence and delicate management at a critical period of her husband’s life.

name: Abigail
title: Abigail (daughter of Nahash)
description: The sister of David, and wife of Jether an Ishmaelite (1 Chr. 2:16, 17). She was the mother of Amasa (2 Sam. 17:25).

name: Abihail
title: Abihail (daughter of Eliab)
description: The second wife of King Rehoboam (2 Chr. 11:18), a descendant of Eliab, David’s eldest brother.

name: Abihail
title: Abihail (father of Esther)
description: The father of Esther and uncle of Mordecai (Esther 2:15).

name: Abihu
description: Father of Him; i.e., “worshipper of God”, the second of the sons of Aaron (Ex. 6:23; Num. 3:2; 26:60; 1 Chr. 6:3). Along with his three brothers he was consecrated to the priest’s office (Ex. 28:1).

name: Abihud
description: One of the sons of Bela, the son of Benjamin (1 Chr. 8:3); called also Ahihud (ver. 7).

name: Abijah
title: Abijah (daughter of Zechariah)
description: The daughter of Zechariah (2 Chr. 29:1; comp. Isa. 8:2), and afterwards the wife of Ahaz. She is also called Abi (2 Kings 18:2).

name: Abijah
title: Abijah (son of Jeroboam)
description: A son of Jeroboam, the first king of Israel. On account of his severe illness when a youth, his father sent his wife to consult the prophet Ahijah regarding his recovery.

name: Abijah
title: Abijah (1 Chronicles 24:10)
description: A descendant of Eleazar, the son of Aaron, a chief of one of the twenty-four orders into which the priesthood was divided by David (1 Chr. 24:10). The order of Abijah was one of those which did not return from the Captivity (Ezra 2:36-39; Neh. 7:39-42; 12:1).

name: Abijah
description: The son of Rehoboam, whom he succeeded on the throne of Judah (1 Chr. 3:10). He is also called Abijam (1 Kings 14:31; 15:1-8).

name: Abimael
description: Father of Mael, one of the sons or descendants of Joktan, in Northern Arabia (Gen. 10:28; 1 Chr. 1:22).

name: Abimelech
title: Abimelech (King of Gerar)
description: A king of Gerar in the time of Isaac, probably the son of the preceeding (Gen. 26:1-22). Isaac sought refuge in his territory during a famine, and there he acted a part with reference to his wife Rebekah similar to that of his father Abraham with reference to Sarah.

name: Abimelech
description: A son of Gideon (Judg. 9:1), who was proclaimed king after the death of his father (Judg. 8:33-9:6). One of his first acts was to murder his brothers, seventy in number, “on one stone,” at Ophrah.

name: Abinadab
title: Abinadab (father of Uzzah)
description: A Levite of Kirjath-jearim, in whose house the ark of the covenant was deposited after having been brought back from the land of the Philistines (1 Sam. 7:1). It remained there twenty years, till it was at length removed by David (1 Sam. 7:1, 2; 1 Chr. 13:7).

name: Abinadab
title: Abinadab (son of Jesse)
description: The second of the eight sons of Jesse (1 Sam. 16:8). He was with Saul in the campaign against the Philistines in which Goliath was slain (1 Sam. 17:13).

name: Abinadab
title: Abinadab (father of son of Abinadab)
description: One of Solomon’s officers, who “provided victuals for the king and his household.” He presided, for this purpose, over the district of Dor (1 Kings 4:11).

name: Abinadab
title: Abinadab (son of Saul)
description: One of Saul’s sons, who peristed with his father in the battle of Gilboa (1 Sam. 31:2; 1 Chr. 10:2).

name: Abinoam
description: Father of kindness, the father of Barak (Judg. 4:6; 5:1).

name: Abiram
title: Abiram (son of Eliab)
description: One of the sons of Eliab, who joined Korah in the conspiracy against Moses and Aaron. He and all the conspirators, with their families and possessions (except the children of Korah), were swallowed up by an earthquake (Num. 16:1-27; 26:9; Ps. 106:17).

name: Abiram
description: The eldest son of Hiel the Bethelite, who perished prematurely in consequence of his father’s undertaking to rebuild Jericho (1 Kings 16:34), according to the words of Joshua (6:26).

name: Abishag
description: Father of (i.e., “given to”) error, a young woman of Shunem, distinguished for her beauty. She was chosen to minister to David in his old age.

name: Abishai
description: Father of (i.e., “desirous of”) a gift, the eldest son of Zeruiah, David’s sister. He was the brother of Joab and Asahel (2 Sam. 2:18; 1 Chr. 2:16).

name: Abishua
title: Abishua (son of Phinehas)
description: The son of Phinehas the high priest (1 Chr. 6:4, 5, 50; Ezra 7:5).

name: Abishua
title: Abishua (son of Bela)
description: The grandson of Benjamin (1 Chr. 8:4).

name: Abishur
description: Father of the wall; i.e., “mason”, one of the two sons of Shammai of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr. 2:28, 29).

name: Abital
description: Father of dew; i.e., “fresh”, David’s fifth wife (2 Sam. 3:4).

name: Abitub
description: Father of goodness, a Benjamite (1 Chr. 8:11).

name: Abiud
description: A descendant of Zerubbabel and father of Eliakim (Matt. 1:13, “Abiud”); called also Juda (Luke 3:26), and Obadiah (1 Chr. 3:21).

name: Abner
description: Father of light; i.e., “enlightening”, the son of Ner and uncle of Saul. He was commander-in-chief of Saul’s army (1 Sam. 14:50; 17:55; 20:25).

name: Abraham
description: Father of a multitude, son of Terah, named (Gen. 11:27) before his older brothers Nahor and Haran, because he was the heir of the promises.

name: Absalom
description: Father of peace; i.e., “peaceful” David’s son by Maacah (2 Sam. 3:3; comp. 1 Kings 1:6). He was noted for his personal beauty and for the extra-ordinary profusion of the hair of his head (2 Sam. 14:25,26).

name: Achaicus
description: (1 Cor. 16:17), one of the members of the church of Corinth who, with Fortunatus and Stephanas, visited Paul while he was at Ephesus, for the purpose of consulting him on the affairs of the church.

name: Achan
description: Called also Achar, i.e., one who troubles (1 Chr. 2:7), in commemoration of his crime, which brought upon him an awful destruction (Josh. 7:1).

name: Achbor
title: Achbor (father of Baal-hanan)
description: An Edomitish king (Gen. 36:38; 1 Chr. 1:49).

name: Achbor
title: Achbor (son of Michaiah)
description: The son of Micah, one of those whom Josiah sent to the prophetess Huldah to ascertain from her the meaning of the recently discovered book of the law (2 Chr. 34:20). He is called Achbor in 2 Kings 22:12.

name: Achish
description: The king with whom David sought refuge when he fled from Saul (1 Sam. 21:10-15). He is called Abimelech in the superscription of Ps. 34.

name: Achsah
description: Anklet, Caleb’s only daughter (1 Chr. 2:49). She was offered in marriage to the man who would lead an attack on the city of Debir, or Kirjath-sepher.

name: Adah
title: Adah (wife of Lamech)
description: The first of Lamech’s two wives, and the mother of Jabal and Jubal (Gen. 4:19, 20, 23).

name: Adah
description: The first of Esau’s three wives, the daughter of Elon the Hittite (Gen. 36:2, 4), called also Bashemath (26:34).

name: Adaiah
title: Adaiah (son of Ethan)
description: Timely (1 Chr. 6:21). A Gershonite Levite.

name: Adam
description: Red, a Babylonian word, the generic name for man, having the same meaning in the Hebrew and the Assyrian languages. It was the name given to the first man, whose creation, fall, and subsequent history and that of his descendants are detailed in the first book of Moses (Gen. 1:27-ch. 5).

name: Adbeel
description: Miracle of God, the third of the twelve sons of Ishmael, and head of an Arabian tribe (Gen. 25:13; 1 Chr. 1:29).

name: Addar
description: Ample, splendid, son of Bela (1 Chr. 8:3); called also “Ard” (Gen. 46:21)

name: Addi
description: Ornament, (Luke 3:28), the son of Cosam, and father of Melchi, one of the progenitors of Christ.

name: Adiel
title: Adiel (1 Chronicles 4:36)
description: A family head of the tribe of Simeon (1 Chr. 4:36).

name: Adina
description: Slender, one of David’s warriors (1 Chr. 11:42), a Reubenite.

name: Adino
description: The Eznite, one of David’s mighty men (2 Sam. 23:8).

name: Adnah
title: Adnah (1 Chronicles 12:20)
description: A chief of the tribe of Manasseh who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:20).

name: Adnah
title: Adnah (2 Chronicles 17:14)
description: A general under Jehoshaphat, chief over 300,000 men (2 Chr. 17:14).

name: Adonijah
description: The fourth son of David (2 Sam. 3:4). After the death of his elder brothers, Amnon and Absalom, he became heir-apparent to the throne.

name: Adonijah
title: Adonijah (2 Chronicles 17:8)
description: A Levite sent with the princes to teach the book of the law to the inhabitants of Judah (2 Chr. 17:8).

name: Adonijah
title: Adonijah (Nehemiah 10:16)
description: One of the “chiefs of the people” after the Captivity (Neh. 10:16).

name: Adonikam
description: Whom the Lord sets up, one of those “which came with Zerubbabel” (Ezra 2:13). His “children,” or retainers, to the number of 666, came up to Jerusalem (8:13).

name: Adoniram
description: One who was “over the tribute;” i.e., “over the levy.” He was stoned by the Israelites after they had revolted from Rehoboam (2 Chr. 10:18).

name: Adrammelech
title: Adrammelech (2 Kings 17:31)
description: An idol; a form of the sun-god worshipped by the inhabitants of Sepharvaim (2 Kings 17:31), and brought by the Sepharvite colonists into Samaria.

name: Adrammelech
title: Adrammelech (son of Sennacherib)
description: A son of Sennacherib, king of Assyria (2 Kings 19:37; Isa. 37:38).

name: Adriel
description: Flock of God, the son of Barzillai, the Meholathite, to whom Saul gave in marriage his daughter Merab (1 Sam. 18:19).

name: Agabus
description: A “prophet,” probably one of the seventy disciples of Christ. He prophesied at Antioch of an approaching famine (Acts 11:27, 28).

name: Agag
title: Agag (Numbers 24:7)
description: A king of the Amalekites referred to by Balaam (Num. 24:7). He lived at the time of the Exodus.

name: Agag
title: Agag (1 Samuel 15:8)
description: Another king of the Amalekites whom Saul spared unlawfully, but whom Samuel on his arrival in the camp of Saul ordered, in retributive justice (Judg. 1), to be brought out and cut in pieces (1 Sam. 15:8-33. Comp. Ex. 17:11; Num. 14:45).

name: Agee
description: Fugitive, the father of Shammah, who was one of David’s mighty men (2 Sam. 23:11)

name: Agrippa
description: Son of the foregoing, was born at Rome, A.D. 27. He was the brother of Bernice and Drusilla. The Emperor Claudius (A.D. 48) invested him with the office of superintendent of the Temple of Jerusalem, and made him governor (A.D. 50) of Chalcis.

name: Agur
description: Gatherer; the collector, mentioned as author of the sayings in Prov. 30. Nothing is known of him beyond what is there recorded.

name: Ahab
description: The son of Omri, whom he succeeded as the seventh king of Israel. His history is recorded in 1 Kings 16-22. His wife was Jezebel (q.v.), who exercised a very evil influence over him.

name: Ahab
title: Ahab (son of Kolaiah)
description: A false prophet referred to by Jeremiah (Jer. 29:21), of whom nothing further is known.

name: Ahasuerus
description: The son of Darius Hystaspes, the king named in the Book of Esther. He ruled over the kingdoms of Persia, Media, and Babylonia, “from India to Ethiopia.”

name: Ahaz
description: The son and successor of Jotham, king of Judah (2 Kings 16; Isa. 7-9; 2 Chr. 28). He gave himself up to a life of wickedness and idolatry.

name: Ahaz
title: Ahaz (son of Micah)
description: A grandson of Jonathan (1 Chr. 8:35; 9:42).

name: Ahaziah
title: Ahaziah (son of Ahab)
description: The son and successor of Ahab. He followed the counsels of his mother Jezebel, and imitated in wickedness the ways of his father.

name: Ahaziah
description: The son of Joram, or Jehoram, and sixth king of Judah. Called Jehoahaz (2 Chr. 21:17; 25:23), and Azariah (2 Chr. 22:6).

name: Ahiah
title: Ahiah (son of Shavsha)
description: One of Solomon’s secretaries (1 Kings 4:3).

name: Ahiah
title: Ahiah (son of Ehud)
description: One of the sons of Bela (1 Chr. 8:7, R.V.). In A.V. called “Ahiah.”

name: Ahiam
description: Mother’s brother, one of David’s thirty heroes (2 Sam. 23:33; 1 Chr. 11:35).

name: Ahiezer
title: Ahiezer (son of Shemaah)
description: The chief of the Benjamite slingers that repaired to David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:3).

name: Ahihud
title: Ahihud (son of Shelomi)
description: Name different in Hebrew, meaning brother of Judah. Chief of the tribe of Asher; one of those appointed by Moses to superintend the division of Canaan among the tribe (Num. 34:27).

name: Ahihud
title: Ahihud (son of Ehud)
description: A son of Bela, the son of Benjamin (1 Chr. 8:7).

name: Ahijah
title: Ahijah (1 Kings 11:29)
description: A prophet of Shiloh (1 Kings 11:29; 14:2), called the “Shilonite,” in the days of Rehoboam.

name: Ahijah
title: Ahijah (son of Jerahmeel)
description: One of the five sons of Jerahmeel, who was great-grandson of Judah (1 Chr. 2:25).

name: Ahijah
title: Ahijah (1 Chronicles 11:36)
description: A Pelonite, one of David’s heroes (1 Chr. 11:36); called also Eliam (2 Sam. 23:34).

name: Ahijah
title: Ahijah (1 Chronicles 26:20)
description: A Levite having charge of the sacred treasury in the temple (1 Chr. 26:20).

name: Ahikam
description: Brother of support = helper, one of the five whom Josiah sent to consult the prophetess Huldah in connection with the discovery of the book of the law (2 Kings 22:12-14; 2 Chr. 34:20).

name: Ahimaaz
title: Ahimaaz (father of Ahinoam)
description: The father Ahinoam, the wife of Saul (1 Sam. 14:50).

name: Ahimaaz
description: The son and successor of Zadok in the office of high priest (1 Chr. 6:8, 53). On the occasion of the revolt of Absalom he remained faithful to David, and was of service to him in conveying to him tidings of the proceedings of Absalom in Jerusalem (2 Sam. 15:24-37; 17:15-21).

name: Ahiman
title: Ahiman (son of Anak)
description: One of the three giant Anakim brothers whom Caleb and the spies saw in Mount Hebron (Num. 13:22) when they went in to explore the land. They were afterwards driven out and slain (Josh. 15:14; Judg. 1:10).

name: Ahiman
title: Ahiman (1 Chronicles 9:17)
description: One of the guardians of the temple after the Exile (1 Chr. 9:17).

name: Ahimelech
title: Ahimelech (son of Ahitub)
description: Son of Ahitub (1 Sam. 14:3, 18), Ichabod’s brother; the same probably as Ahimelech, who was high priest at Nob in the reign of Saul (1 Sam. 22:11).

name: Ahimelech
title: Ahimelech (son of Abiathar)
description: The son of Abiathar, and high priest in the time of David (1 Chr. 18:16). In the parallel passage, 2 Sam. 8:17, we have the name Ahimelech, and Abiathar, the son of Ahimelech.

name: Ahinadab
description: Brother of liberality = liberal, one of the twelve commissariat officers appointed by Solomon in so many districts of his kingdom to raise supplies by monthly rotation for his household. He was appointed to the district of Mahanaim (1 Kings 4:14), east of Jordan.

name: Ahinoam
title: Ahinoam (daughter of Ahimaaz)
description: The daughter of Ahimaaz, and wife of Saul (1 Sam. 14:50).

name: Ahinoam
title: Ahinoam (mother of Amnon)
description: A Jezreelitess, the first wife of David (1 Sam. 25:43; 27:3). She was the mother of Amnon (2 Sam. 3:2). (See 1 Sam. 30:5, 18; 2 Sam. 2:2.)

name: Ahio
title: Ahio (son of Abinadab)
description: One of the sons of Abinadab the Levite. While Uzzah went by the side of the ark, he walked before it guiding the oxen which drew the cart on which it was carried, after having brought it from his father’s house in Gibeah (1 Chr. 13:7; 2 Sam. 6:3, 4).

name: Ahio
title: Ahio (son of Beriah)
description: One of the sons of Beriah (1 Chr. 8:14).

name: Ahio
title: Ahio (son of Abiel)
description: One of the sons of Jehiel the Gibeonite (1 Chr. 8:31; 9:37).

name: Ahira
description: Brother of evil = unlucky, or my brother is friend, chief of the tribe of Naphtali at the Exodus (Num. 1:15; 2:29).

name: Ahishar
description: Brother of song = singer, the officer who was “over the household” of Solomon (1 Kings 4:6).

name: Ahithophel
description: Brother of insipidity or impiety, a man greatly renowned for his sagacity among the Jews. At the time of Absalom’s revolt he deserted David (Ps. 41:9; 55:12-14) and espoused the cause of Absalom (2 Sam. 15:12).

name: Ahitub
title: Ahitub (son of Phinehas)
description: The son of Phinehas. On the death of his grandfather Eli he succeeded to the office of high priest, and was himself succeeded by his son Ahijah (1 Sam. 14:3; 22:9, 11, 12, 20).

name: Ahitub
title: Ahitub (son of Amariah, 2 Samuel 8:17)
description: The father of Zadok, who was made high priest by Saul after the extermination of the family of Ahimelech (1 Chr. 6:7, 8; 2 Sam. 8:17).

name: Ahoah
description: Brotherly, one of the sons of Bela, the son of Benjamin (1 Chr. 8:4). He is also called Ahiah (ver. 7) and Iri (1 Chr. 7:7).

name: Aholiab
description: Tent of the father, an artist of the tribe of Dan, appointed to the work of preparing materials for the tabernacle (Ex. 31:6; 35:34; 36:1, 2; 38:23).

name: Aholibah
description: My tent is in her, the name of an imaginary harlot, applied symbolically to Jerusalem, because she had abandoned the worship of the true God and given herself up to the idolatries of foreign nations. (Ezek. 23:4, 11, 22, 36, 44).

name: Aholibamah
title: Aholibamah (daughter of Beeri)
description: Jewess, the daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and one of Esau’s wives (Gen. 26:34), elsewhere called Aholibamah (36:2-14).

name: Akan
description: He twists, one of the sons of Ezer, the son of Seir the Horite (1 Chr. 1:42).

name: Akkub
title: Akkub (son of Elioenai)
description: A descendant of David (1 Chr. 3:24).

name: Akkub
title: Akkub (1 Chronicles 9:17)
description: A Levite who kept the gate of the temple after the return from Babylon (1 Chr. 9:17; Ezra 2:42; Neh. 7:45).

name: Akkub
title: Akkub (Ezra 2:45)
description: The head of one of the families of Nethinim (Ezra 2:45).

name: Alameth
description: One of the nine sons of Becher, the son of Benjamin (1 Chr. 7:8).

name: Alemeth
description: One of the sons of Jehoadah, or Jarah, son of Ahaz (1 Chr. 8:36).

name: Alexander
title: Alexander (son of Simon)
description: A man whose father, Simon the Cyrenian, bore the cross of Christ (Mark 15:21).

name: Alexander
title: Alexander (Son of Simon)
description: A relative of Annas the high priest, present when Peter and John were examined before the Sanhedrim (Acts 4:6).

name: Alexander
title: Alexander (Jew of Ephesus)
description: A Jew of Ephesus who took a prominent part in the uproar raised there by the preaching of Paul (Acts 19:33). The Jews put him forward to plead their cause before the mob.

name: Alexander
title: Alexander (1 Timothy 1:20)
description: A coppersmith who, with Hymenaeus and others, promulgated certain heresies regarding the resurrection (1 Tim. 1:19; 2 Tim. 4:14), and made shipwreck of faith and of a good conscience. Paul excommunicated him (1 Tim. 1:20; comp. 1 Cor. 5:5).

name: Allon
description: The son of Jedaiah, of the family of the Simeonites, who expelled the Hamites from the valley of Gedor (1 Chr. 4:37).

name: Almodad
description: Immeasurable, the first named of the sons of Joktan (Gen. 10:26), the founder of an Arabian tribe.

name: Alphaeus
title: Alphaeus (father of James)
description: The father of James the Less, the apostle and writer of the epistle (Matt. 10:3; Mark 3:18; Luke 6:15; Acts 1:13), and the husband of Mary (John 19:25). The Hebrew form of this name is Cleopas, or Clopas (q.v.).

name: Alphaeus
title: Alphaeus (father of Matthew)
description: The father of Levi, or Matthew (Mark 2:14).

name: Amalek
description: Dweller in a valley, the son of Eliphaz and grandson of Esau (Gen. 36:12; 1 Chr. 1:36); the chief of an Idumean tribe (Gen. 36:16). His mother was a Horite, a tribe whose territory the descendants of Esau had seized.

name: Amariah
title: Amariah (son of Meraioth)
description: One of the descendants of Aaron by Eleazar (1 Chr. 6:7, 52). He was probably the last of the high priests of Eleazar’s line prior to the transfer of that office to Eli, of the line of Ithamar.

name: Amariah
title: Amariah (son of Hebron)
description: A Levite, son of Hebron, of the lineage of Moses (1 Chr. 23:19; 24:23).

name: Amariah
title: Amariah (2 Chronicles 19:11)
description: A “chief priest” who took an active part in the reformation under Jehoshaphat (2 Chr. 19:11); probably the same as mentioned in 1 Chr. 6:9.

name: Amariah
title: Amariah (2 Chronicles 31:15)
description: One of the high priests in the time of Hezekiah (2 Chr. 31:15).

name: Amasa
description: The son of Abigail, a sister of king David (1 Chr. 2:17; 2 Sam. 17:25). He was appointed by David to command the army in room of his cousin Joab (2 Sam. 19:13), who afterwards treacherously put him to death as a dangerous rival (2 Sam. 20:4-12).

name: Amasa
title: Amasa (son of Hadlai)
description: A son of Hadlai, and chief of Ephraim (2 Chr. 28:12) in the reign of Ahaz.

name: Amasai
title: Amasai (son of Elkanah)
description: A Levite, son of Elkanah, of the ancestry of Samuel (1 Chr. 6:25, 35).

name: Amasai
title: Amasai (1 Chronicles 12:18)
description: The leader of a body of men who joined David in the “stronghold,” probably of Adullam (1 Chr. 12:18).

name: Amasai
title: Amasai (1 Chronicles 15:24)
description: One of the priests appointed to precede the ark with blowing of trumpets on its removal from the house of Obed-edom (1 Chr. 15:24).

name: Amasai
title: Amasai (father of Mahath)
description: The father of a Levite, one of the two Kohathites who took a prominent part at the instance of Hezekiah in the cleansing of the temple (2 Chr. 29:12).

name: Amasiah
description: Burden of (i.e., “sustained by”) Jehovah, the “son of Zichri, who willingly offered himself unto the Lord,” a captain over thousands under Jehoshaphat (2 Chr. 17:16; comp. Judg. 5:9).

name: Amaziah
description: The son and successor of Joash, and eighth king of the separate kingdom of Judah (2 Kings 14:1-4). He began his reign by punishing the murderers of his father (5-7; 2 Chr. 25:3-5).

name: Amaziah
title: Amaziah (father of Joshah)
description: The father of Joshah, one of the Simeonite chiefs in the time of Hezekiah (1 Chr. 4:34).

name: Amaziah
title: Amaziah (son of Hilkiah)
description: A Levite, son of Hilkiah, of the descendants of Ethan the Merarite (1 Chr. 6:45).

name: Amaziah
title: Amaziah (Amos 7:10)
description: A priest of the golden calves at Bethel (Amos 7:10-17).

name: Amittai
description: True, the father of Jonah the prophet, a native of Gath-hepher (2 Kings 14:25; Jonah 1:1).

name: Ammiel
title: Ammiel (son of Gemalli)
description: One of the twelve spies sent by Moses to search the land of Canaan (Num. 13:12). He was one of the ten who perished by the plague for their unfavourable report (Num. 14:37).

name: Ammiel
title: Ammiel (father of Machir)
description: The father of Machir of Lo-debar, in whose house Mephibosheth resided (2 Sam. 9:4, 5; 17:27).

name: Ammiel
title: Ammiel (son of Shimei)
description: One of the sons of Obed-edom the Levite (1 Chr. 26:5).

name: Ammihud
title: Ammihud (son of Laadan)
description: The father of the Ephraimite chief Elishama, at the time of the Exodus (Num. 1:10; 2:18; 7:48, 53).

name: Ammihud
title: Ammihud (father of Talmai)
description: The father of Talmai, king of Geshur, to whom Absalom fled after the murder of Amnon (2 Sam. 13:37).

name: Ammihud
title: Ammihud (son of Omri)
description: The son of Omri, and the father of Uthai (1 Chr. 9:4).

name: Amminadab
description: The father of Nahshon, who was chief of the tribe of Judah (Num. 1:7; 2:3; 7:12, 17; 10:14). His daughter Elisheba was married to Aaron (Ex. 6:23).

name: Amminadab
title: Amminadab (1 Chronicles 15:10)
description: Chief of the 112 descendants of Uzziel the Levite (1 Chr. 15:10, 11).

name: Ammishaddai
description: People of the Almighty, the father of Ahiezer, who was chief of the Danites at the time of the Exodus (Num. 1:12; 2:25). This is one of the few names compounded with the name of God, Shaddai, “Almighty.”

name: Ammizabad
description: People of the giver, the son of Benaiah, who was the third and chief captain of the host under David (1 Chr. 27:6).

name: Amnon
description: The eldest son of David, by Ahinoam of Jezreel (1 Chr. 3:1; 2 Sam. 3:2). Absalom caused him to be put to death for his great crime in the matter of Tamar (2 Sam. 13:28, 29).

name: Amnon
title: Amnon (son of Shimon)
description: One of the sons of Shammai, of the children of Ezra (1 Chr. 4:20; comp. 17).

name: Amon
title: Amon (1 Kings 22:26)
description: The governor of Samaria in the time of Ahab. The prophet Micaiah was committed to his custody (1 Kings 22:26; 2 Chr. 18:25).

name: Amon
description: The son of Manasseh, and fourteenth king of Judah. He restored idolatry, and set up the images which his father had cast down.

name: Amorite
description: Highlanders, or hillmen, the name given to the descendants of one of the sons of Canaan (Gen. 14:7), called Amurra or Amurri in the Assyrian and Egyptian inscriptions.

name: Amos
title: Amos (Amos 1:1)
description: Borne; a burden, one of the twelve minor prophets. He was a native of Tekota, the modern Tekua, a town about 12 miles south-east of Bethlehem.

name: Amoz
description: Strong, the father of the prophet Isaiah (2 Kings 19:2, 20; 20:1; Isa. 1:1; 2:1). As to his personal history little is positively known.

name: Amplias
description: A Roman Christian saluted by Paul (Rom. 16:8).

name: Amram
description: The son of Kohath, the son of Levi. He married Jochebed, “his father’s sister,” and was the father of Aaron, Miriam, and Moses (Ex. 6:18, 20; Num. 3:19).

name: Amraphel
description: King of Shinar, southern Chaldea, one of the confederates of Chedorlaomer, king of Elam, in a war against Sodom and cities of the plain (Gen. 14:1, 4).

name: Anak
description: Long-necked, the son of Arba, father of the Anakim (Josh. 15:13; 21:11, Heb. Anok).

name: Anamim
description: The name of an Egyptian tribe descended from Mizraim (Gen. 10:13; 1 Chr. 1:11).

name: Anammelech
description: One of the gods worshipped by the people of Sepharvaim, who colonized Samaria (2 Kings 17:31). The name means “Anu is king.”

name: Anan
description: Cloud, one of the Israelites who sealed the covenant after the return from Babylon (Neh. 10:26).

name: Ananias
title: Ananias (Husband of Sapphira)
description: One of the members of the church at Jerusalem, who conspired with his wife Sapphira to deceive the brethren, and who fell down and immediately expired after he had uttered the falsehood (Acts 5:5).

name: Ananias
title: Ananias (Disciple at Damascus)
description: A Christian at Damascus (Acts 9:10). He became Paul’s instructor; but when or by what means he himself became a Christian we have no information.

name: Ananias
title: Ananias (High Priest)
description: The high priest before whom Paul was brought in the procuratorship of Felix (Acts 23:2, 5, 24). He was so enraged at Paul’s noble declaration, “I have lived in all good conscience before God until this day,” that he commanded one of his attendants to smite him on the mouth.

name: Anath
description: An answer; i.e., to “prayer”, the father of Shamgar, who was one of the judges of Israel (Judg. 3:31).

name: Andrew
description: Manliness, a Greek name; one of the apostles of our Lord. He was of Bethsaida in Galilee (John 1:44), and was the brother of Simon Peter (Matt. 4:18; 10:2).

name: Andronicus
description: Man-conquering, a Jewish Christian, the kinsman and fellowprisoner of Paul (Rom. 16:7); “of note among the apostles.”

name: Aner
description: A Canaanitish chief who joined his forces with those of Abraham in pursuit of Chedorlaomer (Gen. 14:13, 24).

name: Anna
description: Grace, an aged widow, the daughter of Phanuel. She was a “prophetess,” like Miriam, Deborah, and Huldah (2 Chr. 34:22). After seven years of married life her husband died, and during her long widowhood she daily attended the temple services.

name: Annas
description: Was high priest A.D. 7-14. In A.D. 25 Caiaphas, who had married the daughter of Annas (John 18:13), was raised to that office, and probably Annas was now made president of the Sanhedrim, or deputy or coadjutor of the high priest, and thus was also called high priest along with Caiaphas (Luke 3:2).

name: Antipas
description: A “faithful martyr” (Rev. 2:13), of whom nothing more is certainly known.

name: Apelles
description: A Christian at Rome whom Paul salutes (Rom. 16:10), and styles “approved in Christ.”

name: Apollos
description: A Jew “born at Alexandria,” a man well versed in the Scriptures and eloquent (Acts 18:24; R.V., “learned”). He came to Ephesus (about A.D. 49), where he spake “boldly” in the synagogue (18:26), although he did not know as yet that Jesus of Nazareth was the Messiah.

name: Apollyon
description: Destruction, the Hebrew name (equivalent to the Greek Apollyon, i.e., destroyer) of “the angel of the bottomless pit” (Rev. 9:11).

name: Apphia
description: Increasing, a female Christian at Colosse (Philemon 1:2), supposed by some to have been the wife of Philemon.

name: Aquila
description: Eagle, a native of Pontus, by occupation a tent-maker, whom Paul met on his first visit to Corinth (Acts 18:2). Along with his wife Priscilla he had fled from Rome in consequence of a decree (A.D. 50) by Claudius commanding all Jews to leave the city.

name: Arad
description: One of the sons of Beriah (1 Chr. 8:15).

name: Aram
title: Aram (son of Shem)
description: The son of Shem (Gen. 10:22); according to Gen. 22:21, a grandson of Nahor. In Matt. 1:3, 4, and Luke 3:33, this word is the Greek form of Ram, the father of Amminadab (1 Chr. 2:10).

name: Aram
title: Aram (son of Kemuel)
description: The son of Shem (Gen. 10:22); according to Gen. 22:21, a grandson of Nahor. In Matt. 1:3, 4, and Luke 3:33, this word is the Greek form of Ram, the father of Amminadab (1 Chr. 2:10).

name: Aran
description: Wild goat, a descendant of Seir the Horite (Gen. 36:28).

name: Archelaus
description: Ruler of the people, son of Herod the Great, by Malthace, a Samaritan woman. He was educated along with his brother Antipas at Rome.

name: Archippus
description: Master of the horse, a “fellow-soldier” of Paul’s (Philemon 1:2), whom he exhorts to renewed activity (Col. 4:17). He was a member of Philemon’s family, probably his son.

name: Ard
title: Ard (son of Bela)
description: Descent, a grandson of Benjamin (Num. 26:38-40). In 1 Chr. 8:3 he is called Addar. His descendants are mentioned in Num. 26:40.

name: Ardon
description: Descendant, the last of the three sons of Caleb by his first wife Azubah (1 Chr. 2:18).

name: Aretas
description: The father-in-law of Herod Antipas, and king of Arabia Petraea. His daughter returned to him on the occasion of her husband’s entering into an adulterous alliance with Herodias, the wife of Herod-Philip, his half-brother (Luke 3:19, 20; Mark 6:17; Matt. 14:3).

name: Arieh
description: The lion, the name of one of the body-guard slain with Pekahiah at Samaria (2 Kings 15:25) by the conspirator Pekah.

name: Ariel
description: One of the chief men sent by Ezra to procure Levites for the sanctuary (Ezra 8:16).

name: Arioch
title: Arioch (king of Ellasar)
description: A king of Ellasar who was confederate with Chedorlamer (Gen. 14:1, 9). The tablets recently discovered by Mr. Pinches (see CHALDEA) show the true reading is Eri-Aku of Larsa.

name: Aristarchus
description: Best ruler, native of Thessalonica (Acts 20:4), a companion of Paul (Acts 19:29; 27:2). He was Paul’s “fellow-prisoner” at Rome (Col. 4:10; Philemon 1:24).

name: Arkite
description: (Gen. 10:17; 1 Chr. 1:15), a designation of certain descendants from the Phoenicians or Sidonians, the inhabitants of Arka, 12 miles north of Tripoli, opposite the northern extremity of Lebanon.

name: Armoni
description: Inhabitant of a fortress, the first-named of the two sons of Saul and Rizpah. He was delivered up to the Gibeonites by David, and hanged by them (2 Sam. 21:8, 9).

name: Arphaxad
description: Son of Shem, born the year after the Deluge. He died at the age of 438 years (Gen. 11:10-13; 1 Chr. 1:17, 18; Luke 3:36).

name: Artaxerxes
title: Artaxerxes (Ezra 4:7)
description: The king who obstructed the rebuilding of the temple (Ezra 4:7). He was probably the Smerdis of profane history.

name: Artaxerxes
description: The king mentioned in Ezra 7:1, in the seventh year (B.C. 458) of whose reign Ezra led a second colony of Jews back to Jerusalem, was probably Longimanus, who reigned for forty years (B.C. 464-425); the grandson of Darius, who, fourteen years later, permitted Nehemiah to return and rebuild…

name: Asa
description: Physician, son of Abijah and grandson of Rehoboam, was the third king of Judah. He was zealous in maintaining the true worship of God, and in rooting all idolatry, with its accompanying immoralities, out of the land (1 Kings 15:8-14).

name: Asahel
description: Made by God, the youngest son of Zeruiah, David’s sister. He was celebrated for his swiftness of foot. When fighting against Ish-bosheth at Gibeon, in the army of his brother Joab, he was put to death by Abner, whom he pursued from the field of battle (2 Sam. 2:18, 19).

name: Asahiah
description: The son of Amoz (Isa. 1:1; 2:1), who was apparently a man of humble rank. His wife was called “the prophetess” (8:3), either because she was endowed with the prophetic gift, like Deborah (Judg. 4:4) and Huldah (2 Kings 22:14-20), or simply because she was the wife of “the prophet” (Isa. 38:1).

name: Asaph
title: Asaph (father of Joah)
description: The “recorder” in the time of Hezekiah (2 Kings 18:18, 37).

name: Asaph
title: Asaph (Levite)
description: A Levite; one of the leaders of David’s choir (1 Chr. 6:39). Psalms 50 and 73-83 inclusive are attributed to him. He is mentioned along with David as skilled in music, and a “seer” (2 Chr. 29:30).

name: Asaph
title: Asaph (Nehemiah 2:8)
description: The “keeper of the king’s forest,” to whom Nehemiah requested from Artaxerxes a “letter” that he might give him timber for the temple at Jerusalem (Neh. 2:8).

name: Asenath
description: An Egyptian name, meaning “gift of the sun-god”, daughter of Potipherah, priest of On or Heliopolis, wife of Joseph (Gen. 41:45). She was the mother of Manasseh and Ephraim (50-52; 46:20).

name: Asher
description: Happy, Jacob’s eigth son; his mother was Zilpah, Leah’s handmaid (Gen. 30:13). Of the tribe founded by him nothing is recorded beyond its holding a place in the list of the tribes (35:26; 46:17; Ex. 1:4, etc.) It increased in numbers twenty-nine percent, during the thirty-eight years’ wanderings.

name: Ashkenaz
description: One of the three sons of Gomer (Gen. 10:3), and founder of one of the tribes of the Japhetic race.

name: Ashpenaz
description: The master of the eunuchs of Nebuchadnezzar (Dan. 1:3), the “Rabsaris” of the court. His position was similar to that of the Kislar-aga of the modern Turkish sultans.

name: Ashtoreth
description: The moon goddess of the Phoenicians, representing the passive principle in nature, their principal female deity; frequently associated with the name of Baal, the sun-god, their chief male deity (Judg. 10:6; 1 Sam. 7:4; 12:10).

name: Asnappar
description: Probably the same as Assur-bani-pal (Sardanapalos of the Greeks), styled the “great and noble” (Ezra 4:10), was the son and successor (B.C. 668) of Esar-haddon (q.v.).

name: Asshur
description: Second son of Shem (Gen. 10:22; 1 Chr. 1:17). He went from the land of Shinar and built Nineveh, etc. (Gen. 10:11, 12). He probably gave his name to Assyria, which is the usual translation of the word, although the form Asshur is sometimes retained (Num. 24:22, 24; Ezek. 27:23, etc.).

name: Athaliah
description: The daughter of Ahab and Jezebel, and the wife of Jehoram, king of Judah (2 Kings 8:18), who “walked in the ways of the house of Ahab” (2 Chr. 21:6), called “daughter” of Omri (2 Kings 8:26).

name: Augustus
description: The cognomen of the first Roman emperor, C. Julius Caesar Octavianus, during whose reign Christ was born (Luke 2:1). His decree that “all the world should be taxed” was the divinely ordered occasion of Jesus’ being born, according to prophecy (Micah 5:2), in Bethlehem.

name: Azariah
title: Azariah (son of Ethan)
description: Son of Ethan, of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr. 2:8).

name: Azariah
title: Azariah (son of Oded)
description: The son of Oded, a remarkable prophet in the days of Asa (2 Chr. 15:1). He stirred up the king and the people to a great national reformation.

name: Azariah
title: Azariah (2 Chronicles 26:17)
description: High priest in the reign of Uzziah, king of Judah (2 Kings 14:21; 2 Chr. 26:17-20). He was contemporary with the prophets Isaiah, Amos, and Joel.

name: Azariah
title: Azariah (Daniel 1:6)
description: The original name of Abed-nego (Dan. 1:6, 7, 11, 16). He was of the royal family of Judah, and with his other two companions remarkable for his personal beauty and his intelligence as well as piety.

name: Azaziah
title: Azaziah (1 Chronicles 15:21)
description: One of the Levitical harpers in the temple (1 Chr. 15:21).

name: Azaziah
title: Azaziah (father of Hoshea)
description: The father of Hoshea, who was made ruler over the Ephraimites (1 Chr. 27:20).

name: Azaziah
title: Azaziah (2 Chronicles 31:13)
description: One who had charge of the temple offerings (2 Chr. 31:13).

name: Azel
description: Noble, a descendant of king Saul (1 Chr. 8:37; 9:43, 44).

name: Azmaveth
title: Azmaveth (2 Samuel 23:31)
description: One of David’s thirty warriors (2 Sam. 23:31).

name: Azmaveth
title: Azmaveth (son of Adiel)
description: An overseer over the royal treasury in the time of David and Solomon (1 Chr. 27:25).

name: Azubah
title: Azubah (daughter of Shilhi)
description: The daughter of Shilhi, and mother of king Jehoshaphat (1 Kings 22:42).

name: Azubah
title: Azubah (wife of Caleb)
description: The wife of Caleb (1 Chr. 2:18, 19).

name: Azur
title: Azur (father of Hananiah)
description: The father of Hananiah, a false prophet (Jer. 28:1).

name: Azur
title: Azur (father of Jaazaniah)
description: The father of Jaazaniah (Ezek. 11:1).

name: Azzur
description: One of those who sealed the covenant with Jehovah on the return from Babylon (Neh. 10:17).

name: Baal
description: The name appropriated to the principal male god of the Phoenicians. It is found in several places in the plural BAALIM (Judg. 2:11; 10:10; 1 Kings 18:18; Jer. 2:23; Hos. 2:17).

name: Baal
title: Baal (son of Abiel)
description: A Benjamite, son of Jehiel, the progenitor of the Gibeonites (1 Chr. 8:30; 9:36).

name: Baal-hanan
title: Baalhanan (son of Achbor)
description: A king of Edom, son of Achbor (Gen. 36:38, 39; 1 Chr. 1:49, 50).

name: Baal-hanan
title: Baalhanan (1 Chronicles 27:28)
description: An overseer of “the olive trees and sycomore trees in the low plains” (the Shephelah) under David (1 Chr. 27:28).

name: Baal-zebub
description: Fly-lord, the god of the Philistines at Ekron (2 Kings 1:2, 3, 16). This name was given to the god because he was supposed to be able to avert the plague of flies which in that region was to be feared.

name: Baalis
description: King of the Ammonites at the time of the Babylonian captivity (Jer. 40:14). He hired Ishmael to slay Gedaliah who had been appointed governor over the cities of Judah.

name: Baana
title: Baana (son of Ahilud)
description: One of Solomon’s purveyors (1 Kings 4:12).

name: Baana
title: Baana (father of Zadok)
description: Father of Zadok (Neh. 3:4).

name: Baanah
title: Baanah (son of Rimmon)
description: One of the two sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, a captain in Saul’s army. He and his brother Rechab assassinated Ishbosheth (2 Sam. 4:2), and were on this account slain by David, and their mutilated bodies suspended over the pool at Hebron (5, 6, 12).

name: Baanah
title: Baanah (father of Heleb)
description: The father of Heled, who was one of David’s thirty heroes (2 Sam. 23:29; 1 Chr. 11:30).

name: Baanah
title: Baanah (son of Hushai)
description: Son of Hushai, another of Solomon’s purveyors (1 Kings 4:16).

name: Baasha
description: Bravery, the third king of the separate kingdom of Israel, and founder of its second dynasty (1 Kings 15; 16; 2 Chr. 16:1-6).

name: Balaam
description: Lord of the people; foreigner or glutton, as interpreted by others, the son of Beor, was a man of some rank among the Midianites (Num. 31:8; comp. 16).

name: Baladan
description: He has given a son, the father of the Babylonian king (2 Kings 20:12; Isa. 39:1) Merodach-baladan (q.v.).

name: Balak
description: Empty; spoiler, a son of Zippor, and king of the Moabites (Num. 22:2, 4). From fear of the Israelites, who were encamped near the confines of his territory, he applied to Balaam (q.v.) to curse them; but in vain (Josh. 24:9).

name: Bani
title: Bani (2 Samuel 23:36)
description: One of David’s thirty-seven warriors, a Gadite (2 Sam. 23:36).

name: Barabbas
description: I.e., son of Abba or of a father, a notorious robber whom Pilate proposed to condemn to death instead of Jesus, whom he wished to release, in accordance with the Roman custom (John 18:40; Mark 15:7; Luke 23:19).

name: Barachel
description: Whom God has blessed, a Buzite, the father of Elihu, one of Job’s friends (Job 32:2, 6).

name: Barak
description: Lightning, the son of Abinoam (Judg. 4:6). At the summons of Deborah he made war against Jabin. She accompanied him into the battle, and gave the signal for the little army to make the attack; in which the host of Jabin was completely routed.

name: Bariah
description: Fugitive, one of Shemaiah’s five sons. Their father is counted along with them in 1 Chr. 3:22.

name: Barkos
description: Painter, (Ezra 2:53; Neh. 7:55). The father of some of the Nethinim.

name: Barnabas
description: Son of consolation, the surname of Joses, a Levite (Acts 4:36). His name stands first on the list of prophets and teachers of the church at Antioch (13:1).

name: Barsabas
title: Barsabas Justus
description: Surnamed Barsabas (Acts 1:23); also called Justus. He was one of those who “companied with the apostles all the time that the Lord Jesus went out and in among them” (Acts 1:21), and was one of the candidates for the place of Judas.

name: Bartholomew
description: Son of Tolmai, one of the twelve apostles (Matt. 10:3; Acts 1:13); generally supposed to have been the same as Nathanael.

name: Bartimaeus
description: Son of Timaeus, one of the two blind beggars of Jericho (Mark 10:46; Matt. 20:30). His blindness was miraculously cured on the ground of his faith.

name: Baruch
description: The secretary of the prophet Jeremiah (32:12; 36:4). He was of the tribe of Judah (51:59). To him Jeremiah dictated his prophecies regarding the invasion of the Babylonians and the Captivity.

name: Barzillai
title: Barzillai (2 Samuel 17:27)
description: A Gileadite of Rogelim who was distinguished for his loyalty to David. He liberally provided for the king’s followers (2 Sam. 17:27).

name: Barzillai
title: Barzillai (father of Adriel)
description: A Meholathite, the father of Adriel (2 Sam. 21:8).

name: Barzillai
title: Barzillai (Ezra 2:61)
description: A priest who married a daughter of the preceding (Ezra 2:61).

name: Bashemath
description: The daughter of Ishmael, the last of Esau’s three wives (Gen. 36:3, 4, 13), from whose son Reuel four tribes of the Edomites sprung.

name: Bathsheba
description: Daughter of the oath, or of seven, called also Bath-shu’a (1 Chr. 3:5), was the daughter of Eliam (2 Sam. 11:3) or Ammiel (1 Chr. 3:5), and wife of Uriah the Hittite.

name: Bealiah
description: Whose Lord is Jehovah, a Benjamite, one of David’s thirty heroes of the sling and bow (1 Chr. 12:5).

name: Bedan
title: Bedan (1 Samuel 12:11)
description: One of the judges of Israel (1 Sam. 12:11). It is uncertain who he was. Some suppose that Barak is meant, others Samson, but most probably this is a contracted form of Abdon (Judg. 12:13).

name: Beeri
title: Beeri (father of Aholibamah)
description: The father of Judith, one of the wives of Esau (Gen. 26:34), the same as Adah (Gen. 36:2).

name: Bela
title: Bela (son of Beor)
description: The son of Beor, and a king of Edom (Gen. 36:32, 33; 1 Chr. 1:43).

name: Bela
title: Bela (son of Azaz)
description: A son of Azaz (1 Chr. 5:8).

name: Bela
title: Bela (son of Benjamin)
description: The eldest son of Benjamin (Num. 26:38; “Belah,” Gen. 46:21).

name: Belshazzar
description: Bel protect the king!, the last of the kings of Babylon (Dan. 5:1). He was the son of Nabonidus by Nitocris, who was the daughter of Nebuchadnezzar and the widow of Nergal-sharezer.

name: Ben-ammi
description: Son of my kindred; i.e., “born of incest”, the son of Lot by his youngest daughter (Gen. 19:38).

name: Ben-hadad
description: The king of Syria whom Asa, king of Judah, employed to invade Israel (1 Kings 15:18).

name: Ben-hadad
title: Ben-hadad (2 Kings 6:24)
description: Son of the preceding, also king of Syria. He was long engaged in war against Israel. He was murdered probably by Hazael, by whom he was succeeded (2 Kings 8:7-15), after a reign of some thirty years.

name: Ben-hadad
title: Ben-hadad (son of Hazael)
description: King of Damascus, and successor of his father Hazael on the throne of Syria (2 Kings 13:3, 4). His misfortunes in war are noticed by Amos (1:4).

name: Benaiah
description: The son of Jehoiada, chief priest (1 Chr. 27:5). He was set by David over his body-guard of Cherethites and Pelethites (2 Sam. 8:18; 1 Kings 1:32; 1 Chr. 18:17).

name: Benaiah
title: Benaiah (1 Chronicles 15:18)
description: A musical Levite (1 Chr. 15:18, 20).

name: Benaiah
title: Benaiah (son of Jeiel)
description: The son of Jeiel (2 Chr. 20:14).

name: Benjamin
title: Benjamin (patriarch)
description: The younger son of Jacob by Rachel (Gen. 35:18). His birth took place at Ephrath, on the road between Bethel and Bethlehem, at a short distance from the latter place.

name: Beor
title: Beor (father of Bela)
description: The father of Bela, one of the kings of Edom (Gen. 36:32).

name: Beor
title: Beor (father of Balaam)
description: The father of Balaam (Num. 22:5; 24:3, 15; 31:8). In 2 Pet. 2:15 he is called Bosor.

name: Bera
description: Gift, or son of evil, king of Sodom at the time of the invasion of the four kings under Chedorlaomer (Gen. 14:2, 8, 17, 21).

name: Berachah
description: One of the Benjamite warriors, Saul’s brethren, who joined David when at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:3).

name: Berechiah
title: Berechiah (son of Shimea)
description: Son of Shimea, and father of Asaph the musician (1 Chr. 6:39; 15:17).

name: Berechiah
title: Berechiah (son of Zerubbabel)
description: The fourth of the five sons of Zerubbabel, of the royal family of Judah (1 Chr. 3:20).

name: Berechiah
title: Berechiah (son of Meshillemoth)
description: One of the seven Ephraimite chieftains, son of Meshillemoth (2 Chr. 28:12).

name: Bered
description: A son of Shuthelah, and grandson of Ephraim (1 Chr. 7:20).

name: Beriah
title: Beriah (son of Asher)
description: One of Asher’s four sons, and father of Heber (Gen. 46:17).

name: Beriah
title: Beriah (son of Ephraim)
description: A son of Ephraim (1 Chr. 7:20-23), born after the slaughter of his brothers, and so called by his father “because it went evil with his house” at that time.

name: Beriah
title: Beriah (son of Elpaal)
description: A Benjamite who with his brother Shema founded Ajalon and expelled the Gittites (1 Chr. 8:13).

name: Bernice
description: Bearer of victory, the eldest daughter of Agrippa I., the Herod Agrippa of Acts 12:20. After the early death of her first husband she was married to her uncle Herod, king of Chalcis.

name: Bethuel
description: The son of Nahor by Milcah; nephew of Abraham, and father of Rebekah (Gen. 22:22, 23; 24:15, 24, 47). He appears in person only once (24:50).

name: Bezaleel
title: Bezaleel (son of Uri)
description: In the shadow of God; i.e., “under his protection”, the artificer who executed the work of art in connection with the tabernacle in the wilderness (Ex. 31:2; 35:30).

name: Bezer
description: A descendant of Asher (1 Chr. 7:37).

name: Bigtha
description: Garden, or gift of fortune, one of the seven eunuchs or chamberlains who had charge of the harem of Ahasuerus (Esther 1:10).

name: Bigthana
description: One of the eunuchs who “kept the door” in the court of Ahasuerus. With Teresh he conspired against the king’s life. Mordecai detected the conspiracy, and the culprits were hanged (Esther 2:21-23; 6:1-3).

name: Bildad
description: Son of contention, one of Job’s friends. He is called “the Shuhite,” probably as belonging to Shuah, a district in Arabia, in which Shuah, the sixth son of Abraham by Keturah, settled (Gen. 25:2).

name: Bilgah
title: Bilgah (1 Chronicles 24:14)
description: The head of the fifteenth sacerdotal course for the temple service (1 Chr. 24:14).

name: Bilgah
title: Bilgah (Nehemiah 10:8)
description: A priest who returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel (Neh. 12:5, 18).

name: Bilhah
description: Faltering; bashful, Rachel’s handmaid, whom she gave to Jacob (Gen. 29:29). She was the mother of Dan and Naphtali (Gen. 30:3-8).

name: Bilshan
description: Son of the tongue; i.e., “eloquent”, a man of some note who returned from the Captivity with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:2; Neh. 7:7).

name: Birsha
description: Son of wickedness, a king of Gomorrah whom Abraham succoured in the invasion of Chedorlaomer (Gen. 14:2).

name: Blastus
description: Chamberlain to king Herod Agrippa I. (Acts 12:20). Such persons generally had great influence with their masters.

name: Boaz
description: The husband of Ruth, a wealthy Bethlehemite. By the “levirate law” the duty devolved on him of marrying Ruth the Moabitess (Ruth 4:1-13).

name: Buz
title: Buz (son of Nahor)
description: The second son of Nahor and Milcah, and brother of Huz (Gen. 22:21). Elihu was one of his descendants (Job 32:2).

name: Buz
title: Buz (father of Jahdo)
description: One of the chiefs of the tribe of Gad (1 Chr. 5:14).

name: Caiaphas
description: The Jewish high priest (A.D. 27-36) at the beginning of our Lord’s public ministry, in the reign of Tiberius (Luke 3:2), and also at the time of his condemnation and crucifixion (Matt. 26:3, 57; John 11:49; 18:13, 14).

name: Cain
description: The first-born son of Adam and Eve (Gen. 4). He became a tiller of the ground, as his brother Abel followed the pursuits of pastoral life.

name: Cainan
title: Cainan (antediluvian patriarch)
description: The fourth antediluvian patriarch, the eldest son of Enos. He was 70 years old at the birth of his eldest son Mahalaleel, after which he lived 840 years (Gen. 5:9-14), and was 910 years old when he died.

name: Cainan
title: Cainan (son of Arphaxad)
description: The son of Arphaxad (Luke 3:36). He is nowhere named in the Old Testament. He is usually called the “second Cainan.”

name: Calcol
description: (1 Chr. 2:6), sustenance, the same probably as Chalcol (1 Kings 4:31), one of the four sages whom Solomon excelled in wisdom; for “he was wiser than all men.”

name: Caleb
description: The son of Jephunneh (Num. 13:6; 32:12; Josh. 14:6, 14). He was one of those whom Moses sent to search the land in the second year after the Exodus.

name: Caleb
title: Caleb (son of Hezron)
description: One of the three sons of Hezron of the tribe of Judah. He is also called Chelubai (1 Chr. 2:9). His descendants are enumerated (18-20, 42-49).

name: Canaan
description: The fourth son of Ham (Gen. 10:6). His descendants were under a curse in consequence of the transgression of his father (9:22-27).

name: Candace
description: The queen of the Ethiopians whose “eunuch” or chamberlain was converted to Christianity by the instrumentality of Philip the evangelist (Acts 8:27).

name: Carmi
title: Carmi (son of Reuben)
description: The last named of the four sons of Reuben (Gen. 46:9).

name: Carmi
title: Carmi (son of Zabdi)
description: The son of Zimri, and the father of Achan (Josh. 7:1), “the troubler of Israel.”

name: Casluhim
description: Fortified, a people descended from Mizraim (Gen. 10:14; 1 Chr. 1:12). Their original seat was probably somewhere in Lower Egypt, along the sea-coast to the south border of Palestine.

name: Chedorlaomer
description: (= Khudur-Lagamar of the inscriptions), king of Elam. Many centuries before the age of Abraham, Canaan and even the Sinaitic peninsula had been conquered by Babylonian kings, and in the time of Abraham himself Babylonia was ruled by a dynasty which claimed sovereignity over Syria and Palestine.

name: Chemosh
description: The destroyer, subduer, or fish-god, the god of the Moabites (Num. 21:29; Jer. 48:7, 13, 46). The worship of this god, “the abomination of Moab,” was introduced at Jerusalem by Solomon (1 Kings 11:7), but was abolished by Josiah (2 Kings 23:13).

name: Chenaanah
title: Chenaanah (father of Zedekiah)
description: The father of Zedekiah (1 Kings 22:11, 24).

name: Chenaniah
title: Chenaniah (1 Chronicles 15:22)
description: Whom Jehovah hath made. “Chief of the Levites,” probably a Kohathite (1 Chr. 15:22), and therefore not the same as mentioned in 26:29.

name: Chesed
description: Gain, the son of Nahor (Gen. 22:22).

name: Chilion
description: The pining one, the younger son of Elimelech and Naomi, and husband of Orpah, Ruth’s sister (Ruth 1:2; 4:9).

name: Chloe
description: Verdure, a female Christian (1 Cor. 1:11), some of whose household had informed Paul of the divided state of the Corinthian church. Nothing is known of her.

name: Chushan-rishathaim
description: Cush of double wickedness, or governor of two presidencies, the king of Mesopotamia who oppressed Israel in the generation immediately following Joshua (Judg. 3:8).

name: Claudia
description: A female Christian mentioned in 2 Tim. 4:21. It is a conjecture having some probability that she was a British maiden, the daughter of king Cogidunus, who was an ally of Rome, and assumed the name of the emperor, his patron, Tiberius Claudius, and that she was the wife of Pudens.

name: Claudius
title: Claudius (4th Roman Emperor)
description: The fourth Roman emperor. He succeeded Caligula (A.D. 41). Though in general he treated the Jews, especially those in Asia and Egypt, with great indulgence, yet about the middle of his reign (A.D. 49) he banished them all from Rome (Acts 18:2).

name: Claudius
title: Claudius Lysias
description: Claudius Lysias, a Greek who, having obtained by purchase the privilege of Roman citizenship, took the name of Claudius (Acts 21:31-40; 22:28; 23:26).

name: Clement
description: Mild, a Christian of Philippi, Paul’s “fellow-labourer,” whose name he mentions as “in the book of life” (Phil. 4:3).

name: Cleophas
description: (abbreviation of Cleopatros), one of the two disciples with whom Jesus conversed on the way to Emmaus on the day of the resurrection (Luke 24:18).

name: Conaniah
description: Whom Jehovah hath set, a Levite placed over the tithes brought into the temple (2 Chr. 35:9).

name: Cornelius
description: A centurion whose history is narrated in Acts 10. He was a “devout man,” and like the centurion of Capernaum, believed in the God of Israel.

name: Coz
description: A descendant of Judah. 1 Chr. 4:8, “Coz;” R.V., “Hakkoz.”

name: Crescens
description: Increasing, probably one of the seventy disciples of Christ. He was one of Paul’s assistants (2 Tim. 4:10), probably a Christian of Rome.

name: Crispus
description: Curled, the chief of the synagogue at Corinth (Acts 18:8). He was converted and, with his family, baptized by Paul (1 Cor. 1:14).

name: Cush
title: Cush (son of Ham)
description: A son, probably the eldest, of Ham, and the father of Nimrod (Gen. 10:8; 1 Chr. 1:10). From him the land of Cush seems to have derived its name.

name: Cyrenius
description: The Grecized form of Quirinus. His full name was Publius Sulpicius Quirinus. Recent historical investigation has proved that Quirinus was governor of Cilicia, which was annexed to Syria at the time of our Lord’s birth.

name: Cyrus
description: (Heb. Ko’resh), the celebrated “King of Persia” (Elam) who was conqueror of Babylon, and issued the decree of liberation to the Jews (Ezra 1:1, 2).

name: Dagon
description: Little fish; diminutive from dag = a fish, the fish-god; the national god of the Philistines (Judg. 16:23). This idol had the body of a fish with the head and hands of a man.

name: Damaris
description: A heifer, an Athenian woman converted to Christianity under the preaching of Paul (Acts 17:34). Some have supposed that she may have been the wife of Dionysius the Areopagite.

name: Dan
description: The fifth son of Jacob. His mother was Bilhah, Rachel’s maid (Gen. 30:6, “God hath judged me”, Heb. dananni). The blessing pronounced on him by his father was, “Dan shall judge his people” (49:16), probably in allusion to the judgeship of Samson, who was of the tribe of Dan.

name: Daniel
title: Daniel (son of David)
description: David’s second son, “born unto him in Hebron, of Abigail the Carmelitess” (1 Chr. 3:1). He is called also Chileab (2 Sam. 3:3).

name: Daniel
description: Beltis protect the king!, the Chaldee name given to Daniel by Nebuchadnezzar (Dan. 1:7).

name: Darda
description: Pearl of wisdom, one of the four who were noted for their wisdom, but whom Solomon excelled (1 Kings 4:31).

name: Darius
title: Darius (Nehemiah 12:22)
description: Darius the Persian (Neh. 12:22) was probably the Darius II. (Ochus or Nothus) of profane history, the son of Artaxerxes Longimanus, who was the son and successor of Ahasuerus (Xerxes).

name: Dathan
description: Welled; belonging to a fountain, a son of Eliab, a Reubenite, who joined Korah (q.v.) in his conspiracy, and with his accomplices was swallowed up by an earthquake (Num. 16:1; 26:9; Deut. 11:6; Ps. 106:17).

name: Daughter of Pharaoh
title: Daughter of Pharaoh (daughter of Pharaoh, Exodus 2:5)
description: The princess who adopted the infant Moses (q.v.), Ex. 2:10. She is twice mentioned in the New Testament (Acts 7:21: Heb. 11:24).

name: Daughter of Pharaoh
title: Daughter of Pharaoh (daughter of Pharaoh, 1 Kings 3:1)
description: The wife of Solomon (1 Kings 3:1). This is the first reference since the Exodus to any connection of Israel with Egypt.

name: David
description: Beloved, the eighth and youngest son of Jesse, a citizen of Bethlehem. His father seems to have been a man in humble life.

name: Debir
description: The king of Eglon, one of the five Canaanitish kings who were hanged by Joshua (Josh. 10:3, 23) after the victory at Gibeon.

name: Deborah
title: Deborah (wife of Lapidoth)
description: A prophetess, “wife” (woman?) of Lapidoth. Jabin, the king of Hazor, had for twenty years held Israel in degrading subjection.

name: Dedan
title: Dedan (son of Raamah)
description: A son of Raamah (Gen. 10:7). His descendants are mentioned in Isa. 21:13, and Ezek. 27:15. They probably settled among the sons of Cush, on the north-west coast of the Persian Gulf.

name: Dedan
title: Dedan (son of Jokshan)
description: A son of Jokshan, Abraham’s son by Keturah (1 Chr. 1:32). His descendants settled on the Syrian borders about the territory of Edom.

name: Delaiah
title: Delaiah (1 Chronicles 24:18)
description: The head of the twenty-third division of the priestly order (1 Chr. 24:18).

name: Delaiah
title: Delaiah (Ezra 2:60)
description: The head of one of the bands of exiles that returned under Zerubbabel to Jerusalem (Ezra 2:60; Neh. 7:62).

name: Delaiah
title: Delaiah (son of Shemaiah)
description: A son of Shemaiah, and one of the courtiers to whom Jeremiah’s first roll of prophecy was read (Jer. 36:12).

name: Delilah
description: Languishing, a Philistine woman who dwelt in the valley of Sorek (Judg. 16:4-20). She was bribed by the “lords of the Philistines” to obtain from Samson the secret of his strength and the means of overcoming it (Judg. 16:4-18).

name: Demas
description: A companion and fellow-labourer of Paul during his first imprisonment at Rome (Philemon 1:24; Col. 4:14). It appears, however, that the love of the world afterwards mastered him, and he deserted the apostle (2 Tim. 4:10).

name: Demetrius
description: A silversmith at Ephesus, whose chief occupation was to make “silver shrines for Diana” (q.v.), Acts 19:24, i.e., models either of the temple of Diana or of the statue of the goddess.

name: Diana
description: So called by the Romans; called Artemis by the Greeks, the “great” goddess worshipped among heathen nations under various modifications.

name: Diblaim
description: Doubled cakes, the mother of Gomer, who was Hosea’s wife (Hos. 1:3).

name: Dinah
description: Judged; vindicated, daughter of Jacob by Leah, and sister of Simeon and Levi (Gen. 30:21). She was seduced by Shechem, the son of Hamor, the Hivite chief, when Jacob’s camp was in the neighbourhood of Shechem.

name: Dionysius
description: The Areopagite, one of Paul’s converts at Athens (Acts 17:34).

name: Dishan
description: Antelope, the youngest son of Seir the Horite, head of one of the tribes of Idumaea (Gen. 36:21, 28, 30).

name: Dodanim
description: Leaders, a race descended from Javan (Gen. 10:4). They are known in profane history as the Dardani, originally inhabiting Illyricum.

name: Dodo
title: Dodo (father of Puah)
description: A descendant of Issachar (Judg. 10:1).

name: Dodo
title: Dodo (father of Eleazar)
description: An Ahohite, father of Eleazar, who was one of David’s three heroes (2 Sam. 23:9; 1 Chr. 11:12). He was the same with Dodai mentioned in 1 Chr. 27:4.

name: Dodo
title: Dodo (father of Elhanan)
description: A Bethlehemite, and father of Elhanan, who was one of David’s thirty heroes (2 Sam. 23:24).

name: Doeg
description: Fearful, an Edomite, the chief overseer of Saul’s flocks (1 Sam. 21:7). At the command of Saul he slew the high priest Ahimelech (q.v.) at Nob, together with all the priests to the number of eighty-five persons. (Comp. Ps. 52, title.)

name: Dorcas
description: (in Greek called Dorcas), gazelle, a disciple at Joppa. She was distinguished for her alms-deeds and good works. Peter, who was sent for from Lydda on the occasion of her death, prayed over the dead body, and said, “Tabitha, arise.”

name: Drusilla
description: Third and youngest daughter of Herod Agrippa I. (Acts 12:1-4, 20-23). Felix, the Roman procurator of Judea, induced her to leave her husband, Azizus, the king of Emesa, and become his wife.

name: Ebal
title: Ebal (son of Shobal)
description: A descendant of Seir the Horite (Gen. 36:23).

name: Ebal
title: Ebal (son of Joktan)
description: A descendant of Eber (1 Chr. 1:22), called also Obal (Gen. 10:28).

name: Ebed
title: Ebed (father of Gaal)
description: Slave, the father of Gaal, in whom the men of Shechem “put confidence” in their conspiracy against Abimelech (Judg. 9:26, 26, 30, 31).

name: Eber
title: Eber (Heber)
description: The third post-duluvian patriach after Shem (Gen. 10:24; 11:14). He is regarded as the founder of the Hebrew race (10:21; Num. 24:24).

name: Eber
title: Eber (a Benjamite)
description: The oldest of the three sons of Elpaal the Benjamite (1 Chr. 8:12).

name: Eber
title: Eber (Amok Family Head)
description: The head of the priestly family of Amok in the time of Zerubbabel (Neh. 12:20).

name: Ebiasaph
description: Father of gathering; the gatherer, the youngest of the three sons of Korah the Levite, head of a family of Korhites (Ex. 6:24); called Ebisaph (1 Chr. 6:37).

name: Eden
title: Eden (son of Joah)
description: Son of Joah, and one of the Levites who assisted in reforming the public worship of the sanctuary in the time of Hezekiah (2 Chr. 29:12).

name: Eder
description: The second of the three sons of Mushi, of the family of Merari, appointed to the Levitical office (1 Chr. 23:23; 24:30).

name: Eglah
description: A heifer, one of David’s wives, and mother of Ithream (2 Sam. 3:5; 1 Chr. 3:3). According to a Jewish tradition she was Michal.

name: Eglon
description: Chieftain or king of one of the Moabite tribes (Judg. 3:12-14). Having entered into an alliance with Ammon and Amalek, he overran the trans-Jordanic region, and then crossing the Jordan, seized on Jericho, the “city of palm trees,” which had been by this time rebuilt, but not as a fortress.

name: Ehud
title: Ehud (son of Gera)
description: The son of Gera, of the tribe of Benjamin (Judg. 3:15).

name: Ehud
title: Ehud (son of Bilhan)
description: A descendant of Benjamin (1 Chr. 7:10), his great-grandson.

name: Elah
title: Elah (Genesis 36:41)
description: One of the Edomite chiefs or “dukes” of Mount Seir (Gen. 36:41).

name: Elah
title: Elah (son of Baasha)
description: The son and successor of Baasha, king of Israel (1 Kings 16:8-10). He was killed while drunk by Zimri, one of the captains of his chariots, and was the last king of the line of Baasha.

name: Elah
title: Elah (father of Hoshea)
description: The father of Hoshea, the last king of Israel (2 Kings 15:30; 17:1).

name: Elah
title: Elah (son of Caleb)
description: The second of the three sons of Caleb, the son of Jephunneh (1 Chr. 4:15).

name: Elam
title: Elam (son of Shem)
description: Highland, the son of Shem (Gen. 10:22), and the name of the country inhabited by his descendants (14:1, 9; Isa. 11:11; 21:2, etc.) lying to the east of Babylonia, and extending to the shore of the Mediterranean, a distance in a direct line of about 1,000 miles.

name: Elasah
title: Elasah (son of Shaphan)
description: The son of Shaphan, one of the two who were sent by Zedekiah to Nebuchadnezzar, and also took charge of Jeremiah’s letter to the captives in Babylon (Jer. 29:3).

name: Eldad
description: Whom God has loved, one of the seventy elders whom Moses appointed (Num. 11:26, 27) to administer justice among the people.

name: Eleasah
title: Eleasah (son of Helez)
description: One of the descendants of Judah, of the family of Hezron (1 Chr. 2:39, “Eleasah”).

name: Eleasah
title: Eleasah (son of Binea)
description: A descendant of king Saul (1 Chr. 8:37; 9:43).

name: Eleazar
description: The third son of Aaron (Ex. 6:23). His wife, a daughter of Putiel, bore him Phinehas (Ex. 6:25). After the death of Nadab and Abihu (Lev. 10:12; Num. 3:4) he was appointed to the charge of the sanctuary (Num. 3:32).

name: Eleazar
title: Eleazar (son of Abinadab)
description: An inhabitant of Kirjath-jearim who was “sanctified” to take charge of the ark, although not allowed to touch it, while it remained in the house of his father Abinadab (1 Sam. 7:1, 2; comp. Num. 3:31; 4:15).

name: Eleazar
title: Eleazar (son of Dodo)
description: The son of Dodo the Ahohite, of the tribe of Benjamin, one of the three most eminent of David’s thirty-seven heroes (1 Chr. 11:12) who broke through the Philistine host and brought him water from the well of Bethlehem (2 Sam. 23:9, 16).

name: Eleazar
title: Eleazar (son of Mahli)
description: A Levite of the family of Merari (1 Chr. 23:21, 22).

name: Eleazar
title: Eleazar (son of Phinehas)
description: A son of Phinehas associated with the priests in taking charge of the sacred vessels brought back to Jerusalem after the Exile (Ezra 8:33).

name: Elhanan
title: Elhanan (son of Jair)
description: A warrior of the time of David famed for his exploits. In the Authorized Version (2 Sam. 21:19) it is recorded that “Elhanan the son of Jaare-oregim, a Bethlehemite, slew the brother of Goliath.”

name: Elhanan
title: Elhanan (son of Dodo)
description: The son of Dodo, and one of David’s warriors (2 Sam. 23:24).

name: Eli
description: Ascent, the high priest when the ark was at Shiloh (1 Sam. 1:3, 9). He was the first of the line of Ithamar, Aaron’s fourth son (1 Chr. 24:3; comp. 2 Sam. 8:17), who held that office.

name: Eliab
title: Eliab (son of Helon)
description: A son of Helon, and chief of the tribe of Zebulun at the time of the census in the wilderness (Num. 1:9; 2:7).

name: Eliab
title: Eliab (son of Pallu)
description: A Reubenite, son of Pallu (Num. 16:1, 12; 26:8, 9; Deut. 11:6).

name: Eliab
title: Eliab (1 Chronicles 12:9)
description: One of the Gadite heroes who joined David in his stronghold in the wilderness (1 Chr. 12:9).

name: Eliada
title: Eliada (son of David)
description: One of David’s sons born after his establishment in Jerusalem (2 Sam. 5:16).

name: Eliada
title: Eliada (2 Chronicles 17:17)
description: A mighty man of war, a Benjamite (2 Chr. 17:17).

name: Eliadah
description: An Aramite of Zobah, captain of a marauding band that troubled Solomon (1 Kings 11:23).

name: Eliakim
title: Eliakim (son of Hilkiah)
description: The son of Hilkiah, who was sent to receive the message of the invading Assyrians and report it to Isaiah (2 Kings 18:18; 19:2; Isa. 36:3; 37:2).

name: Eliakim
title: Eliakim (son of Abiud)
description: The son of Abiud, of the posterity of Zerubbabel (Matt. 1:13).

name: Eliakim
title: Eliakim (son of Melea)
description: The son of Melea (Luke 3:30), and probably grandson of Nathan.

name: Eliam
title: Eliam (father of Bathsheba)
description: The father of Bathsheba, the wife of Uriah (2 Sam. 11:3). In 1 Chr. 3:5 his name is Ammiel.

name: Eliam
title: Eliam (son of Ahithophel)
description: This name also occurs as that of a Gilonite, the son of Ahithophel, and one of David’s thirty warriors (2 Sam. 23:34). perhaps these two were the same person.

name: Eliashib
title: Eliashib (1 Chronicles 24:12)
description: A priest, head of one of the courses of the priests of the time of David (1 Chr. 24:12).

name: Eliashib
title: Eliashib (son of Joiakim)
description: A high priest in the time of Ezra and Nehemiah (Neh. 12:22, 23). He rebuilt the eastern city wall (3:1), his own mansion being in that quarter, on the ridge Ophel (3:20, 21).

name: Eliathah
description: To whom God will come, one of the foureen sons of the Levite Heman, and musician of the temple in the time of David (1 Chr. 25:4).

name: Elidad
description: Whom God has loved, son of Chislon, and chief of the tribe of Benjamin; one of those who were appointed to divide the Promised Land among the tribes (Num. 34:21).

name: Eliel
title: Eliel (1 Chronicles 5:24)
description: A chief of Manasseh, on the east of Jordan (1 Chr. 5:24).

name: Eliel
title: Eliel (1 Chronicles 12:11)
description: A Gadite who joined David in the hold at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:11).

name: Eliel
title: Eliel (2 Chronicles 31:13)
description: One of the overseers of the offerings in the reign of Hezekiah (2 Chr. 31:13).

name: Eliezer
title: Eliezer (Abraham's Steward)
description: “Of Damascus,” the “steward” (R.V., “possessor”) of Abraham’s house (Gen. 15:2, 3). It was probably he who headed the embassy sent by Abraham to the old home of his family in Padan-aram to seek a wife for his son Isaac.

name: Eliezer
title: Eliezer (son of Moses)
description: One of the two sons of Moses, born during his sojourn in Midian (Ex. 18:4; 1 Chr. 23:15, 17). He remained with his mother and brother Gershom with Jethro when Moses returned to Egypt. (Ex. 18:4).

name: Eliezer
title: Eliezer (son of Becher)
description: The son of Becher, and grandson of Benjamin (1 Chr. 7:8).

name: Eliezer
title: Eliezer (1 Chronicles 15:24)
description: One of the priests who blew the trumpet before the ark when it was brought to Jerusalem (1 Chr. 15:24).

name: Eliezer
title: Eliezer (son of Zichri)
description: Son of Zichri, and chief of the Reubenites under David (1 Chr. 27:16).

name: Eliezer
title: Eliezer (son of Dodavah)
description: A prophet in the time of Jehoshaphat (2 Chr. 20:37). Others of this name are mentioned Luke 3:29; Ezra 8:16; 10:18, 23, 31.

name: Elihu
title: Elihu (son of Nahath)
description: The son of Tohu, and grandfather of Elkanah (1 Sam. 1:1). He is called also Eliel (1 Chr. 6:34) and Eliab (6:27).

name: Elihu
title: Elihu (1 Chronicles 12:20)
description: One of the captains of thousands of Manasseh who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:20).

name: Elihu
title: Elihu (son of Shemaiah)
description: One of the family of Obed-edom, who were appointed porters of the temple under David (1 Chr. 26:7).

name: Elihu
title: Elihu (son of Barachel)
description: “The son of Barachel, a Buzite” (Job 32:2), one of Job’s friends. When the debate between Job and his friends is brought to a close, Elihu for the first time makes his appearance, and delivers his opinion on the points at issue (Job 32-37).

name: Elijah
description: “The Tishbite,” the “Elias” of the New Testament, is suddenly introduced to our notice in 1 Kings 17:1 as delivering a message from the Lord to Ahab.

name: Elika
description: God is his rejector, one of David’s thirty-seven distinguished heros (2 Sam. 23:25).

name: Elimelech
description: God his king, a man of the tribe of Judah, of the family of the Hezronites, and kinsman of Boaz, who dwelt in Bethlehem in the days of the judges.

name: Eliphalet
description: God his deliverance, one of David’s sons (2 Sam. 5:16); called also Eliphelet (1 Chr. 3:8).

name: Eliphaz
title: Eliphaz (son of Esau)
description: The son of Esau by his wife Adah, and father of several Edomitish tribes (Gen. 36:4, 10, 11, 16).

name: Elipheleh
description: God will distinguish him, one of the porters appointed to play “on the Sheminith” on the occasion of the bringing up of the ark to the city of David (1 Chr. 15:18, 21).

name: Eliphelet
title: Eliphelet (son of Ahasbai)
description: One of David’s distinguished warriors (2 Sam. 23:34); called also Eliphal in 1 Chr. 11:35.

name: Eliphelet
title: Eliphelet (son of Eleasah)
description: A descendant of king Saul through Jonathan (1 Chr. 8:39).

name: Elisabeth
description: God her oath, the mother of John the Baptist (Luke 1:5). She was a descendant of Aaron. She and her husband Zacharias (q.v.) “were both righteous before God” (Luke 1:5, 13).

name: Elisha
description: God his salvation, the son of Shaphat of Abel-meholah, who became the attendant and disciple of Elijah (1 Kings 19:16-19).

name: Elishah
description: The oldest of the four sons of Javan (Gen. 10:4), whose descendants peopled Greece. It has been supposed that Elishah’s descendants peopled the Peloponnesus, which was known by the name of Elis.

name: Elishama
title: Elishama (son of Ammihud)
description: A prince of Benjamin, grandfather of Joshua (Num. 1:10; 1 Chr. 7:26).

name: Elishama
title: Elishama (son of David)
description: One of David’s sons (2 Sam. 5:16).

name: Elishama
title: Elishama (2 Chronicles 17:8)
description: A priest sent by Jehoshaphat to teach the people the law (2 Chr. 17:8).

name: Elishaphat
description: Whom God has judged, one of the “captains of hundreds” associated with Jehoiada in the league to overthrow the usurpation of Athaliah (2 Chr. 23:1).

name: Elisheba
description: God is her oath, the daughter of Amminadab and the wife of Aaron (Ex. 6:23).

name: Elishua
description: God his salvation, a son of David, 2 Sam. 5:15 = Elishama, 1 Chr. 3:6.

name: Elkanah
title: Elkanah (son of Korah)
description: The second son of Korah (Ex. 6:24), or, according to 1 Chr. 6:22, 23, more correctly his grandson.

name: Elkanah
description: Another Levite of the line of Heman the singer, although he does not seem to have performed any of the usual Levitical offices.

name: Elon
title: Elon (father of Adah)
description: A Hittite, father of Bashemath, Esau’s wife (Gen. 26:34).

name: Elon
title: Elon (son of Zebulun)
description: One of the sons of Zebulun (Gen. 46:14).

name: Elon
title: Elon (Judges 12:11)
description: The eleventh of the Hebrew judges. He held office for ten years (Judg. 12:11, 12). He is called the Zebulonite.

name: Elymas
description: Magician or sorcerer, the Arabic name of the Jew Bar-jesus, who withstood Paul and Barnabas in Cyprus. He was miraculously struck with blindness (Acts 13:11).

name: Enoch
title: Enoch (son of Cain)
description: The eldest son of Cain (Gen. 4:17), who built a city east of Eden in the land of Nod, and called it “after the name of his son Enoch.” This is the first “city” mentioned in Scripture.

name: Enoch
title: Enoch (father of Methuselah)
description: The son of Jared, and father of Methuselah (Gen. 5:21; Luke 3:37). His father was one hundred and sixty-two years old when he was born.

name: Enos
description: Man the son of Seth, and grandson of Adam (Gen. 5:6-11; Luke 3:38). He lived nine hundred and five years.

name: Epaenetus
description: Commendable, a Christian at Rome to whom Paul sent his salutation (Rom. 16:5). He is spoken of as “the first fruits of Achaia” (R.V., “of Asia”, i.e., of proconsular Asia, which is probably the correct reading).

name: Epaphras
