description: Lovely, spoken of by Paul (Col. 1:7; 4:12) as “his dear fellow-servant,” and “a faithful minister of Christ.” He was thus evidently with him at Rome when he wrote to the Colossians.

name: Ephah
title: Ephah (mother of Moza)
description: A concubine of Caleb.

name: Ephah
title: Ephah (daughter of Jahdai)
description: A descendant of Judah. Ephah, a word of Egyptian origin, meaning measure; a grain measure containing “three seahs or ten omers,” and equivalent to the bath for liquids (Ex. 16:36; 1 Sam. 17:17; Zech. 5:6).

name: Epher
title: Epher (son of Midian)
description: One of the sons of Midian, who was Abraham’s son by Keturah (Gen. 25:4).

name: Epher
title: Epher (1 Chronicles 5:24)
description: The head of one of the families of trans-Jordanic Manasseh who were carried captive by Tiglath-pileser (1 Chr. 5:24).

name: Ephraim
description: Double fruitfulness (“for God had made him fruitful in the land of his affliction”). The second son of Joseph, born in Egypt (Gen. 41:52; 46:20).

name: Ephratah
description: The second wife of Caleb, the son of Hezron, mother of Hur, and grandmother of Caleb, who was one of those that were sent to spy the land (1 Chr. 2:19, 50).

name: Ephron
description: The son of Zohar a Hittite, the owner of the field and cave of Machpelah (q.v.), which Abraham bought for 400 shekels of silver (Gen. 23:8-17; 25:9; 49:29, 30).

name: Erastus
description: A companion of Paul at Ephesus, who was sent by him along with Timothy into Macedonia (Acts 19:22). Corinth was his usual place of abode (2 Tim. 4:20); but probably he may have been the same as the preceding.

name: Esau
title: Esau (Edom)
description: Hairy, Rebekah’s first-born twin son (Gen. 25:25). The name of Edom, “red”, was also given to him from his conduct in connection with the red lentil “pottage” for which he sold his birthright (30, 31).

name: Eshcol
description: A young Amoritish chief who joined Abraham in the recovery of Lot from the hands of Chedorlaomer (Gen. 14:13, 24).

name: Esther
description: The queen of Ahasuerus, and heroine of the book that bears her name. She was a Jewess named Hadas’sah (the myrtle), but when she entered the royal harem she received the name by which she henceforth became known (Esther 2:7).

name: Ethan
title: Ethan (son of Mahol)
description: “The Ezrahite,” distinguished for his wisdom (1 Kings 4:31). He is named as the author of the 89th Psalm. He was of the tribe of Levi.

name: Ethan
title: Ethan (son of Zimmah)
description: A Levite of the family of Gershom (1 Chr. 6:21), probably the same as Ethan (42).

name: Ethbaal
description: With Baal, a king of Sidon (B.C. 940-908), father of Jezebel, who was the wife of Ahab (1 Kings 16:31). He is said to have been also a priest of Astarte, whose worship was closely allied to that of Baal, and this may account for his daughter’s zeal in promoting idolatry in Israel.

name: Euodias
description: A good journey, a female member of the church at Philippi. She was one who laboured much with Paul in the gospel. He exhorts her to be of one mind with Syntyche (Phil. 4:2).

name: Eutychus
description: Fortunate, (Acts 20:9-12), a young man of Troas who fell through drowsiness from the open window of the third floor of the house where Paul was preaching, and was “taken up dead.”

name: Eve
description: Life; living, the name given by Adam to his wife (Gen. 3:20; 4:1). The account of her creation is given in Gen. 2:21, 22.

name: Evil-merodach
description: Merodach’s man, the son and successor of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon (2 Kings 25:27; Jer. 52:31, 34). He seems to have reigned but two years (B.C. 562-560).

name: Ezekiel
description: One of the great prophets, the son of Buzi the priest (Ezek. 1:3). He was one of the Jewish exiles who settled at Tel-Abib, on the banks of the Chebar, “in the land of the Chaldeans.”

name: Ezer
title: Ezer (son of Seir)
description: One of the sons of Seir, the native princes, “dukes,” of Mount Hor (Gen. 36:21, 27).

name: Ezra
description: The “scribe” who led the second body of exiles that returned from Babylon to Jerusalem B.C. 459, and author of the book of Scripture which bears his name.

name: Ezra
title: Ezra (Nehemiah 12:1)
description: A priest among those that returned to Jerusalem under Zerubabel (Neh. 12:1).

name: Ezri
description: Help of Jehovah, the son of Chelub. He superintended, under David, those who “did the work of the field for tillage” (1 Chr. 27:26).

name: Felix
description: Happy, the Roman procurator of Judea before whom Paul “reasoned” (Acts 24:25). He appears to have expected a bribe from Paul, and therefore had several interviews with him.

name: Fortunatus
description: Fortunate, a disciple of Corinth who visited Paul at Ephesus, and returned with Stephanas and Achaicus, the bearers of the apostle’s first letter to the Corinthians (1 Cor. 16:17).

name: Gaal
description: Loathing, the son of Ebed, in whom the Shechemites “placed their confidence” when they became discontented with Abimelech.

name: Gabriel
description: Champion of God, used as a proper name to designate the angel who was sent to Daniel (8:16) to explain the vision of the ram and the he-goat, and to communicate the prediction of the seventy weeks (Dan. 9:21-27).

name: Gad
description: Jacob’s seventh son, by Zilpah, Leah’s handmaid, and the brother of Asher (Gen. 30:11-13; 46:16, 18). In the Authorized Version of 30:11 the words, “A troop cometh: and she called,” etc., should rather be rendered, “In fortune [R.V., ‘Fortunate’]: and she called,” etc., or “Fortune cometh,” etc.

name: Gad
title: Gad (1 Samuel 22:5)
description: A prophet who joined David in the “hold,” and at whose advice he quitted it for the forest of Hareth (1 Chr. 29:29; 2 Chr. 29:25; 1 Sam. 22:5).

name: Gaddi
description: Fortunate, the representative of the tribe of Manasseh among the twelve “spies” sent by Moses to spy the land (Num. 13:11).

name: Gaddiel
description: Fortune (i.e., sent) of God, the representative of the tribe of Zebulum among the twelve spies (Num. 13:10).

name: Gahar
description: Lurking-place, one of the chief of the Nethinim, whose descendants returned to Jerusalem under Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:47).

name: Gaius
title: Gaius (of Macedonia)
description: A Macedonian, Paul’s fellow-traveller, and his host at Corinth when he wrote his Epistle to the Romans (16:23). He with his household were baptized by Paul (1 Cor. 1:14).

name: Gaius
title: Gaius (of Derbe)
description: A man of Derbe who accompanied Paul into Asia on his last journey to Jerusalem

name: Gaius
title: Gaius (Romans 16:23)
description: A Macedonian, Paul’s fellow-traveller, and his host at Corinth when he wrote his Epistle to the Romans (16:23). He with his household were baptized by Paul (1 Cor. 1:14).

name: Gaius
title: Gaius (3 John 1:1)
description: A Christain of Asia Minor to whom John addressed his third epistle (3 John 1:1).

name: Gallio
description: The elder brother of Seneca the philosopher, who was tutor and for some time minister of the emperor Nero. He was “deputy”, i.e., proconsul, as in Revised Version, of Achaia, under the emperor Claudius, when Paul visited Corinth (Acts 18:12).

name: Gamaliel
title: Gamaliel (son of Pedahzur)
description: A chief of the tribe of Manasseh at the census at Sinai (Num. 1:10; 2:20; 7:54, 59).

name: Gamaliel
title: Gamaliel (Acts 5:34)
description: The son of rabbi Simeon, and grandson of the famous rabbi Hillel. He was a Pharisse, and therefore the opponent of the party of the Sadducees.

name: Gamul
description: Weaned the leader of one of the priestly courses (1 Chr. 24:17).

name: Gareb
description: One of David’s warriors (2 Sam. 23:38), an Ithrite.

name: Geber
title: Geber (son of Uri)
description: A valiant man, (1 Kings 4:19), one of Solomon’s purveyors, having jurisdiction over a part of Gilead, comprising all the kingdom of Sihon and part of the kingdom of Og (Deut. 2; 31).

name: Gedaliah
description: The son of Ahikam, and grandson of Shaphan, secretary of king Josiah (Jer. 26:24). After the destruction of Jerusalem (see ZEDEKIAH), Nebuchadnezzar left him to govern the country as tributary to him (2 Kings 25:22; Jer. 40:5; 52:16).

name: Gedaliah
title: Gedaliah (son of Jeduthun)
description: The son of Jeduthum (1 Chr. 25:3, 9).

name: Gedaliah
title: Gedaliah (son of Pashur)
description: One of the Jewish nobles who conspired against Jeremiah (Jer. 38:1).

name: Gehazi
description: Valley of vision, Elisha’s trusted servant (2 Kings 4:31; 5:25; 8:4, 5). He appears in connection with the history of the Shunammite (2 Kings 4:14, 31) and of Naaman the Syrian.

name: Gemariah
title: Gemariah (son of Hilkiah)
description: The son of Hilkiah, who accompanied Shaphan with the tribute-money from Zedekiah to Nebuchadnezzar, and was the bearer at the same time of a letter from Jeremiah to the Jewish captives at Babylon (Jer. 29:3, 4).

name: Gemariah
title: Gemariah (son of Shaphan)
description: The son of Shaphan, and one of the Levites of the temple in the time of Jehoiakim (Jer. 36:10; 2 Kings 22:12). Baruch read aloud to the people from Gemariah’s chamber, and again in the hearing of Gemariah and other scribes, the prophecies of Jeremiah (Jer. 36:11-20), which filled him with terror.

name: Genubath
description: Theft, the son of Hadad, of the Edomitish royal family. He was brought up in Pharaoh’s household. His mother was a sister of Tahpenes, the king of Egypt’s wife, mentioned in 1 Kings 11:20.

name: Gera
title: Gera (son of Benjamin)
description: The father of Ehud the judge (Judg. 3:15).

name: Gera
title: Gera (father of Shimei)
description: The father of Shimei, who so grossly abused David (2 Sam. 16:5; 19:16, 18).

name: Gershom
title: Gershom (son of Moses)
description: The elder of the two sons of Moses born to him in Midian (Ex. 2:22; 18:3).

name: Gershom
title: Gershom (son of Manasseh)
description: The son of Manasseh (Judg. 18:30), in R.V. “of Moses.”

name: Gershom
title: Gershom (Ezra 8:2)
description: A descendant of Phinehas who returned with Ezra from Babylon (Ezra 8:2).

name: Gershon
description: Ger’shom expulsion, the eldest of Levi’s three sons (Gen. 46:11; Ex. 6:16). In the wilderness the sons of Gershon had charge of the fabrics of the tabernacle when it was moved from place to place, the curtains, veils, tent-hangings (Num. 3: 21-26).

name: Geshem
description: Or Gashmu, firmness, probably chief of the Arabs south of Palestine, one of the enemies of the Jews after the return from Babylon (Neh. 2:19; 6:1, 2). He united with Sanballat and Tobiah in opposing the rebuilding of the wall of Jerusalem.

name: Gideon
description: Called also Jerubbaal (Judg. 6:29, 32), was the first of the judges whose history is circumstantially narrated (Judg. 6-8).

name: Girgasite
description: Dwelling in clayey soil, the descendants of the fifth son of Canaan (Gen. 10:16), one of the original tribes inhabiting the land of Canaan before the time of the Israelites (Gen. 15:21; Deut. 7:1).

name: God
description: (A.S. and Dutch God; Dan. Gud; Ger. Gott), the name of the Divine Being. It is the rendering (1) of the Hebrew ’El, from a word meaning to be strong; (2) of ’Eloah, plural ’Elohim.

name: Gog
title: Gog (son of Shemaiah)
description: A Reubenite (1 Chr. 5:4), the father of Shimei.

name: Goliath
description: A famous giant of Gath, who for forty days openly defied the armies of Israel, but was at length slain by David with a stone from a sling (1 Sam. 17:4).

name: Gomer
title: Gomer (son of Japheth)
description: The eldest son of Japheth, and father of Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah (Gen. 10:2, 3), whose descendants formed the principal branch of the population of South-eastern Europe.

name: Hadad
title: Hadad (son of Bedad)
description: An Edomite king who defeated the Midianites (Gen. 36:35; 1 Chr. 1:46).

name: Hadad
title: Hadad (father of Genubath)
description: One of “the king’s seed in Edom.” He fled into Egypt, where he married the sister of Pharaoh’s wife (1 Kings 11:14-22). He became one of Solomon’s adversaries.

name: Hadad
title: Hadad (husband of Mehetabel)
description: One of the Edomitish kings (Gen. 36:39) about the time of Saul. Called also Hadad (1 Chr. 1:50, 51). It is probable that in these cases Hadar may be an error simply of transcription for Hadad.

name: Hadar
description: A son of Ishmael (Gen. 25:15); in 1 Chr. 1:30 written Hadad.

name: Hadarezer
description: Hadad is help; called also Hadarezer, Adod is his help, the king of Zobah. Hanun, the king of the Ammonites, hired among others the army of Hadadezer to assist him in his war against David.

name: Hadlai
description: Resting, an Ephraimite; the father of Amasa, mentioned in 2 Chr. 28:12.

name: Hadoram
description: The fifth son of Joktan, the founder of an Arab tribe (Gen. 10:27; 1 Chr. 1:21).

name: Hagar
description: Flight, or, according to others, stranger, an Egyptian, Sarah’s handmaid (Gen. 16:1; 21:9, 10), whom she gave to Abraham (q.v.) as a secondary wife (16:2).

name: Haggai
description: Festive, one of the twelve so-called minor prophets. He was the first of the three (Zechariah, his contemporary, and Malachi, who was about one hundred years later, being the other two) whose ministry belonged to the period of Jewish history which began after the return from captivity in Babylon.

name: Haggith
description: Festive; the dancer, a wife of David and the mother of Adonijah (2 Sam. 3:4; 1 Kings 1:5, 11; 2:13; 1 Chr. 3:2), who, like Absalom, was famed for his beauty.

name: Hakkoz
description: The thorn, the head of one of the courses of the priests (1 Chr. 24:10).

name: Ham
description: Warm, hot, and hence the south; also an Egyptian word meaning “black”, the youngest son of Noah (Gen. 5:32; comp. 9:22, 24).

name: Haman
description: (of Persian origin), magnificent, the name of the vizier (i.e., the prime minister) of the Persian king Ahasuerus (Esther 3:1, etc.).

name: Hammedatha
description: Father of Haman, designated usually “the Agagite” (Esther 3:1, 10; 8:5).

name: Hammelech
description: The king’s, the father of Jerahmeel, mentioned in Jer. 36:26. Some take this word as a common noun, “the king”, and understand that Jerahmeel was Jehoiakim’s son.

name: Hammoleketh
description: The queen, the daughter of Machir and sister of Gilead (1 Chr. 7:17, 18). Abiezer was one of her three children.

name: Hamor
description: He-ass, a Hivite from whom Jacob purchased the plot of ground in which Joseph was afterwards buried (Gen. 33:19). He is called “Emmor” in Acts 7:16.

name: Hamul
description: Spared, one of the sons of Pharez, son of Judah (1 Chr. 2:5). His descendants are called Hamulites (Num. 26:21).

name: Hamutal
description: Kinsman of the dew, the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah, wife of king Josiah, and mother of king Jehoahaz (2 Kings 23:31), also of king Zedekiah (2 Kings 24:18).

name: Hanameel
description: Whom God has graciously given, the cousin of Jeremiah, to whom he sold the field he possessed in Anathoth, before the siege of Jerusalem (Jer. 32:6-12).

name: Hanan
title: Hanan (son of Azel)
description: A descendant of Saul (1 Chr. 8:38).

name: Hanan
title: Hanan (son of Maachah)
description: One of David’s heroes (1 Chr. 11:43).

name: Hanan
title: Hanan (Ezra 2:46)
description: One of the Nethinim (Ezra 2:46).

name: Hanan
title: Hanan (Nehemiah 8:7)
description: One of the Levites who assisted Ezra (Neh. 8:7).

name: Hanan
title: Hanan (Nehemiah 10:22)
description: One of the chiefs who subscribed the covenant (Neh. 10:22).

name: Hanani
title: Hanani (father of Jehu)
description: A prophet who was sent to rebuke king Asa for entering into a league with Benhadad I., king of Syria, against Judah (2 Chr. 16:1-10). He was probably the father of the prophet Jehu (1 Kings 16:7).

name: Hanani
title: Hanani (son of Heman)
description: One of the sons of Heman (1 Chr. 25:4, 25).

name: Hanani
title: Hanani (son of Hachaliah)
description: Probably a brother of Nehemiah (Neh. 1:2; 7:2), who reported to him the melancholy condition of Jerusalem. Nehemiah afterwards appointed him to have charge of the city gates.

name: Hananiah
title: Hananiah (son of Zerubbabel)
description: Son of Zerubbabel (1 Chr. 3:19, 21).

name: Hananiah
title: Hananiah (son of Shashak)
description: A chief of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chr. 8:24).

name: Hananiah
title: Hananiah (son of Heman)
description: One of the sons of Heman (1 Chr. 25:4, 23).

name: Hananiah
title: Hananiah (2 Chronicles 26:11)
description: One of Uzziah’s military officers (2 Chr. 26:11).

name: Hananiah
title: Hananiah (Nehemiah 7:2)
description: The “ruler of the palace; he was a faithful man, and feared God above many” (Neh. 7:2).

name: Hananiah
title: Hananiah (Nehemiah 12:12)
description: A priest, son of Jeremiah (Neh. 12:12).

name: Hananiah
title: Hananiah (father of Shelemiah)
description: Grandfather of the captain who arrested Jeremiah (Jer. 37:13).

name: Haniel
description: A chief of the tribe of Asher (1 Chr. 7:39).

name: Hannah
description: Favour, grace, one of the wives of Elkanah the Levite, and the mother of Samuel (1 Sam. 1; 2).

name: Hanniel
description: A chief of the tribe of Manasseh (Num. 34:23).

name: Hanun
title: Hanun (son of Nahash)
description: The son and successor of Nahash, king of Moab. David’s messengers, sent on an embassy of condolence to him to Rabbah Ammon, his capital, were so grossly insulted that he proclaimed war against Hanun.

name: Haran
title: Haran (brother of Abraham)
description: Heb. haran; i.e., “mountaineer.” The eldest son of Terah, brother of Abraham and Nahor, and father of Lot, Milcah, and Iscah.

name: Haran
title: Haran (son of Caleb)
description: The son of Caleb of Judah (1 Chr. 2:46) by his concubine Ephah.

name: Harbona
description: (a Persian word meaning “ass-driver”), one of the seven eunuchs or chamberlains of king Ahasuerus (Esther 1:10; 7:9).

name: Harhaiah
description: Zeal of Jehovah, (Neh. 3:8) “of the goldsmiths,” one whose son helped to repair the wall of Jerusalem.

name: Harhur
description: Fever, one of the Nethinim (Ezra 2:51).

name: Harim
title: Harim (1 Chronicles 24:8)
description: The head of the second course of priests (1 Chr. 24:8).

name: Harnepher
description: A chief of the tribe of Asher (1 Chr. 7:36).

name: Harsha
description: Worker or enchanter, one of the Nethinim (Ezra 2:52; Neh. 7:54).

name: Harum
description: Elevated, (1 Chr. 4:8), a descendant of Judah.

name: Haruz
description: Eager, the father of Meshullemeth, the wife of king Manasseh (2 Kings 21:19) and mother of king Amon.

name: Hasadiah
description: Favoured by Jehovah, one of the sons of Pedaiah (1 Chr. 3:20), of the royal line of David.

name: Hasenuah
description: Bristling or hated, a Benjamite (1 Chr. 9:7).

name: Hashabiah
title: Hashabiah (2 Chronicles 35:9)
description: One of the chief Levites (2 Chr. 35:9).

name: Hashabiah
title: Hashabiah (Ezra 8:19)
description: One of the chief priests in the time of Ezra (Ezra 8:24).

name: Hashabniah
title: Hashabniah (Nehemiah 9:5)
description: One of the Levites whom Ezra appointed to interpret the law to the people (Neh. 9:5).

name: Hashbadana
description: Consideration in judging, stood at Ezra’s left hand when he read the law (Neh. 8:4).

name: Hashubah
description: Ibid., a descendant of David (1 Chr. 3:20).

name: Hashum
title: Hashum (Nehemiah 8:4)
description: Stood on Ezra’s left hand while he read the law (Neh. 8:4).

name: Hasrah
description: Poverty, “keeper of the wardrobe,” i.e., of the sacerdotal vestments (2 Chr. 34:22); called Harhas 2 Kings 22:14. He was husband of the prophetess Huldah.

name: Hasshub
description: A Levite of the family of Merari (Neh. 11:15; 1 Chr. 9:14).

name: Hasupha
description: Uncovered, one of the Nethinim (Ezra 2:43; Neh. 7:46).

name: Hatach
description: Verity, one of the eunuchs or chamberlains in the palace of Ahasuerus (Esther 4:5, 6, 9, 10).

name: Hathath
description: Terror, son of Othniel (1 Chr. 4:13).

name: Hatipha
description: Captured, one of the Nethinim (Ezra 2:54).

name: Hatita
description: Exploration, one of the temple porters or janitors (Ezra 2:42). He returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel.

name: Hattush
title: Hattush (Nehemiah 10:4)
description: A priest who returned with Zerubbabel (Neh. 12:2).

name: Havilah
title: Havilah (son of Cush)
description: One of the sons of Cush (Gen. 10:7).

name: Havilah
title: Havilah (son of Joktan)
description: A son of Joktan (Gen. 10:29; 1 Chr. 1:23).

name: Hazael
description: Whom God beholds, an officer of Ben-hadad II., king of Syria, who ultimately came to the throne, according to the word of the Lord to Elijah (1 Kings 19:15), after he had put the king to death (2 Kings 8:15).

name: Hazarmaveth
description: Court of death, the third son of Joktan, and a region in Arabia-Felix settled by him (Gen. 10:26; 1 Chr. 1:20). It is probably the modern province of Hadramaut, situated on the Indian Ocean east of the modern Yemen.

name: Hazo
description: Vision, one of the sons of Nahor (Gen. 22:22).

name: Heber
title: Heber (son of Beriah)
description: Son of Beriah and grandson of Asher (Gen. 46:17; 1 Chr. 7:31, 32).

name: Heber
title: Heber (husband of Jael)
description: The Kenite (Judg. 4:11, 17; 5:24), a descendant of Hobab. His wife Jael received Sisera (q.v.) into her tent and then killed him.

name: Heber
title: Heber (son of Abihail)
description: One of the seven heads of the families of the Gadites (1 Chr. 5:13).

name: Hebron
title: Hebron (son of Kohath)
description: The third son of Kohath the Levite (Ex. 6:18; 1 Chr. 6:2, 18).

name: Hegai
description: Eunuch, had charge of the harem of Ahasuerus (Esther 2:8).

name: Helah
description: Rust, (1 Chr. 4:5, 7), one of the wives of Ashur.

name: Heleb
description: Fatness, one of David’s warriors (2 Sam. 23:29).

name: Helek
description: A portion, (Josh. 17:2), descended from Manasseh.

name: Helem
description: One who returned from Babylon.

name: Helez
title: Helez (2 Samuel 23:26)
description: One of David’s warriors (2 Sam. 23:26).

name: Helez
title: Helez (son of Azariah)
description: One of Judah’s posterity (1 Chr. 2:39).

name: Heli
description: Elevation, father of Joseph in the line of our Lord’s ancestry (Luke 3:23).

name: Helkai
description: Smooth-tongued, one of the chief priests in the time of Joiakim (Neh. 12:15).

name: Helon
description: Strong, father of Eliab, who was “captain of the children of Zebulun” (Num. 1:9; 2:7).

name: Heman
title: Heman (son of Mahol)
description: A son of Zerah, noted for his wisdom.

name: Heman
title: Heman (son of Zerah)
description: A son of Zerah, noted for his wisdom.

name: Heman
description: Grandson of Samuel (1 Chr. 6:33; 15:17), to whom the 88th Psalm probably was inscribed. He was one of the “seers” named in 2 Chr. 29:14, 30, and took a leading part in the administration of the sacred services.

name: Henadad
title: Henadad (Ezra 3:9)
description: Favour of Hadad, the name of a Levite after the Captivity (Ezra 3:9).

name: Hepher
title: Hepher (son of Gilead)
description: The youngest son of Gilead (Num. 26:32; 27:1).

name: Hepher
title: Hepher (son of Ashur)
description: The second son of Asher (1 Chr. 4:6).

name: Hepher
title: Hepher (1 Chronicles 11:36)
description: One of David’s heroes (1 Chr. 11:36).

name: Hermes
description: Mercury, a Roman Christian (Rom. 16:14).

name: Hermogenes
description: Mercury-born, at one time Paul’s fellow-labourer in Asia Minor, who, however, afterwards abandoned him, along with one Phygellus, probably on account of the perils by which they were beset (2 Tim. 1:15).

name: Herod Antipas
description: Herod’s son by Malthace (Matt. 14:1; Luke 3:1, 19; 9:7; Acts 13:1).

name: Herod Agrippa I
description: Son of Aristobulus and Bernice, and grandson of Herod the Great. He was made tetrarch of the provinces formerly held by Lysanias II., and ultimately possessed the entire kingdom of his grandfather, Herod the Great, with the title of king.

name: Herodias
description: (Matt. 14:3-11; Mark 6:17-28; Luke 3:19), the daughter of Aristobulus and Bernice. While residing at Rome with her husband Herod Philip I. and her daughter, Herod Antipas fell in with her during one of his journeys to that city.

name: Herodion
description: A Christian at Rome whom Paul salutes and calls his “kinsman” (Rom. 16:11).

name: Heth
description: Dread, a descendant of Canaan, and the ancestor of the Hittites (Gen. 10:18; Deut. 7:1), who dwelt in the vicinity of Hebron (Gen. 23:3, 7).

name: Hezekiah
description: Son of Ahaz (2 Kings 18:1; 2 Chr. 29:1), whom he succeeded on the throne of the kingdom of Judah. He reigned twenty-nine years (B.C. 726-697).

name: Hezion
description: Vision, the father of Tabrimon, and grandfather of Ben-hadad, king of Syria (1 Kings 15:18).

name: Hezir
title: Hezir (1 Chronicles 24:15)
description: The head of the seventeenth course of the priests (1 Chr. 24:15).

name: Hezir
title: Hezir (Nehemiah 10:20)
description: One who sealed Nehemiah’s covenant.

name: Hezrai
description: A Carmelite, one of David’s warriors (1 Chr. 11:37).

name: Hezron
title: Hezron (son of Reuben)
description: One of the sons of Reuben (Gen. 46:9; Ex. 6:14).

name: Hezron
title: Hezron (son of Pharez)
description: The older of the two sons of Pharez (Gen. 46:12).

name: Hiel
description: Life of (i.e., from) God, a native of Bethel, who built (i.e., fortified) Jericho some seven hundred years after its destruction by the Israelites.

name: Hilkiah
title: Hilkiah (father of Eliakim)
description: The father of Eliakim (2 Kings 18:18, 26, 37).

name: Hilkiah
description: The high priest in the reign of Josiah (1 Chr. 6:13; Ezra 7:1). To him and his deputy (2 Kings 23:5), along with the ordinary priests and the Levites who had charge of the gates, was entrusted the purification of the temple in Jerusalem.

name: Hillel
description: Praising, a Pirathonite, father of the judge Abdon (Judg. 12:13, 15).

name: Hiram
description: Also “Huram” and “Horam,” king of Tyre. He entered into an alliance with David, and assisted him in building his palace by sending him able workmen, and also cedar-trees and fir-trees from Lebanon (2 Sam. 5:11; 1 Chr. 14:1).

name: Hiram
title: Hiram (1 Kings 7:13)
description: The “master workman” whom Hiram sent to Solomon. He was the son of a widow of Dan, and of a Tyrian father.

name: Hivite
description: One of the original tribes scattered over Palestine, from Hermon to Gibeon in the south. The name is interpreted as “midlanders” or “villagers” (Gen. 10:17; 1 Chr. 1:15).

name: Hizkijah
description: (Neh. 10:17), one who sealed the covenant.

name: Hobab
description: Beloved, the Kenite, has been usually identified with Jethro (q.v.), Ex. 18:5, 27; comp. Num. 10:29, 30.

name: Hodijah
title: Hodijah (Nehemiah 8:7)
description: One of the Levites who assisted Ezra in expounding the law (Neh. 8:7; 9:5).

name: Hodijah
title: Hodijah (Nehemiah 10:18)
description: A Levite who sealed the covenant.

name: Hoglah
description: Partridge, one of the daughters of Zelophehad the Gileadite, to whom portions were assigned by Moses (Num. 26:33; 27:1; 36:11).

name: Hoham
description: Jehovah impels, the king of Hebron who joined the league against Gibeon. He and his allies were defeated (Josh. 10:3, 5, 16-27).

name: Holy Spirit
description: The third Person of the adorable Trinity. His personality is proved (1) from the fact that the attributes of personality, as intelligence and volition, are ascribed to him (John 14:17, 26; 15:26; 1 Cor. 2:10, 11; 12:11).

name: Hophni
description: Pugilist or client, one of the two sons of Eli, the high priest (1 Sam. 1:3; 2:34), who, because he was “very old,” resigned to them the active duties of his office.

name: Hosah
description: A Levite of the family of Merari (1 Chr. 16:38).

name: Hosea
description: Salvation, the son of Beeri, and author of the book of prophecies bearing his name. He belonged to the kingdom of Israel.

name: Hoshea
title: Hoshea (son of Elah)
description: The last king of Israel. He conspired against and slew his predecessor, Pekah (Isa. 7:16), but did not ascend the throne till after an interregnum of warfare of eight years (2 Kings 17:1, 2).

name: Hoshea
title: Hoshea (son of Azaziah)
description: The ruler of Ephraim in David’s time.

name: Hotham
description: A stroke, great-grandson of Asher (1 Chr. 7:35).

name: Hul
description: Circle, the second son of Aram (Gen. 10:23), and grandson of Shem.

name: Huldah
description: Weasel, a prophetess; the wife of Shallum. She was consulted regarding the “book of the law” discovered by the high priest Hilkiah (2 Kings 22:14-20; 2 Chr. 34:22-28).

name: Hur
description: The husband of Miriam, Moses’ sister (Ex. 17:10-12). He was associated with Aaron in charge of the people when Moses was absent on Sinai (Ex. 24:14).

name: Hur
title: Hur (Numbers 31:8)
description: One of the five princes of Midian who were defeated and slain by the Israelites under the command of Phinehas (Num. 31:8).

name: Hurai
description: Linen-worker, one of David’s heroes, a native of the valley of Mount Gaash (1 Chr. 11:32).

name: Huram
title: Huram (son of Benjamin)
description: Generally “Huram,” one of the sons of Bela (1 Chr. 8:5).

name: Hushai
description: Quick, “the Archite,” “the king’s friend” (1 Chr. 27:33).

name: Ibhar
description: Chosen, one of David’s sons (1 Chr. 3:6; 2 Sam. 5:15).

name: Ibzan
description: Illustrious, the tenth judge of Israel (Judg. 12:8-10). He ruled seven years.

name: Iddo
title: Iddo (father of Ahinadab)
description: Timely. The father of Ahinadab, who was one of Solomon’s purveyors (1 Kings 4:14).

name: Iddo
title: Iddo (son of Zechariah)
description: Lovely. The son of Zechariah (1 Chr. 27:21), the ruler of Manasseh in David’s time.

name: Iddo
title: Iddo (2 Chronicles 9:29)
description: Lovely. A prophet of Judah who wrote the history of Rehoboam and Abijah (2 Chr. 12:15). He has been identified with Oded (2 Chr. 15:1).

name: Igal
title: Igal (son of Joseph)
description: One of the spies of the tribe of Issachar.

name: Igal
title: Igal (son of Nathan)
description: Son of Nathan of Zobah, and one of David’s warriors (2 Sam. 23:36).

name: Ilai
description: An Ahohite, one of David’s chief warriors (1 Chr. 11:29); called also Zalmon (2 Sam. 23:28).

name: Imla
description: Replenisher, the father of Micaiah the prophet (2 Chr. 18:7, 8).

name: Immer
title: Immer (1 Chronicles 24:14)
description: The head of the sixteenth priestly order (1 Chr. 24:14).

name: Immer
title: Immer (father of Zadok)
description: The father of Zadok (Neh. 3:29).

name: Iphedeiah
description: Set free by Jehovah, a chief of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chr. 8:25).

name: Ira
title: Ira (2 Samuel 20:26)
description: A Jairite and priest, a royal chaplain (2 Sam. 20:26) or confidential adviser (comp. 2 Sam. 8:18; 1 Chr. 18:17).

name: Ira
title: Ira (son of Ikkesh)
description: A Tekoite, one of David’s thirty warriors (2 Sam. 23:26).

name: Ira
title: Ira (2 Samuel 23:38)
description: An Ithrite, also one of David’s heroes (2 Sam. 23:38).

name: Irad
description: Runner; wild ass, one of the antediluvian patriarchs, the father of Mehujael (Gen. 4:18), and grandson of Cain.

name: Iram
description: Citizen, chief of an Edomite tribe in Mount Seir (Gen. 36:43).

name: Isaac
description: The only son of Abraham by Sarah. He was the longest lived of the three patriarchs (Gen. 21:1-3). He was circumcised when eight days old (4-7); and when he was probably two years old a great feast was held in connection with his being weaned.

name: Isaiah
description: The son of Amoz (Isa. 1:1; 2:1), who was apparently a man of humble rank. His wife was called “the prophetess” (8:3), either because she was endowed with the prophetic gift, like Deborah (Judg. 4:4) and Huldah (2 Kings 22:14-20), or simply because she was the wife of “the prophet” (Isa. 38:1).

name: Iscah
description: Spy, the daughter of Haran and sister of Milcah and Lot (Gen. 11:29, 31).

name: Ish-bosheth
description: Man of shame or humiliation, the youngest of Saul’s four sons, and the only one who survived him (2 Sam. 2-4). His name was originally Eshbaal (1 Chr. 8:33; 9:39).

name: Ishbak
description: Leaving, one of Abraham’s sons by Keturah (Gen. 25:2).

name: Ishbi-benob
description: My seat at Nob, one of the Rephaim, whose spear was three hundred shekels in weight. He was slain by Abishai (2 Sam. 21:16, 17).

name: Ishmael
title: Ishmael (Son of Hagar)
description: Abraham’s eldest son, by Hagar the concubine (Gen. 16:15; 17:23). He was born at Mamre, when Abraham was eighty-six years of age, eleven years after his arrival in Canaan (16:3; 21:5).

name: Ishmael
description: The son of Nethaniah, “of the seed royal” (Jer. 40:8, 15). He plotted against Gedaliah, and treacherously put him and others to death.

name: Ishmaiah
description: Son of Obadiah, and viceroy of Zebulun under David and Solomon (1 Chr. 27:19).

name: Ismaiah
description: A Gibeonite who joined David at Ziklag, “a hero among the thirty and over the thirty” (1 Chr. 12:4).

name: Israel
title: Jacob (Israel)
description: One who follows on another’s heels; supplanter, (Gen. 25:26; 27:36; Hos. 12:2-4), the second born of the twin sons of Isaac by Rebekah.

name: Issachar
description: Hired (Gen. 30:18). “God hath given me,” said Leah, “my hire (Heb. sekhari)...and she called his name Issachar.” He was Jacob’s ninth son, and was born in Padan-aram (comp. 28:2).

name: Ithamar
description: Palm isle, the fourth and youngest son of Aaron (1 Chr. 6:3). He was consecrated to the priesthood along with his brothers (Ex. 6:23); and after the death of Nadab and Abihu, he and Eleazar alone discharged the functions of that office (Lev. 10:6, 12; Num. 3:4).

name: Ittai
title: Ittai (2 Samuel 15:19)
description: A native of Gath, a Philistine, who had apparently the command of the six hundred heroes who formed David’s band during his wanderings (2 Sam. 15:19-22; comp. 1 Sam. 23:13; 27:2; 30:9, 10).

name: Ittai
title: Ittai (son of Ribai)
description: A Benjamite, one of David’s thirty heroes (2 Sam. 23:29).

name: Izhar
description: Oil, one of the sons of Kohath, and grandson of Levi (Ex. 6:18, 21; Num. 16:1).

name: Jaakobah
description: Heel-catcher, a form of the name Jacob, one of the descendants of Simeon (1 Chr. 4:36).

name: Jaala
description: A wild she-goat, one of the Nethinim, whose descendants returned from the Captivity (Neh. 7:58).

name: Jaalam
description: Concealer, the second of Esau’s three sons by Aholibamah (Gen. 36:5, 14).

name: Jaanai
description: Mourner, one of the chief Gadites (1 Chr. 5:12).

name: Jaasiel
description: Made by God, one of David’s body-guard, the son of Abner (1 Chr. 27:21), called Jasiel in 1 Chr. 11:47.

name: Jaazaniah
title: Jaazaniah (son of Jeremiah)
description: The son of Jeremiah, and one of the chief Rechabites (Jer. 35:3).

name: Jaazaniah
title: Jaazaniah (son of Shaphan)
description: The son of Shaphan (Ezek. 8:11).

name: Jaaziah
description: Comforted by Jehovah, a descendant of Merari the Levite (1 Chr. 24:26, 27).

name: Jaaziel
description: Comforted by God, a Levitical musician (1 Chr. 15:18).

name: Jabal
description: A stream, a descendant of Cain, and brother of Jubal; “the father of such as dwell in tents and have cattle” (Gen. 4:20). This description indicates that he led a wandering life.

name: Jabesh
description: The father of Shallum (2 Kings 15:10, 13, 14), who usurped the throne of Israel on the death of Zachariah.

name: Jabez
description: A descendant of Judah, of whom it is recorded that “God granted him that which he requested” (1 Chr. 4:9, 10).

name: Jabin
description: A king of Hazor, at the time of the entrance of Israel into Canaan (Josh. 11:1-14), whose overthrow and that of the northern chief with whom he had entered into a confederacy against Joshua was the crowning act in the conquest of the land (11:21-23; comp. 14:6-15).

name: Jabin
title: Jabin (king of Hazor)
description: Another king of Hazor, called “the king of Canaan,” who overpowered the Israelites of the north one hundred and sixty years after Joshua’s death, and for twenty years held them in painful subjection.

name: Jachan
description: Mourner, one of the chief Gadite “brothers” in Bashan (1 Chr. 5:13).

name: Jachin
title: Jachin (son of Simeon)
description: The fourth son of Simeon (Gen. 46:10), called also Jarib (1 Chr. 4:24).

name: Jachin
title: Jachin (1 Chronicles 9:10)
description: One of the priests who returned from the Exile (1 Chr. 9:10).

name: Jachin
title: Jachin (1 Chronicles 24:17)
description: The head of one of the courses (the twenty-first) of priests (1 Chr. 24:17).

name: Jaddua
title: Jaddua (Nehemiah 10:21)
description: One of the chiefs who subscribed the covenant (Neh. 10:21).

name: Jaddua
title: Jaddua (son of Johanan)
description: The last high priest mentioned in the Old Testament (Neh. 12:11, 22), sons of Jonathan.

name: Jadon
description: Judge, a Meronothite who assisted in rebuilding the walls of Jerusalem (Neh. 3:7).

name: Jael
description: Mountain-goat, the wife of Heber the Kenite (Judg. 4:17-22). When the Canaanites were defeated by Barak, Sisera, the captain of Jabin’s army, fled and sought refuge with the friendly tribe of Heber, beneath the oaks of Zaanaim.

name: Jahath
title: Jahath (son of Shimei)
description: A son of Shimei, and grandson of Gershom (1 Chr. 23:10).

name: Jahath
title: Jahath (son of Shelomoth)
description: One of the sons of Shelomoth, of the family of Kohath (1 Chr. 24:22).

name: Jahath
title: Jahath (2 Chronicles 34:12)
description: A Levite of the family of Merari, one of the overseers of the repairs of the temple under Josiah (2 Chr. 34:12).

name: Jahaziel
title: Jahaziel (1 Chronicles 16:6)
description: A priest who accompanied the removal of the ark to Jerusalem (1 Chr. 16:6).

name: Jahaziel
title: Jahaziel (son of Hebron)
description: The third son of Hebron (1 Chr. 23:19).

name: Jahaziel
title: Jahaziel (son of Zechariah)
description: The son of Zechariah, a Levite of the family of Asaph (2 Chr. 20:14-17). He encouraged Jehoshaphat against the Moabites and Ammonites.

name: Jahdai
description: Grasper, a descendant of Caleb, of the family of Hezron (1 Chr. 2:47).

name: Jahzeel
description: Allotted by God, the first of the sons of Naphtali (Gen. 46:24).

name: Jahzerah
description: Returner, the son of Meshullam, and father of Adiel (1 Chr. 9:12).

name: Jair
title: Jair (father of Elhanan)
description: The father of Elhanan, who slew Lahmi, the brother of Goliath (1 Chr. 20:5).

name: Jair
title: Jair (son of Shimei)
description: A Benjamite, the father of Mordecai, Esther’s uncle (Esther 2:5).

name: Jairus
description: A ruler of the synagogue at Capernaum, whose only daughter Jesus restored to life (Mark 5:22; Luke 8:41).

name: Jakeh
description: Pious, the father of Agur (Prov. 30:1). Nothing is known of him.

name: Jakim
title: Jakim (1 Chronicles 24:12)
description: Chief of the twelfth priestly order (1 Chr. 24:12).

name: Jalon
description: Lodger, the last of the four sons of Ezra, of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr. 4:17).

name: Jambres
description: One of those who opposed Moses in Egypt (2 Tim. 3:8).

name: James
title: James (Son of Zebedee)
description: The son of Zebedee and Salome; an elder brother of John the apostle. He was one of the twelve. He was by trade a fisherman, in partnership with Peter (Matt. 20:20; 27:56).

name: James
title: James (Son of Alphaeus)
description: The son of Alphaeus, or Cleopas, “the brother” or near kinsman or cousin of our Lord (Gal. 1:18, 19), called James “the Less,” or “the Little,” probably because he was of low stature.

name: James
title: James (Brother of Jesus)
description: The son of Alphaeus, or Cleopas, “the brother” or near kinsman or cousin of our Lord (Gal. 1:18, 19), called James “the Less,” or “the Little,” probably because he was of low stature.

name: Jannes
description: One of the Egyptians who “withstood Moses” (2 Tim. 3:8).

name: Japheth
description: Wide spreading: “God shall enlarge Japheth” (Heb. Yaphat Elohim le-Yephet, Gen. 9:27. Some, however, derive the name from yaphah, “to be beautiful;” hence white), one of the sons of Noah, mentioned last in order (Gen. 5:32; 6:10; 7:13), perhaps first by birth (10:21; comp. 9:24).

name: Japhia
title: Japhia (Joshua 10:3)
description: The king of Lachish, who joined in the confederacy against Joshua (Josh. 10:3), and was defeated and slain. In one of the Amarna tablets he speaks of himself as king of Gezer.

name: Japhia
title: Japhia (son of David)
description: One of the sons of David (2 Sam. 5:15), born in Jerusalem.

name: Jared
description: The fourth antediluvian patriarch in descent from Seth (Gen. 5:15-20; Luke 3:37), the father of Enoch; called Jered in 1 Chr. 1:2.

name: Jarib
title: Jarib (Ezra 8:16)
description: One of the chiefs sent by Ezra to bring up the priests to Jerusalem (Ezra 8:16).

name: Jashen
description: Sleeping, called also Hashem (1 Chr. 11:34); a person, several of whose sons were in David’s body-guard (2 Sam. 23:32).

name: Jasher
description: Upright. “The Book of Jasher,” rendered in the LXX. “the Book of the Upright One,” by the Vulgate “the Book of Just Ones,” was probably a kind of national sacred song-book, a collection of songs in praise of the heroes of Israel, a “book of golden deeds,” a national anthology.

name: Jashobeam
title: Jashobeam (son of Zabdiel)
description: Dweller among the people; or to whom the people turn, the Hachmonite (1 Chr. 11:11), one of David’s chief heroes who joined him at Ziklag (12:6).

name: Jashub
title: Jashub (son of Issachar)
description: The third of Issachar’s four sons (1 Chr. 7:1); called also Job (Gen. 46:13).

name: Jason
description: He that will cure, the host of Paul and Silas in Thessalonica. The Jews assaulted his house in order to seize Paul, but failing to find him, they dragged Jason before the ruler of the city (Acts 17:5-9).

name: Javan
description: The fourth “son” of Japheth (Gen. 10:2), whose descendants settled in Greece, i.e., Ionia, which bears the name of Javan in Hebrew.

name: Jebusite
description: The name of the original inhabitants of Jebus, mentioned frequently among the seven nations doomed to destruction (Gen. 10:16; 15:21; Ex. 3:8, 17; 13:5, etc.).

name: Jecoliah
description: Able through Jehovah, the wife of King Amaziah, and mother of King Uzziah (2 Chr. 26:3).

name: Jedaiah
title: Jedaiah (son of Shimri)
description: Invoker of Jehovah. The son of Shimri, a chief Simeonite (1 Chr. 4:37).

name: Jedaiah
title: Jedaiah (son of Joiarib)
description: A priest in Jerusalem after the Exile (1 Chr. 9:10).

name: Jedaiah
title: Jedaiah (1 Chronicles 24:7)
description: Knowing Jehovah. The chief of one of the courses of the priests (1 Chr. 24:7).

name: Jedaiah
title: Jedaiah (son of Harumaph)
description: One of those who repaired the walls of Jerusalem after the return from Babylon (Neh. 3:10).

name: Jediael
title: Jediael (son of Benjamin)
description: One of the sons of Benjamin, whose descendants numbered 17,200 warriors (1 Chr. 7:6, 10, 11).

name: Jediael
title: Jediael (son of Shimri)
description: A Shimrite, one of David’s bodyguard (1 Chr. 11:45). Probably same as in 12:20.

name: Jediael
title: Jediael (son of Meshelemiah)
description: A Korhite of the family of Ebiasaph, and one of the gate-keepers to the temple (1 Chr. 26:2).

name: Jeduthun
title: Jeduthun (Ethan)
description: A Levite of the family of Merari, one of the leaders of the temple music (1 Chr. 6:44; 15:17, 19). He was probably the same as Jeduthun.

name: Jehaleleel
description: A descendant of Judah (1 Chr. 4:16).

name: Jehalelel
description: A Levite of the family of Merari (2 Chr. 29:12).

name: Jehdeiah
title: Jehdeiah (son of Shubael)
description: One of the Levitical attendants at the temple, a descendant of Shubael (1 Chr. 24:20).

name: Jehdeiah
title: Jehdeiah (1 Chronicles 27:30)
description: A Meronothite, herdsman of the asses under David and Solomon (1 Chr. 27:30).

name: Jehiel
title: Jehiel (son of Hothan)
description: One of David’s guard (1 Chr. 11:44).

name: Jehiel
title: Jehiel (1 Chronicles 15:18)
description: One of the Levites “of the second degree,” appointed to conduct the music on the occasion of the ark’s being removed to Jerusalem (1 Chr. 15:18, 20).

name: Jehiel
title: Jehiel (son of Hachmoni)
description: A Hachmonite, a tutor in the family of David toward the close of his reign (1 Chr. 27:32).

name: Jehiel
title: Jehiel (son of Jehoshaphat)
description: The second of Jehoshaphat’s six sons (2 Chr. 21:2).

name: Jehiel
title: Jehiel (2 Chronicles 29:14)
description: One of the Levites of the family of Heman who assisted Hezekiah in his work of reformation (2 Chr. 29:14).

name: Jehiel
title: Jehiel (2 Chronicles 35:8)
description: A “prince” and “ruler of the house of God” who contributed liberally to the renewal of the temple sacrifices under Josiah (2 Chr. 35:8).

name: Jehiel
title: Jehiel (father of Obadiah)
description: The father of Obadiah (Ezra 8:9).

name: Jehizkiah
description: Jehovah strengthens, one of the chiefs of Ephraim (2 Chr. 28:12).

name: Jehoaddan
description: Jehovah his ornament, the wife of King Jehoash, and mother of King Amaziah (2 Kings 14:2).

name: Jehoahaz
title: Jehoahaz (son of Jehu)
description: The son and successor of Jehu, king of Israel (2 Kings 10:35). He reigned seventeen years, and followed the evil ways of the house of Jeroboam.

name: Jehoahaz
title: Jehoahaz (son of Josiah)
description: A son of king Josiah (1 Chr. 3:15; Jer. 22:11), who was elected to succeed his father on the throne, although he was two years younger than his brother Eliakim.

name: Jehohanan
title: Jehohanan (son of Meshelemiah)
description: A Korhite, the head of one of the divisions of the temple porters (1 Chr. 26:3).

name: Jehohanan
title: Jehohanan (2 Chronicles 17:15)
description: One of Jehoshaphat’s “captains” (2 Chr. 17:15).

name: Jehoiachin
description: Succeeded his father Jehoiakin (B.C. 599) when only eight years of age, and reigned for one hundred days (2 Chr. 36:9). He is also called Jeconiah (Jer. 24:1; 27:20, etc.), and Coniah (22:24; 37:1).

name: Jehoiada
title: Jehoiada (father of Benaiah)
description: The father of Benaiah, who was one of David’s chief warriors (2 Sam. 8:18; 20:23).

name: Jehoiada
title: Jehoiada (father of Zacharias)
description: The high priest at the time of Athaliah’s usurpation of the throne of Judah. He married Jehosheba, or Jehoshabeath, the daughter of king Jehoram (2 Chr. 22:11), and took an active part along with his wife in the preservation and training of Jehoash when Athaliah slew all the royal family of Judah.

name: Jehoiakim
description: He whom Jehovah has set up, the second son of Josiah, and eighteenth king of Judah, which he ruled over for eleven years (B.C. 610-599).

name: Jehoiarib
description: Jehovah defends, a priest at Jerusalem, head of one of the sacerdotal courses (1 Chr. 9:10; 24:7). His “course” went up from Babylon after the Exile (Ezra 2:36-39; Neh. 7:39-42).

name: Jehonathan
title: Jehonathan (son of Uzziah)
description: One of the stewards of David’s store-houses (1 Chr. 27:25).

name: Jehonathan
title: Jehonathan (2 Chronicles 17:8)
description: A Levite who taught the law to the people of Judah (2 Chr. 17:8).

name: Jehoram
description: The eldest son and successor of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah. He reigned eight years (B.C. 892-885) alone as king of Judah, having been previously for some years associated with his father (2 Chr. 21:5, 20; 2 Kings 8:16).

name: Jehoram
title: Jehoram (2 Chronicles 17:8)
description: A priest sent by Jehoshaphat to instructruct the people in Judah (2 Chr. 17:8).

name: Jehoshabeath
description: Jehovah-swearing, the daughter of Jehoram, the king of Israel. She is called Jehoshabeath in 2 Chr. 22:11. She was the only princess of the royal house who was married to a high priest, Jehoiada (2 Chr. 22:11).

name: Jehoshaphat
title: Jehoshaphat (son of Ahilud)
description: Son of Ahilud, “recorder” or annalist under David and Solomon (2 Sam. 8:16), a state officer of high rank, chancellor or vizier of the kingdom.

name: Jehoshaphat
title: Jehoshaphat (son of Paruah)
description: Solomon’s purveyor in Issachar (1 Kings 4:17).

name: Jehoshaphat
description: The son and successor of Asa, king of Judah. After fortifying his kingdom against Israel (2 Chr. 17:1, 2), he set himself to cleanse the land of idolatry (1 Kings 22:43).

name: Jehoshaphat
title: Jehoshaphat (son of Nimshi)
description: The son of Nimshi, and father of Jehu, king of Israel (2 Kings 9:2, 14).

name: Jehoshaphat
title: Jehoshaphat (1 Chronicles 15:24)
description: One of the priests who accompanied the removal of the ark to Jerusalem (1 Chr. 15:24).

name: Jehozabad
title: Jehozabad (son of Shimrith)
description: The son of Shomer, one of the two conspirators who put king Jehoash to death in Millo in Jerusalem (2 Kings 12:21).

name: Jehozabad
title: Jehozabad (son of Shimei)
description: The son of Obed-edom (1 Chr. 26:4), one of the Levite porters.

name: Jehu
title: Jehu (son of Hanani)
description: The son of Hanani, a prophet of Judah (1 Kings 16:1, 7; 2 Chr. 19:2; 20:34), who pronounced the sentence of God against Baasha, the king of Israel.

name: Jehu
description: King of Israel, the son of Jehoshaphat (2 Kings 9:2), and grandson of Nimshi. The story of his exaltation to the throne is deeply interesting.

name: Jehu
title: Jehu (son of Obed)
description: The son of Obed, and father of Azariah (1 Chr. 2:38).

name: Jehu
title: Jehu (1 Chronicles 12:3)
description: One of the Benjamite slingers that joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:3).

name: Jehudi
description: A Jew, son of Nethaniah. He was sent by the princes to invite Baruch to read Jeremiah’s roll to them (Jer. 36:14, 21).

name: Jeiel
title: Jeiel (1 Chronicles 5:7)
description: A Reubenite chief.

name: Jeiel
title: Jeiel (1 Chronicles 15:18)
description: One of the Levites who took part in praising God on the removal of the ark to Jerusalem (1 Chr. 16:5).

name: Jeiel
title: Jeiel (2 Chronicles 29:13)
description: A Levite of the sons of Asaph.

name: Jeiel
title: Jeiel (2 Chronicles 35:9)
description: One of the chief Levites, who made an offering for the restoration of the Passover by Josiah (2 Chr. 35:9).

name: Jemima
description: Dove, the eldest of Job’s three daughters born after his time of trial (Job 42:14).

name: Jemuel
description: One of Simeon’s five sons (1 Chr. 4:24), called also Jemuel (Gen. 46:10).

name: Jephthah
description: Whom God sets free, or the breaker through, a “mighty man of valour” who delivered Israel from the oppression of the Ammonites (Judg. 11:1-33), and judged Israel six years (12:7).

name: Jephunneh
description: The father of Caleb, who was Joshua’s companion in exploring Canaan (Num. 13:6), a Kenezite (Josh. 14:14).

name: Jephunneh
title: Jephunneh (son of Jether)
description: One of the descendants of Asher (1 Chr. 7:38).

name: Jerahmeel
title: Jerahmeel (son of Hezron)
description: The son of Hezron, the brother of Caleb (1 Chr. 2:9, 25, 26, etc.).

name: Jerahmeel
title: Jerahmeel (son of Kish)
description: The son of Kish, a Levite (1 Chr. 24:29).

name: Jerahmeel
title: Jerahmeel (son of Hammelech)
description: Son of Hammelech (Jer. 36:26).

name: Jered
description: A son of Ezra probably (1 Chr. 4:18).

name: Jeremiah
title: Jeremiah (father of Hamutal)
description: The father of Hamutal (2 Kings 23:31), the wife of Josiah.

name: Jeremiah
title: Jeremiah (1 Chronicles 5:24)
description: One of the chiefs of the tribe of Manasseh on the east of Jordan (1 Chr. 5:24).

name: Jeremiah
title: Jeremiah (1 Chronicles 12:4)
description: A Benjamite slinger who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:4).

name: Jeremiah
title: Jeremiah (1 Chronicles 12:10)
description: A Gadite who joined David in the wilderness (1 Chr. 12:10).

name: Jeremiah
title: Jeremiah (1 Chronicles 12:13)
description: A Gadite warrior (1 Chr. 12:13).

name: Jeremiah
description: One of the “greater prophets” of the Old Testament, son of Hilkiah (q.v.), a priest of Anathoth (Jer. 1:1; 32:6). He was called to the prophetical office when still young (1:6), in the thirteenth year of Josiah (B.C. 628).

name: Jeremoth
title: Jeremoth (son of Mushi)
description: A Merarite Levite.

name: Jerimoth
title: Jerimoth (son of Bela)
description: One of the sons of Bela (1 Chr. 7:7).

name: Jerimoth
title: Jerimoth (1 Chronicles 12:5)
description: A Benjamite slinger who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:5).

name: Jerimoth
title: Jerimoth (son of Heman)
description: A Levitical musician under Heman his father (1 Chr. 25:4).

name: Jerimoth
title: Jerimoth (son of Azriel)
description: Ruler of Naphtali.

name: Jerimoth
title: Jerimoth (son of David)
description: One of David’s sons (2 Chr. 11:18).

name: Jerimoth
title: Jerimoth (2 Chronicles 31:13)
description: A Levite, one of the overseers of the temple offerings (2 Chr. 31:13) in the reign of Hezekiah.

name: Jeroboam
description: The son of Nebat (1 Kings 11:26-39), “an Ephrathite,” the first king of the ten tribes, over whom he reigned twenty-two years (B.C. 976-945).

name: Jeroboam
title: Jeroboam (son of Joash)
description: Jeroboam II., the son and successor of Jehoash, and the fourteenth king of Israel, over which he ruled for forty-one years, B.C. 825-784 (2 Kings 14:23).

name: Jeroham
title: Jeroham (son of Elihu)
description: Father of Elkanah, and grandfather of the prophet Samuel (1 Sam. 1:1).

name: Jeroham
title: Jeroham (son of Pelaliah)
description: A priest, perhaps the same as in Neh. 11:12.

name: Jeroham
title: Jeroham (father of Azareel)
description: The father of Azareel, the “captain” of the tribe of Dan (1 Chr. 27:22).

name: Jeroham
title: Jeroham (father of Azariah)
description: One whose son assisted in placing Joash on the throne.

name: Jerubbesheth
description: Contender with the shame; i.e., idol, a surname also of Gideon (2 Sam. 11:21).

name: Jerushah
description: Possession, or possessed; i.e., “by a husband”, the wife of Uzziah, and mother of king Jotham (2 Kings 15:33).

name: Jesaiah
title: Jesaiah (son of Hananiah)
description: One of the three sons of Hananiah (1 Chr. 3:21).

name: Jeshaiah
title: Jeshaiah (son of Rehabiah)
description: A Kohathite Levite, the father of Joram, of the family of Eliezer (1 Chr. 26:25); called also Isshiah (24:21).

name: Jeshaiah
title: Jeshaiah (son of Jeduthun)
description: One of the sons of Jeduthum (1 Chr. 25:3, 15).

name: Jeshaiah
title: Jeshaiah (son of Athaliah)
description: Son of Athaliah (Ezra 8:7).

name: Jesharelah
description: Upright towards God, the head of the seventh division of Levitical musicians (1 Chr. 25:14).

name: Jeshebeab
description: Seat of his father, the head of the fourteenth division of priests (1 Chr. 24:13).

name: Jesher
description: Uprightness, the first of the three sons of Caleb by Azubah (1 Chr. 2:18).

name: Jeshua
title: Jeshua (2 Chronicles 31:15)
description: A Levite appointed by Hezekiah to distribute offerings in the priestly cities (2 Chr. 31:15).

name: Jeshua
title: Jeshua (son of Kadmiel)
description: Son of Kadmiel (Neh. 12:24).

name: Jeshua
title: Jeshua (son of Jozadak)
description: Head of the ninth priestly order (Ezra 2:36); called also Jeshuah (1 Chr. 24:11).

name: Jesse
description: Firm, or a gift, a son of Obed, the son of Boaz and Ruth (Ruth 4:17, 22; Matt. 1:5, 6; Luke 3:32). He was the father of eight sons, the youngest of whom was David (1 Sam. 17:12).

name: Jesus
description: A Jewish Christian surnamed Justus (Col. 4:11). Je’sus, the proper, as Christ is the official, name of our Lord. To distinguish him from others so called, he is spoken of as “Jesus of Nazareth” (John 18:7), and “Jesus the son of Joseph” (John 6:42).

name: Jesus
title: Jesus Christ
description: Anointed, the Greek translation of the Hebrew word rendered “Messiah” (q.v.), the official title of our Lord, occurring five hundred and fourteen times in the New Testament.

name: Jether
title: Jether (son of Gideon)
description: The oldest of Gideon’s seventy sons (Judg. 8:20).

name: Jether
title: Jether (father of Amasa)
description: The father of Amasa, David’s general (1 Kings 2:5, 32); called Ithra (2 Sam. 17:25).

name: Jether
title: Jether (son of Jada)
description: One of Judah’s posterity.

name: Jetheth
description: A peg, or a prince, one of the Edomitish kings of Mount Seir (Gen. 36:40).

name: Jethro
description: “The priest of Midian,” Moses’ father-in-law (Ex. 2:18)=Raguel (Num. 10:29). If he be identified with Jethro (q.v.), then this may be regarded as his proper name, and Jether or Jethro (i.e., “excellency”) as his official title.

name: Jetur
description: An enclosure, one of the twelve sons of Ishmael (Gen. 25:15).

name: Jeuel
description: Snatched away by God, a descendant of Zerah (1 Chr. 9:6).

name: Jeush
title: Jeush (son of Esau)
description: The oldest of Esau’s three sons by Aholibamah (Gen. 36:5, 14, 18).

name: Jeush
title: Jeush (son of Bilhan)
description: A son of Bilhan, grandson of Benjamin (1 Chr. 7:10).

name: Jeush
title: Jeush (son of Shimei)
description: A Levite, one of the sons of Shimei (1 Chr. 23:10, 11).

name: Jeush
title: Jeush (son of Rehoboam)
description: One of the three sons of Rehoboam (2 Chr. 11:19).

name: Jezaniah
description: A Maachathite (2 Kings 25:23; Jer. 40:8; 42:1). He is also called Azariah (Jer. 43:2).

name: Jezebel
description: Chaste, the daughter of Ethbaal, the king of the Zidonians, and the wife of Ahab, the king of Israel (1 Kings 16:31). This was the “first time that a king of Israel had allied himself by marriage with a heathen princess; and the alliance was in this case of a peculiarly disastrous kind.

name: Jeziel
description: Assembled by God, a son of Azmaveth. He was one of the Benjamite archers who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:3).

name: Joab
description: One of the three sons of Zeruiah, David’s sister, and “captain of the host” during the whole of David’s reign (2 Sam. 2:13; 10:7; 11:1; 1 Kings 11:15).

name: Joah
title: Joah (son of Asaph)
description: The son of Asaph, and “recorder” (q.v.) or chronicler to King Hezekiah (2 Kings 18:18, 26, 37).

name: Joah
title: Joah (son of Shimei)
description: One of the sons of Obed-edom (1 Chr. 26:4), a Korhite porter.

name: Joah
title: Joah (son of Joahaz)
description: Son of Joahaz, and “recorder” (q.v.) or keeper of the state archives under King Josiah (2 Chr. 34:8).

name: Joahaz
description: (2 Chr. 34:8), a contracted form of Jehoahaz (q.v.).

name: Joanna
title: Joanna (son of Rhesa)
description: The grandson of Zerubbabel, in the lineage of Christ (Luke 3:27); the same as Hananiah (1 Chr. 3:19).

name: Joanna
title: Joanna (wife of Chuza)
description: The wife of Chuza, the steward of Herod Antipas, tetrarch of Galilee (Luke 8:3). She was one of the women who ministered to our Lord, and to whom he appeared after his resurrection (Luke 8:3; 24:10).

name: Joash
title: Joash (father of Gideon)
description: A contracted form of Jehoash, the father of Gideon (Judg. 6:11, 29; 8:13, 29, 32).

name: Joash
title: Joash (son of Ahab)
description: One of King Ahab’s sons (1 Kings 22:26).

name: Joash
title: Joash (son of Ahaziah)
description: The son of King Ahaziah. While yet an infant, he was saved from the general massacre of the family by his aunt Jehosheba, and was apparently the only surviving descendant of Solomon (2 Chr. 21:4, 17).

name: Joash
title: Joash (son of Jehoahaz)
description: The son and successor of Jehoahaz, king of Israel (2 Kings 14:1; comp. 12:1; 13:10). When he ascended the throne the kingdom was suffering from the invasion of the Syrians.

name: Joash
title: Joash (son of Shemaah)
description: One of the Benjamite archers who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:3).

name: Joash
title: Joash (1 Chronicles 27:28)
description: One who had charge of the royal stores of oil under David and Solomon (1 Chr. 27:28).

name: Job
description: Persecuted, an Arabian patriarch who resided in the land of Uz (q.v.). While living in the midst of great prosperity, he was suddenly overwhelmed by a series of sore trials that fell upon him.

name: Jobab
title: Jobab (son of Joktan)
description: One of the sons of Joktan, and founder of an Arabian tribe (Gen. 10:29).

name: Jobab
title: Jobab (son of Zerah)
description: King of Edom, succeeded Bela (Gen. 36:33, 34).

name: Jobab
title: Jobab (Joshua 11:1)
description: A Canaanitish king (Josh. 11:1) who joined the confederacy against Joshua.

name: Jochebed
description: Jehovah is her glory, the wife of Amram, and the mother of Miriam, Aaron, and Moses (Num. 26:59). She is spoken of as the sister of Kohath, Amram’s father (Ex. 6:20; comp. 16, 18; 2:1-10).

name: Joel
title: Joel (son of Samuel)
description: The oldest of Samuel’s two sons appointed by him as judges in Beersheba (1 Sam. 8:2).

name: Joel
title: Joel (1 Chronicles 11:38)
description: One of David’s famous warriors (1 Chr. 11:38).

name: Joel
title: Joel (1 Chronicles 15:7)
description: A Levite of the family of Gershom (1 Chr. 15:7, 11).

name: Joel
title: Joel (son of Pethuel)
description: The second of the twelve minor prophets. He was the son of Pethuel. His personal history is only known from his book.

name: Joelah
description: A Benjamite who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:7).

name: Joezer
description: Jehovah is his help, one of the Korhites who became part of David’s body-guard (1 Chr. 12:6).

name: Johanan
description: Son of Careah, one of the Jewish chiefs who rallied round Gedaliah, whom Nebuchadnezzar had made governor in Jerusalem (2 Kings 25:23; Jer. 40:8).

name: Johanan
title: Johanan (son of Josiah)
description: The oldest of King Josiah’s sons (1 Chr. 3:15).

name: Johanan
title: Johanan (1 Chronicles 12:12)
description: One of the Gadite heroes who joined David in the desert of Judah (1 Chr. 12:12).

name: John
title: John the Baptist
description: The “forerunner of our Lord.” We have but fragmentary and imperfect accounts of him in the Gospels. He was of priestly descent.

name: John
title: John the Apostle
description: THE APOSTLE, brother of James the “Greater” (Matt. 4:21; 10:2; Mark 1:19; 3:17; 10:35). He was one, probably the younger, of the sons of Zebedee (Matt. 4:21) and Salome (Matt. 27:56; comp. Mark 15:40), and was born at Bethsaida.

name: John
title: John (Relative of the High Priest)
description: One who, with Annas and Caiaphas, sat in judgment on the apostles Peter and John (Acts 4:6). He was of the kindred of the high priest; otherwise unknown.

name: Joiakim
description: (whom Jehovah has set up) = Jehoiakim, a high priest, the son and successor of Jeshua (Neh. 12:10, 12, 26).

name: Joiarib
title: Joiarib (father of Jedaiah)
description: The founder of one of the courses of the priests (Neh. 11:10).

name: Joiarib
title: Joiarib (Ezra 8:16)
description: A “man of understanding” whom Ezra sent to “bring ministers for the house of God.”

name: Joiarib
title: Joiarib (son of Zechariah)
description: A descendant of Judah.

name: Jokim
description: Whom Jehovah has set up, one of the descendants of Shelah (1 Chr. 4:22).

name: Jokshan
description: Snarer, the second son of Abraham and Keturah (Gen. 25:2, 3; 1 Chr. 1:32).

name: Joktan
description: Little, the second of the two sons of Eber (Gen. 10:25; 1 Chr. 1:19). There is an Arab tradition that Joktan (Arab. Kahtan) was the progenitor of all the purest tribes of Central and Southern Arabia.

name: Jonadab
title: Jonadab (son of Rechab)
description: A son of Rechab, the founder of a tribe who bound themselves by a vow to abstain from wine (Jer. 35:6-19). There were different settlements of Rechabites (Judg. 1:16; 4:11; 1 Chr. 2:55).

name: Jonadab
title: Jonadab (son of Shammah)
description: Son of Shammah, and David’s nephew, and also one of his chief warriors (2 Sam. 21:21). He slew a giant in Gath.

name: Jonah
description: A dove, the son of Amittai of Gath-hepher. He was a prophet of Israel, and predicted the restoration of the ancient boundaries (2 Kings 14:25-27) of the kingdom.

name: Jonas
description: The father of the apostles Peter (John 21:15-17) and Andrew; but the reading should be (also in 1:42), as in the Revised Version, “John,” instead of Jonas.

name: Jonathan
title: Jonathan (son of Gershom)
description: A Levite descended from Gershom (Judg. 18:30). His history is recorded in 17:7-13 and 18:30. The Rabbins changed this name into Manasseh “to screen the memory of the great lawgiver from the stain of having so unworthy an apostate among his near descendants.”

name: Jonathan
description: The eldest son of king Saul, and the bosom friend of David. He is first mentioned when he was about thirty years of age, some time after his father’s accession to the throne (1 Sam. 13:2).

name: Jonathan
title: Jonathan (son of Abiathar)
description: Son of the high priest Abiathar, and one who adhered to David at the time of Absalom’s rebellion (2 Sam. 15:27, 36). He is the last descendant of Eli of whom there is any record.

name: Joram
description: The son of Ahab and Jezebel, and successor to his brother Ahaziah on the throne of Israel. He reigned twelve years, B.C. 896-884 (2 Kings 1:17; 3:1).

name: Joram
title: Joram (son of Toi)
description: The son of Tou, king of Hamath, sent by his father to congratulate David on his victory over Hadarezer, king of Syria (1 Chr. 18:10; called Joram 2 Sam. 8:10).

name: Josabad
description: One of the Benjamite archers who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:4).

name: Josedech
description: Jehovah-justified, the son of the high priest Seraiah at the time of the Babylonian exile (1 Chr. 6:14, 15). He was carried into captivity by Nebuchadnezzar, and probably died in Babylon.

name: Joseph
title: Joseph (son of Jacob)
description: The elder of the two sons of Jacob by Rachel (Gen. 30:23, 24), who, on the occasion of his birth, said, “God hath taken away [Heb. ‘asaph] my reproach.”

name: Joseph
title: Joseph (son of Asaph)
description: One of the sons of Asaph, head of the first division of sacred musicians (1 Chr. 25:2, 9).

name: Joseph
title: Joseph (Mary's Husband)
description: The foster-father of our Lord (Matt. 1:16; Luke 3:23). He lived at Nazareth in Galilee (Luke 2:4). He is called a “just man.”

name: Joseph
title: Joseph (of Arimathea)
description: A native of Arimathea, probably the Ramah of the Old Testament (1 Sam. 1:19), a man of wealth, and a member of the Sanhedrim (Matt. 27:57; Luke 23:50), an “honourable counsellor, who waited for the kingdom of God.”

name: Joseph
title: Joseph (son of Judah)
description: The son of Judah, and father of Semei (Luke 3:26). Other two of the same name in the ancestry of Christ are also mentioned (3:24, 30).

name: Joshua
title: Joshua (son of Josedech)
description: The son of Jozadak, and high priest of the Jews under Zerubbabel (Neh. 7:7; 12:1, 7, 10, 26); called Joshua (Hag. 1:1, 12; 2:2, 4; Zech. 3:1, 3, 6, 8, 9).

name: Joshua
description: Jehovah is his help, or Jehovah the Saviour. The son of Nun, of the tribe of Ephraim, the successor of Moses as the leader of Israel.

name: Josiah
description: Healed by Jehovah, or Jehovah will support. The son of Amon, and his successor on the throne of Judah (2 Kings 22:1; 2 Chr. 34:1).

name: Josiah
title: Josiah (son of Zephaniah)
description: Common in later times among the Jews in Palestine (Matt. 23:37; Luke 13:34). It is noticeable that this familiar bird is only mentioned in these passages in connection with our Lord’s lamentation over the impenitence of Jerusalem.

name: Jotham
title: Jotham (son of Gideon)
description: The youngest of Gideon’s seventy sons. He escaped when the rest were put to death by the order of Abimelech (Judg. 9:5).

name: Jotham
description: The son and successor of Uzziah on the throne of Judah. As during his last years Uzziah was excluded from public life on account of his leprosy, his son, then twenty-five years of age, administered for seven years the affairs of the kingdom in his father’s stead (2 Chr. 26:21, 23; 27:1).

name: Jubal
description: Jubilee, music, Lamech’s second son by Adah, of the line of Cain. He was the inventor of “the harp” (Heb. kinnor, properly “lyre”) and “the organ” (Heb. ‘ugab, properly “mouth-organ” or Pan’s pipe), Gen. 4:21.

name: Jucal
description: Able, the son of Shelemiah. He is also called Jucal (Jer. 38:1). He was one of the two persons whom Zedekiah sent to request the prophet Jeremiah to pray for the kingdom (Jer. 37:3) during the time of its final siege by Nebuchadnezzar.

name: Juda
title: Juda (son of Joseph)
description: The father of Simeon in Christ’s maternal ancestry (Luke 3:30).

name: Judah
title: Judah (patriarch)
description: Praise, the fourth son of Jacob by Leah. The name originated in Leah’s words of praise to the Lord on account of his birth: “Now will I praise [Heb. odeh] Jehovah, and she called his name Yehudah” (Gen. 29:35).

name: Judas
title: Judas (of Galilee)
description: The Graecized form of Judah.

name: Judas
title: Judas (Jew of Damascus)
description: A Jew of Damascus (Acts 9:11), to whose house Ananias was sent. The street called “Straight” in which it was situated is identified with the modern “street of bazaars,” where is still pointed out the so-called “house of Judas.”

name: Judas
title: Judas Barsabas
description: A Christian teacher, surnamed Barsabas. He was sent from Jerusalem to Antioch along with Paul and Barnabas with the decision of the council (Acts 15:22, 27, 32).

name: Judas
title: Judas Iscariot
description: Son of Simon (John 6:71; 13:2, 26), surnamed Iscariot, i.e., a man of Kerioth (Josh. 15:25). His name is uniformly the last in the list of the apostles, as given in the synoptic (i.e., the first three) Gospels.

name: Jude
description: Judas. Among the apostles there were two who bore this name, (1) Judas (Jude 1:1; Matt. 13:55; John 14:22; Acts 1:13), called also Lebbaeus or Thaddaeus (Matt. 10:3; Mark 3:18); and (2) Judas Iscariot (Matt. 10:4; Mark 3:19).

name: Julia
description: A Christian woman at Rome to whom Paul sent his salutations (Rom. 16:15), supposed to be the wife of Philologus.

name: Julius
description: The centurion of the Augustan cohort, or the emperor’s body-guard, in whose charge Paul was sent prisoner to Rome (Acts 27:1, 3, 43). He entreated Paul “courteously,” showing in many ways a friendly regard for him.

name: Junia
description: (Rom. 16:7), a Christian at Rome to whom Paul sends salutations along with Andronicus.

name: Justus
description: A Jewish proselyte at Corinth, in whose house, next door to the synagogue, Paul held meetings and preached after he left the synagogue (Acts 18:7).

name: Kadmiel
description: Before God; i.e., his servant, one of the Levites who returned with Zerubbabel from the Captivity (Neh. 9:4; 10:9; 12:8).

name: Kareah
description: Bald, the father of Johanan and Jonathan, who for a time were loyal to Gedaliah, the Babylonian governor of Jerusalem (Jer. 40:8, 13, 15, 16).

name: Kedar
description: Dark-skinned, the second son of Ishmael (Gen. 25:13). It is the name for the nomadic tribes of Arabs, the Bedouins generally (Isa. 21:16; 42:11; 60:7; Jer. 2:10; Ezek. 27:21), who dwelt in the north-west of Arabia.

name: Kedemah
description: Eastward, the last-named of the sons of Ishmael (Gen. 25:15).

name: Kelita
description: Dwarf, a Levite who assisted Ezra in expounding the law to the people (Neh. 8:7; 10:10).

name: Kemuel
title: Kemuel (son of Nahor)
description: The third son of Nahor (Gen. 22:21).

name: Kemuel
title: Kemuel (son of Shiphtan)
description: Son of Shiphtan, appointed on behalf of the tribe of Ephraim to partition the land of Canaan (Num. 34:24).

name: Kenaz
title: Kenaz (son of Jephunneh)
description: Caleb’s younger brother, and father of Othniel (Josh. 15:17), whose family was of importance in Israel down to the time of David (1 Chr. 27:15). Some think that Othniel (Judg. 1:13), and not Kenaz, was Caleb’s brother.

name: Kenaz
title: Kenaz (son of Elah)
description: Caleb’s grandson (1 Chr. 4:15).

name: Keren-happuch
description: Horn of the face-paint = cosmetic-box, the name of Job’s third daughter (Job. 42:14), born after prosperity had returned to him.

name: Keturah
description: Incense, the wife of Abraham, whom he married probably after Sarah’s death (Gen. 25:1-6), by whom he had six sons, whom he sent away into the east country.

name: Kish
description: A Benjamite, the son of Abiel, and father of king Saul (1 Sam. 9:1, 3; 10:11, 21; 14:51; 2 Sam. 21:14). All that is recorded of him is that he sent his son Saul in search of his asses that had strayed, and that he was buried in Zelah.

name: Kish
title: Kish (son of Mahli)
description: A Levite of the family of Merari (1 Chr. 23:21; 24:29).

name: Kish
title: Kish (son of Abdi)
description: A Levite in the time of Hezekiah (2 Chr. 29:12).

name: Kish
title: Kish (father of Shimei)
description: The great-grandfather of Mordecai (Esther 2:5).

name: Kohath
description: Assembly, the second son of Levi, and father of Amram (Gen. 46:11). He came down to Egypt with Jacob, and lived to the age of one hundred and thirty-three years (Ex. 6:18).

name: Korah
title: Korah (son of Esau)
description: The third son of Esau, by Aholibamah (Gen. 36:14; 1 Chr. 1:35).

name: Korah
title: Korah (Levite)
description: A Levite, the son of Izhar, the brother of Amram, the father of Moses and Aaron (Ex. 6:21). The institution of the Aaronic priesthood and the Levitical service at Sinai was a great religious revolution.

name: Kore
title: Kore (son of Ebiasaph)
description: A Levite and temple-warder of the Korahites, the son of Asaph. He was father of Shallum and Meshelemiah, temple-porters (1 Chr. 9:19; 26:1).

name: Kore
title: Kore (son of Imnah)
description: A Levitical porter at the east gate of the temple (2 Chr. 31:14).

name: Laadan
title: Laadan (son of Gershon)
description: White, one of the two sons of Gershon, the son of Levi (Ex. 6:17; Num. 3:18, 21).

name: Laban
description: The son of Bethuel, who was the son of Nahor, Abraham’s brother. He lived at Haran in Mesopotamia. His sister Rebekah was Isaac’s wife (Gen. 24).

name: Laish
description: The father of Phalti (1 Sam. 25:44).

name: Lamech
title: Lamech (descendant of Cain)
description: The fifth in descent from Cain. He was the first to violate the primeval ordinance of marriage (Gen. 4:18-24). His address to his two wives, Adah and Zillah (4:23, 24), is the only extant example of antediluvian poetry.

name: Lamech
title: Lamech (father of Noah)
description: The seventh in descent from Seth, being the only son of Methuselah. Noah was the oldest of his several sons (Gen. 5:25-31; Luke 3:36).

name: Lapidoth
description: Torches. Deborah is called “the wife of Lapidoth” (Judg. 4:4). Some have rendered the expression “a woman of a fiery spirit,” under the supposition that Lapidoth is not a proper name, a woman of a torch-like spirit.

name: Lazarus
title: Lazarus (John 11:1)
description: The brother of Mary and Martha of Bethany. He was raised from the dead after he had lain four days in the tomb (John 11:1-44).

name: Leah
description: Weary, the eldest daughter of Laban, and sister of Rachel (Gen. 29:16). Jacob took her to wife through a deceit of her father (Gen. 29:23).

name: Lebbaeus
title: Lebbaeus Thaddaeus
description: Breast, the name of one of the apostles (Mark 3:18), called “Lebbaeus” in Matt. 10:3, and in Luke 6:16, “Judas the brother of James;” while John (14:22), probably referring to the same person, speaks of “Judas, not Iscariot.”

name: Lemuel
description: Dedicated to God, a king whom his mother instructed (Prov. 31:1-9). Nothing is certainly known concerning him. The rabbis identified him with Solomon.

name: Leummim
description: Peoples; nations, the last mentioned of the three sons of Dedan, and head of an Arabian tribe (Gen. 25:3).

name: Levi
title: Levi (patriarch)
description: The third son of Jacob by Leah. The origin of the name is found in Leah’s words (Gen. 29:34), “This time will my husband be joined [Heb. yillaveh] unto me.”

name: Levi
title: Levi (son of Simeon)
description: The father of Matthat, and son of Simeon, of the ancestors of Christ (Luke 3:29).

name: Lo-ammi
description: Not my people, a symbolical name given by God’s command to Hosea’s second son in token of Jehovah’s rejection of his people (Hos. 1:9, 10), his treatment of them as a foreign people. This Hebrew word is rendered by “not my people” in ver. 10; 2:23.

name: Lo-ruhamah
description: Not pitied, the name of the prophet Hosea’s first daughter, a type of Jehovah’s temporary rejection of his people (Hos. 1:6; 2:23).

name: Lois
description: The maternal grandmother of Timothy. She is commended by Paul for her faith (2 Tim. 1:5).

name: Lot
description: (Heb. goral, a “pebble”), a small stone used in casting lots (Num. 33:54; Jonah 1:7). The lot was always resorted to by the Hebrews with strictest reference to the interposition of God, and as a method of ascertaining the divine will (Prov. 16:33), and in serious cases of doubt (Esther 3:7).

name: Lotan
description: Coverer, one of the sons of Seir, the Horite (Gen. 36:20, 29).

name: Lucifer
description: Brilliant star, a title given to the king of Babylon (Isa. 14:12) to denote his glory.

name: Lucius
description: Of Cyrene, a Christian teacher at Antioch (Acts 13:1), and Paul’s kinsman (Rom. 16:21). His name is Latin, but his birthplace seems to indicate that he was one of the Jews of Cyrene, in North Africa.

name: Lud
description: The fourth son of Shem (Gen. 10:22; 1 Chr. 1:17), ancestor of the Lydians probably.

name: Ludim
description: Probably the same as Lud (2) (comp. Gen. 10:13; 1 Chr. 1:11). They are associated (Jer. 46:9) with African nations as mercenaries of the king of Egypt.

name: Luke
description: The evangelist, was a Gentile. The date and circumstances of his conversion are unknown. According to his own statement (Luke 1:2), he was not an “eye-witness and minister of the word from the beginning.”

name: Lydia
description: A woman of Thyatira, a “seller of purple,” who dwelt in Philippi (Acts 16:14, 15). She was not a Jewess but a proselyte.

name: Lysanias
description: Tetrarch of Abilene (Luke 3:1), on the eastern slope of Anti-Lebanon, near the city of Damascus.

name: Maacah
description: A daughter of Talmai, king of the old native population of Geshur. She became one of David’s wives, and was the mother of Absalom (2 Sam. 3:3).

name: Maachah
title: Maachah (daughter of Uriel)
description: The daughter of Abishalom (called Absalom, 2 Chr. 11:20-22), the third wife of Rehoboam, and mother of Abijam (1 Kings 15:2).

name: Maachah
title: Maachah (father of Hanan)
description: The father of Hanan, who was one of David’s body-guard (1 Chr. 11:43).

name: Maachah
title: Maachah (father of Achish)
description: The father of Achish, the king of Gath (1 Kings 2:39), called also Maoch (1 Sam. 27:2).

name: Maaseiah
title: Maaseiah (1 Chronicles 15:18)
description: One of the Levites whom David appointed as porter for the ark (1 Chr. 15:18, 20).

name: Maaseiah
title: Maaseiah (son of Adaiah)
description: One of the “captains of hundreds” associated with Jehoiada in restoring king Jehoash to the throne (2 Chr. 23:1).

name: Maaseiah
title: Maaseiah (2 Chronicles 34:8)
description: One who was sent by king Josiah to repair the temple (2 Chr. 34:8). He was governor (Heb. sar, rendered elsewhere in the Authorized Version “prince,” “chief captain,” chief ruler”) of Jerusalem.

name: Maaseiah
title: Maaseiah (father of Zephaniah)
