description: The father of the priest Zephaniah (Jer. 21:1; 37:3).

name: Maasiai
description: Work of Jehovah, one of the priests resident at Jerusalem at the Captivity (1 Chr. 9:12).

name: Maath
description: Small, a person named in our Lord’s ancestry (Luke 3:26).

name: Maaziah
description: The head of the twenty-fourth priestly course (1 Chr. 24:18) in David’s reign.

name: Machir
description: Manasseh’s oldest son (Josh. 17:1), or probably his only son (see 1 Chr. 7:14, 15; comp. Num. 26:29-33; Josh. 13:31). His descendants are referred to under the name of Machirites, being the offspring of Gilead (Num. 26:29).

name: Machir
title: Machir (son of Ammiel)
description: A descendant of the preceding, residing at Lo-debar, where he maintained Jonathan’s son Mephibosheth till he was taken under the care of David (2 Sam. 9:4), and where he afterwards gave shelter to David himself when he was a fugitive (17:27).

name: Madai
description: Middle land, the third “son” of Japheth (Gen. 10:2), the name by which the Medes are known on the Assyrian monuments.

name: Magog
description: Region of Gog, the second of the “sons” of Japheth (Gen. 10:2; 1 Chr. 1:5). In Ezekiel (38:2; 39:6) it is the name of a nation, probably some Scythian or Tartar tribe descended from Japheth.

name: Mahalaleel
title: Mahalaleel (line of Seth)
description: The son of Cainan, of the line of Seth (Gen. 5:12-17); called Maleleel (Luke 3:37).

name: Mahalaleel
description: A descendant of Perez.

name: Mahalath
description: The daughter of Jerimoth, who was one of David’s sons. She was one of Rehoboam’s wives (2 Chr. 11:18).

name: Mahath
title: Mahath (son of Amasai, 1 Chronicles 6:25)
description: A Kohathite Levite, father of Elkanah (1 Chr. 6:35).

name: Mahath
title: Mahath (son of Amasai, 2 Chronicles 29:12)
description: Another Kohathite Levite, of the time of Hezekiah (2 Chr. 29:12).

name: Mahazioth
description: Visions, a Kohathite Levite, chief of the twenty-third course of musicians (1 Chr. 25:4, 30).

name: Maher-shalal-hash-baz
description: Plunder speedeth; spoil hasteth, (Isa. 8:1-3; comp. Zeph. 1:14), a name Isaiah was commanded first to write in large characters on a tablet, and afterwards to give as a symbolical name to a son that was to be born to him (Isa. 8:1, 3), as denoting the sudden attack on Damascus and Syria by the…

name: Mahlah
description: Disease, one of the five daughters of Zelophehad (Num. 27:1-11) who had their father’s inheritance, the law of inheritance having been altered in their favour.

name: Mahlon
description: Sickly, the elder of Elimelech the Bethlehemite’s two sons by Naomi. He married Ruth and died childless (Ruth 1:2, 5; 4:9, 10), in the land of Moab.

name: Mahol
description: Dance, the father of four sons (1 Kings 4:31) who were inferior in wisdom only to Solomon.

name: Malachi
description: Messenger or angel, the last of the minor prophets, and the writer of the last book of the Old Testament canon (Mal. 4:4, 5, 6).

name: Malcham
description: (2 Sam. 12:30, Heb., R.V., “their king;” Jer. 49:1, 3, R.V.; Zeph. 1:5), the national idol of the Ammonites. When Rabbah was taken by David, the crown of this idol was among the spoils.

name: Malchi-shua
description: King of help, one of the four sons of Saul (1 Chr. 8:33). He perished along with his father in the battle of Gilboa (1 Sam. 31:2).

name: Malchiah
title: Malchiah (Nehemiah 8:4)
description: A priest who stood by Ezra when he “read in the book of the law of God” (Neh. 8:4).

name: Malchijah
title: Malchijah (1 Chronicles 24:9)
description: The head of the fifth division of the priests in the time of David (1 Chr. 24:9).

name: Malchijah
title: Malchijah (Nehemiah 12:42)
description: One of the priests appointed as musicians to celebrate the completion of the walls of Jerusalem (Neh. 12:42).

name: Malchus
description: Reigning, the personal servant or slave of the high priest Caiaphas. He is mentioned only by John. Peter cut off his right ear in the garden of Gethsemane (John 18:10).

name: Mallothi
description: My fulness, a Kohathite Levite, one of the sons of Heman the Levite (1 Chr. 25:4), and chief of the nineteenth division of the temple musicians (26).

name: Malluch
title: Malluch (son of Hashabiah)
description: A Levite of the family of Merari (1 Chr. 6:44).

name: Malluch
title: Malluch (Nehemiah 10:4)
description: A priest who returned from Babylon (Neh. 12:2).

name: Mamre
description: An Amoritish chief in alliance with Abraham (Gen. 14:13, 24).

name: Manaen
description: Consoler, a Christian teacher at Antioch.

name: Manasseh
title: Manasseh (son of Joseph)
description: The elder of the two sons of Joseph. He and his brother Ephraim were afterwards adopted by Jacob as his own sons (48:1).

name: Manasseh
title: Manasseh (son of Hezekiah)
description: The elder of the two sons of Joseph. He and his brother Ephraim were afterwards adopted by Jacob as his own sons (48:1).

name: Manoah
description: Rest, a Danite, the father of Samson (Judg. 13:1-22, and 14:2-4).

name: John
title: John Mark
description: The evangelist; “John whose surname was Mark” (Acts 12:12, 25). Mark (Marcus, Col. 4:10, etc.) was his Roman name, which gradually came to supersede his Jewish name John.

name: Martha
description: Bitterness, the sister of Lazarus and Mary, and probably the eldest of the family, who all resided at Bethany (Luke 10:38, 40, 41; John 11:1-39).

name: Mary
title: Mary (Mother of Jesus)
description: The wife of Joseph, the mother of Jesus, called the “Virgin Mary,” though never so designated in Scripture (Matt. 2:11; Acts 1:14).

name: Mary
title: Mary (sister of Lazarus)
description: Mary the sister of Lazarus is brought to our notice in connection with the visits of our Lord to Bethany. She is contrasted with her sister Martha, who was “cumbered about many things” while Jesus was their guest, while Mary had chosen “the good part.”

name: Mary
title: Mary (Mother of John Mark)
description: Mary the mother of John Mark was one of the earliest of our Lord’s disciples. She was the sister of Barnabas (Col. 4:10), and joined with him in disposing of their land and giving the proceeds of the sale into the treasury of the Church (Acts 4:37; 12:12).

name: Mary
title: Mary (of Rome)
description: A Christian at Rome who treated Paul with special kindness (Rom. 16:6).

name: Mary
title: Mary Magdalene
description: A surname derived from Magdala, the place of her nativity, given to one of the Marys of the Gospels to distinguish her from the other Marys (Matt. 27:56, 61; 28:1, etc.).

name: Mash
description: (= Meshech 1 Chr. 1:17), one of the four sons of Aram, and the name of a tribe descended from him (Gen. 10:23) inhabiting some part probably of Mesopotamia. Some have supposed that they were the inhabitants of Mount Masius, the present Karja Baghlar, which forms part of the chain of Taurus.

name: Massa
description: A lifting up, gift, one of the sons of Ishmael, the founder of an Arabian tribe (Gen. 25:14); a nomad tribe inhabiting the Arabian desert toward Babylonia.

name: Mattan
title: Mattan (2 Kings 11:18)
description: A priest of Baal, slain before his altar during the reformation under Jehoiada (2 Kings 11:18).

name: Mattan
title: Mattan (father of Shephatiah)
description: The father of Shephatiah (Jer. 38:1).

name: Mattaniah
title: Mattaniah (son of Heman)
description: A Levite, son of Heman, the chief of the ninth class of temple singers (1 Chr. 25:4, 16).

name: Mattaniah
title: Mattaniah (2 Chronicles 29:13)
description: A Levite who assisted in purifying the temple at the reformation under Hezekiah (2 Chr. 29:13).

name: Mattathias
title: Mattathias (son of Amos)
description: The son of Amos, in the genealogy of our Lord (Luke 3:25).

name: Mattathias
title: Mattathias (son of Semei)
description: The son of Semei, in the same genealogy (Luke 3:26).

name: Matthan
description: The son of Eleazar, and father of Jacob, who was the father of Joseph, the husband of the Virgin Mary (Matt. 1:15).

name: Matthat
title: Matthat (son of Levi, Luke 3:24)
description: The son of Levi, and father of Heli (Luke 3:24).

name: Matthat
title: Matthat (son of Levi, Luke 3:29)
description: Son of another Levi (Luke 3:29).

name: Matthew
description: Gift of God, a common Jewish name after the Exile. He was the son of Alphaeus, and was a publican or tax-gatherer at Capernaum.

name: Matthias
description: Gift of God. Acts 1:23.

name: Mattithiah
title: Mattithiah (son of Shallum)
description: The eldest son of Shallum, of the family of Korah (1 Chr. 9:31).

name: Mattithiah
title: Mattithiah (son of Jeduthun)
description: One of the sons of Jeduthun (1 Chr. 25:3, 21).

name: Mattithiah
title: Mattithiah (Nehemiah 8:4)
description: One who stood by Ezra while reading the law (Neh. 8:4).

name: Medan
description: A son of Jokshan, Abraham’s son by Keturah (1 Chr. 1:32). His descendants settled on the Syrian borders about the territory of Edom.

name: Mehetabeel
description: Whose benefactor is God, the father of Delaiah, and grandfather of Shemaiah, who joined Sanballat against Nehemiah (Neh. 6:10).

name: Mehetabel
description: Wife of Hadad, one of the kings of Edom (Gen. 36:39).

name: Mehujael
description: Smitten by God, the son of Irad, and father of Methusael (Gen. 4:18).

name: Mehuman
description: Faithful, one of the eunchs whom Ahasuerus (Xerxes) commanded to bring in Vashti (Esther 1:10).

name: Mehunim
description: Habitations, (2 Chr. 26:7; R.V. “Meunim,” Vulg. Ammonitae), a people against whom Uzziah waged a successful war. This word is in Hebrew the plural of Ma’on, and thus denotes the Maonites who inhabited the country on the eastern side of the Wady el-Arabah.

name: Melchi
title: Melchi (son of Addi)
description: The son of Addi, and father of Neri (Luke 3:28).

name: Melchisedec
description: King of righteousness, the king of Salem (q.v.). All we know of him is recorded in Gen. 14:18-20. He is subsequently mentioned only once in the Old Testament, in Ps. 110:4.

name: Melea
description: Fulness, the son of Menan and father of Eliakim, in the genealogy of our Lord (Luke 3:31).

name: Melech
description: King, the second of Micah’s four sons (1 Chr. 8:35), and thus grandson of Mephibosheth.

name: Melzar
description: Probably a Persian word meaning master of wine, i.e., chief butler; the title of an officer at the Babylonian court (Dan. 1:11, 16) who had charge of the diet of the Hebrew youths.

name: Memucan
description: Dignified, one of the royal counsellors at the court of Ahasuerus, by whose suggestion Vashti was divorced (Esther 1:14, 16, 21).

name: Menahem
description: Conforting, the son of Gadi, and successor of Shallum, king of Israel, whom he slew. After a reign of about ten years (B.C. 771-760) he died, leaving the throne to his son Pekahiah.

name: Mephibosheth
description: The son of Jonathan, and grandson of Saul (2 Sam. 4:4). He was but five years old when his father and grandfather fell on Mount Gilboa.

name: Mephibosheth
title: Mephibosheth (son of Saul)
description: The name of Saul’s son by the concubine Rizpah (q.v.), the daughter of Aiah. He and his brother Armoni were with five others “hanged on a hill before the Lord” by the Gibeonites, and their bodies exposed in the sun for five months (2 Sam. 21:8-10).

name: Merab
description: Increase, the eldest of Saul’s two daughters (1 Sam. 14:49). She was betrothed to David after his victory over Goliath, but does not seem to have entered heartily into this arrangement (18:2, 17, 19).

name: Meraiah
description: Resistance, a chief priest, a contemporary of the high priest Joiakim (Neh. 12:12).

name: Meraioth
description: Father of Amariah, a high priest of the line of Eleazar (1 Chr. 6:6, 7, 52).

name: Merari
description: Sad; bitter, the youngest son of Levi, born before the descent of Jacob into Egypt, and one of the seventy who accompanied him thither (Gen. 46:11; Ex. 6:16). He became the head of one of the great divisions of the Levites (Ex. 6:19).

name: Mered
description: Rebellion, one of the sons of Ezra, of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr. 4:17).

name: Meremoth
title: Meremoth (son of Urijah)
description: Exaltations, heights, a priest who returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel (Neh. 12:3), to whom were sent the sacred vessels (Ezra 8:33) belonging to the temple. He took part in rebuilding the walls of Jerusalem (Neh. 3:4).

name: Merodach-baladan
description: Merodach has given a son, (Isa. 39:1), “the hereditary chief of the Chaldeans, a small tribe at that time settled in the marshes at the mouth of the Euphrates, but in consequence of his conquest of Babylon afterwards, they became the dominant caste in Babylonia itself.”

name: Mesha
title: Mesha (2 Kings 3:4)
description: Heb. id, a king of Moab, the son of Chemosh-Gad, a man of great wealth in flocks and herds (2 Kings 3:4).

name: Mesha
title: Mesha (son of Caleb)
description: Heb. meysh’a, “deliverance,” the eldest son of Caleb (1 Chr. 2:42), and brother of Jerahmeel.

name: Meshach
description: One of the three Hebrew youths who were trained with Daniel in Babylon (Dan. 1:11, 19), and promoted to the rank of Magi.

name: Meshech
description: Drawing out, the sixth son of Japheth (Gen. 10:2), the founder of a tribe (1 Chr. 1:5; Ezek. 27:13; 38:2, 3). They were in all probability the Moschi, a people inhabiting the Moschian Mountains, between the Black and the Caspian Seas.

name: Meshelemiah
description: Friendship of Jehovah, a Levite of the family of the Korhites, called also Shelemiah (1 Chr. 9:21; 26:1, 2, 9, 14). He was a temple gate-keeper in the time of David.

name: Meshillemith
description: A priest, the son of Immer (Neh. 11:13).

name: Meshillemoth
description: The father of Berechiah (2 Chr. 28:12).

name: Meshullam
title: Meshullam (father of Azaliah)
description: Grandfather of Shaphan, “the scribe,” in the reign of Josiah (2 Kings 22:3).

name: Meshullam
title: Meshullam (son of Abihail)
description: One of the chief Gadites in Bashan in the time of Jotham (1 Chr. 5:13).

name: Meshullam
title: Meshullam (Nehemiah 8:4)
description: One of the principal Israelites who supported Ezra when expounding the law to the people (Neh. 8:4).

name: Meshullam
title: Meshullam (Nehemiah 12:16)
description: A chief priest (Neh. 12:16).

name: Meshullemeth
description: Friend, the wife of Manasseh, and the mother of Amon (2 Kings 21:19), Kings of Judah.

name: Methusael
description: Champion of El; man of God, a descendant of Cain (Gen. 4:18), so called, perhaps, to denote that even among the descendants of Cain God had not left himself without a witness.

name: Methuselah
description: Man of the dart, the son of Enoch, and grandfather of Noah. He was the oldest man of whom we have any record, dying at the age of nine hundred and sixty-nine years, in the year of the Flood (Gen. 5:21-27; 1 Chr. 1:3).

name: Mezahab
description: Water of gold, the father of Matred (Gen. 36:39; 1 Chr. 1:50), and grandfather of Mehetabel, wife of Hadar, the last king of Edom.

name: Mibhar
description: Choice, a Hagarene, one of David’s warriors (1 Chr. 11:38); called also Bani the Gadite (2 Sam. 23:36).

name: Mibsam
title: Mibsam (son of Ishmael)
description: One of Ishmael’s twelve sons, and head of an Arab tribe (Gen. 25:13).

name: Mibsam
title: Mibsam (son of Shallum)
description: A son of Simeon (1 Chr. 4:25).

name: Mibzar
description: Fortress, one of the Edomitish “dukes” descended from Esau (Gen. 36:42; 1 Chr. 1:53).

name: Micah
title: Micah (Judges 17:1)
description: A man of Mount Ephraim, whose history so far is introduced in Judg. 17, apparently for the purpose of leading to an account of the settlement of the tribe of Dan in Northern Palestine, and for the purpose also of illustrating the lawlessness of the times in which he lived (Judg. 18; 19:1-29; 21:25).

name: Micah
title: Micah (son of Shimei)
description: A descendant of Joel the Reubenite (1 Chr. 5:5).

name: Micah
title: Micah (Jeremiah 26:18)
description: “The Morasthite,” so called to distinguish him from Micaiah, the son of Imlah (1 Kings 22:8). He was a prophet of Judah, a contemporary of Isaiah (Micah 1:1), a native of Moresheth of Gath (1:14, 15).

name: Micah
title: Micah (son of Mephibosheth)
description: The son of Merib-baal (Mephibosheth), 1 Chr. 8:34, 35.

name: Micaiah
description: Who is like Jehovah?, the son of Imlah, a faithful prophet of Samaria (1 Kings 22:8-28). Three years after the great battle with Ben-hadad (20:29-34), Ahab proposed to Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, that they should go up against Ramoth-Gilead to do battle again with Ben-hadad.

name: Micha
title: Micha (son of Zichri)
description: The son of Zabdi, a Levite of the family of Asaph (Neh. 11:17, 22).

name: Michael
title: Michael (father of Sethur)
description: The father of Sethur, the spy selected to represent Asher (Num. 13:13).

name: Michael
title: Michael (son of Abihail)
description: A chief Gadite in Bashan (1 Chr. 5:13).

name: Michael
title: Michael (son of Baaseiah)
description: A Gershonite Levite (1 Chr. 6:40).

name: Michael
title: Michael (son of Izrahiah)
description: A chief of the tribe of Issachar.

name: Michael
title: Michael (1 Chronicles 12:20)
description: A Manassite, “a captain of thousands” who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:20).

name: Michael
title: Michael (father of Omri)
description: The father of Omri (1 Chr. 27:18).

name: Michael
title: Michael (son of Jehoshaphat)
description: One of the sons of king Jehoshaphat (2 Chr. 21:2, 4). He was murdered by his brother Jehoram.

name: Michael
title: Michael (Daniel 10:13)
description: The title given to one of the chief angels (Dan. 10:13, 21; 12:1). He had special charge of Israel as a nation. He disputed with Satan (Jude 1:9) about the body of Moses.

name: Michah
description: The first in rank of the priests of the family of Kohathites (1 Chr. 23:20).

name: Michaiah
title: Michaiah (2 Chronicles 17:7)
description: One of those sent out by Jehoshaphat to instruct the people in the law (2 Chr. 17:7).

name: Michaiah
title: Michaiah (son of Gemariah)
description: The son of Gemariah. He reported to the king’s officers Jeremiah’s prediction, which he had heard Baruch read (Jer. 36:11, 13) from his father Gemariah’s chamber in the temple.

name: Michal
description: Rivulet, or who as God?, the younger of Saul’s two daughters by his wife Ahinoam (1 Sam. 14:49, 50). “Attracted by the graces of his person and the gallantry of his conduct, she fell in love with David and became his wife” (18:20-28).

name: Michri
description: Prize of Jehovah, a Benjamite, the father of Uzzi (1 Chr. 9:8).

name: Midian
description: Strife, the fourth son of Abraham by Keturah, the father of the Midianites (Gen. 25:2; 1 Chr. 1:32).

name: Mikloth
title: Mikloth (1 Chronicles 27:4)
description: An officer under Dodai, in the time of David and Solomon (1 Chr. 27:4).

name: Milalai
description: Eloquent, a Levitical musician (Neh. 12:36) who took part in the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem.

name: Miniamin
title: Miniamin (Nehemiah 10:7)
description: A chief priest who returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel (Neh. 12:5), called Mijamin (10:7) and Miniamin (12:17).

name: Miriam
description: The sister of Moses and Aaron (Ex. 2:4-10; 1 Chr. 6:3). Her name is prominent in the history of the Exodus. She is called “the prophetess” (Ex. 15:20).

name: Miriam
title: Miriam (daughter of Mered)
description: One of the descendants of Judah.

name: Mishael
title: Mishael (son of Uzziel)
description: A Levite; the eldest of the three sons of Uzziel (Ex. 6:22).

name: Misham
description: Their cleansing or their beholding, a Benjamite, one of the sons of Elpaal (1 Chr. 8:12).

name: Mishma
title: Mishma (son of Ishmael)
description: One of the sons of Ishmael (Gen. 25:14), and founder of an Arab tribe.

name: Mishmannah
description: Fatness, one of the Gadite heroes who gathered to David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:10).

name: Mispereth
description: Number, one of the Jews who accompanied Zerubbabel from Babylon (Ezra 2:2); called also Mispereth (Neh. 7:7).

name: Mithredath
title: Mithredath (Ezra 1:8)
description: The “treasurer” of King Cyrus (Ezra 1:8).

name: Mizraim
description: The dual form of matzor, meaning a “mound” or “fortress,” the name of a people descended from Ham (Gen. 10:6, 13; 1 Chr. 1:8, 11).

name: Mnason
description: Reminding, or remembrancer, a Christian of Jerusalem with whom Paul lodged (Acts 21:16). He was apparently a native of Cyprus, like Barnabas (11:19, 20), and was well known to the Christians of Caesarea (4:36).

name: Moab
description: Used to denote the people of Moab (Num. 22:3-14; Judg. 3:30; 2 Sam. 8:2; Jer. 48:11, 13).

name: Molech
description: King, the name of the national god of the Ammonites, to whom children were sacrificed by fire. He was the consuming and destroying and also at the same time the purifying fire.

name: Mordecai
description: The son of Jair, of the tribe of Benjamin. It has been alleged that he was carried into captivity with Jeconiah, and hence that he must have been at least one hundred and twenty-nine years old in the twelfth year of Ahasuerus (Xerxes).

name: Moses
description: Drawn (or Egypt. mesu, “son;” hence Rameses, royal son). On the invitation of Pharaoh (Gen. 45:17-25), Jacob and his sons went down into Egypt. This immigration took place probably about 350 years before the birth of Moses.

name: Mother of the Wife of Simon
Moza
title: Moza (son of Caleb)
description: One of the sons of Caleb (1 Chr. 2:46).

name: Moza
title: Moza (son of Zimri)
description: The son of Zimri, of the posterity of Saul (1 Chr. 8:36, 37; 9:42, 43).

name: Mushi
description: Receding, the second of the two sons of Merari (Ex. 6:19; Num. 3:20). His sons were called Mushites (Num. 3:33; 26:58).

name: Naam
description: Pleasantness, one of the three sons of Caleb, the son of Jephunneh (1 Chr. 4:15).

name: Naamah
title: Naamah (line of Cain)
description: The daughter of Lamech and Zillah (Gen. 4: 22).

name: Naamah
description: The daughter of the king of Ammon, one of the wives of Solomon, the only one who appears to have borne him a son, viz., Rehoboam (1 Kings 14:21, 31).

name: Naaman
description: Pleasantness, a Syrian, the commander of the armies of Benhadad II. in the time of Joram, king of Israel.

name: Naarah
description: A girl, the second of Ashur’s two wives, of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr. 4:5, 6).

name: Naarai
description: Youthful, a military chief in David’s army (1 Chr. 11:37), called also Paarai (2 Sam. 23:35).

name: Nabal
description: Foolish, a descendant of Caleb who dwelt at Maon (1 Sam. 25), the modern Main, 7 miles south-east of Hebron. He was “very great, and he had 3,000 sheep and 1,000 goats...but the man was churlish and evil in his doings.”

name: Naboth
description: Fruits, “the Jezreelite,” was the owner of a portion of ground on the eastern slope of the hill of Jezreel (2 Kings 9:25, 26).

name: Nadab
description: The eldest of Aaron’s four sons (Ex. 6:23; Num. 3:2). He with his brothers and their father were consecrated as priests of Jehovah (Ex. 28:1).

name: Nadab
title: Nadab (son of Jeroboam)
description: The son and successor of Jeroboam, the king of Israel (1 Kings 14:20). While engaged with all Israel in laying siege to Gibbethon, a town of southern Dan (Josh. 19:44), a conspiracy broke out in his army, and he was slain by Baasha (1 Kings 15:25-28), after a reign of two years (B.C. 955-953).

name: Nadab
title: Nadab (son of Shammai)
description: One of the sons of Shammai in the tribe of Judah (1 Chr. 2:28, 30).

name: Naharai
description: Snorer, a Berothite, one of David’s heroes, and armour-bearer of Joab (1 Chr. 11:39).

name: Nahash
title: Nahash (1 Samuel 11:1)
description: King of the Ammonites in the time of Saul. The inhabitants of Jabesh-Gilead having been exposed to great danger from Nahash, sent messengers to Gibeah to inform Saul of their extremity.

name: Nahash
title: Nahash (father of Zeruiah)
description: The father of Amasa, who was commander-in-chief of Abasolom’s army (2 Sam. 17:25). Jesse’s wife had apparently been first married to this man, to whom she bore Abigail and Zeruiah, who were thus David’s sisters, but only on the mother’s side (1 Chr. 2:16).

name: Nahath
title: Nahath (2 Chronicles 31:13)
description: A Levite, one of the overseers of the sacred offerings of the temple (2 Chr. 31:13).

name: Nahath
title: Nahath (son of Reuel)
description: One of the four sons of Reuel, the son of Esau (Gen. 36:13, 17).

name: Nahath
title: Nahath (son of Zuph)
description: A Kohathite Levite (1 Chr. 6:26).

name: Nahbi
description: Hidden, one of the twelve spies sent out to explore the land of Canaan (Num. 13:14).

name: Nahor
title: Nahor (father of Terah)
description: The father of Terah, who was the father of Abraham (Gen. 11:22-25; Luke 3:34).

name: Nahor
title: Nahor (brother of Abraham)
description: A son of Terah, and elder brother of Abraham (Gen. 11:26, 27; Josh. 24:2, R.V.). He married Milcah, the daughter of his brother Haran, and remained in the land of his nativity on the east of the river Euphrates at Haran (Gen. 11:27-32).

name: Nahshon
description: Sorcerer, the son of Aminadab, and prince of the children of Judah at the time of the first numbering of the tribes in the wilderness (Ex. 6:23).

name: Naomi
description: Bitter; sad, a symbolical name which Naomi gave to herself because of her misfortunes (Ruth 1:20).

name: Naphtali
description: My wrestling, the fifth son of Jacob. His mother was Bilhah, Rachel’s handmaid (Gen. 30:8). When Jacob went down into Egypt, Naphtali had four sons (Gen. 46:24).

name: Naphtuhim
description: A Hamitic tribe descended from Mizraim (Gen. 10:13). Others identify this word with Napata, the name of the city and territory on the southern frontier of Mizraim, the modern Meroe, at the great bend of the Nile at Soudan.

name: Narcissus
description: Daffodil, a Roman whom Paul salutes (Rom. 16:11). He is supposed to have been the private secretary of the emperor Claudius.

name: Nathan
title: Nathan (son of David)
description: A son of David, by Bathsheba (2 Sam. 5:14), whose name appears in the genealogy of Mary, the mother of our Lord (Luke 3:31).

name: Nathan
description: A prophet in the reigns of David and Solomon (2 Chr. 9:29). He is first spoken of in connection with the arrangements David made for the building of the temple (2 Sam. 7:2, 3, 17), and next appears as the reprover of David on account of his sin with Bathsheba (12:1-14).

name: Nathan
title: Nathan (son of Attai)
description: A prophet in the reigns of David and Solomon (2 Chr. 9:29). He is first spoken of in connection with the arrangements David made for the building of the temple (2 Sam. 7:2, 3, 17), and next appears as the reprover of David on account of his sin with Bathsheba (12:1-14).

name: Nathanael
description: Given or gift of God, one of our Lord’s disciples, “of Cana in Galilee” (John 21:2). He was “an Israelite indeed, in whom was no guile” (1:47, 48).

name: Nebajoth
description: Ishmael’s eldest son (Gen. 25:13), and the prince of an Israelitish tribe (16). He had a sister, Mahalath, who was one of Esau’s wives (Gen. 28:9; 36:3).

name: Nebat
description: Sight; aspect, the father of Jeroboam, the king of Israel (1 Kings 11:26, etc.).

name: Nebuchadnezzar
description: In the Babylonian orthography Nabu-kudur-uzur, which means “Nebo, protect the crown!” or the “frontiers.” In an inscription he styles himself “Nebo’s favourite.”

name: Nebushasban
description: Adorer of Nebo, or Nebo saves me, the “Rabsaris,” or chief chamberlain, of the court of Babylon. He was one of those whom the king sent to release Jeremiah from prison in Jerusalem (Jer. 39:13).

name: Nebuzar-adan
description: “the captain of the guard,” in rank next to the king, who appears prominent in directing affairs at the capture of Jerusalem (2 Kings 25:8-20; Jer. 39:11; 40:2-5).

name: Nedabiah
description: Moved of Jehovah, one of the sons of Jeconiah (1 Chr. 3:18).

name: Nehemiah
title: Nehemiah (son of Hachaliah)
description: The son of Hachaliah (Neh. 1:1), and probably of the tribe of Judah. His family must have belonged to Jerusalem (Neh. 2:3).

name: Nehushta
description: Copper, the daughter of Elnathan of Jerusalem, and the wife of Jehoiakin (2 Kings 24:8), king of Judah.

name: Nemuel
description: A Reubenite, a son of Eliab, and brother of Dathan and Abiram (Num. 26:9).

name: Ner
description: Light, the father of Kish (1 Chr. 8:33). 1 Sam. 14:51 should be read, “Kish, the father of Saul, and Ner, the father of Abner, were the sons of Abiel.” And hence this Kish and Ner were brothers, and Saul and Abner were first cousins (comp. 1 Chr. 9:36).

name: Nergal-sharezer
description: Another of the “princes,” who bore the title of “Rabmag.” He was one of those who were sent to release Jeremiah from prison (Jer. 39:13) by “the captain of the guard.”

name: Nethaneel
title: Nethaneel (son of Zuar)
description: The son of Zuar, chief of the tribe of Issachar at the Exodus (Num. 1:8; 2:5).

name: Nethaneel
title: Nethaneel (son of Jesse)
description: One of David’s brothers (1 Chr. 2:14).

name: Nethaneel
title: Nethaneel (1 Chronicles 15:24)
description: A priest who blew the trumpet before the ark when it was brought up to Jerusalem (1 Chr. 15:24).

name: Nethaneel
title: Nethaneel (son of Shimei)
description: A temple porter, of the family of the Korhites (1 Chr. 26:4).

name: Nethaneel
title: Nethaneel (2 Chronicles 17:7)
description: One of the “princes” appointed by Jehoshaphat to teach the law through the cities of Judah (2 Chr. 17:7).

name: Nethaneel
title: Nethaneel (2 Chronicles 35:9)
description: A chief Levite in the time of Josiah (2 Chr. 35:9).

name: Nethaneel
title: Nethaneel (son of Jonathan)
description: A priest’s son who bore a trumpet at the dedication of the walls of Jerusalem (Neh. 12:36).

name: Nethaniah
title: Nethaniah (2 Chronicles 17:8)
description: A Levite sent by Jehoshaphat to teach the law (2 Chr. 17:8).

name: Neziah
description: Victory; pure, Ezra 2:54; Neh. 7:56.

name: Nicanor
description: Conqueror, one of the seven deacons appointed in the apostolic Church (Acts 6:1-6). Nothing further is known of him.

name: Nicodemus
description: The people is victor, a Pharisee and a member of the Sanhedrin. He is first noticed as visiting Jesus by night (John 3:1-21) for the purpose of learning more of his doctrines, which our Lord then unfolded to him, giving prominence to the necessity of being “born again.”

name: Nicolas
description: The victory of the people, a proselyte of Antioch, one of the seven deacons (Acts 6:5).

name: Nimrod
description: Firm, a descendant of Cush, the son of Ham. He was the first who claimed to be a “mighty one in the earth.” Babel was the beginning of his kingdom, which he gradually enlarged (Gen. 10:8-10).

name: Nimshi
description: Saved. Jehu was “the son of Jehoshaphat, the son of Nimshi” (2 Kings 9:2; comp. 1 Kings 19:16).

name: Noadiah
title: Noadiah (son of Binnui)
description: A Levite who returned from Babylon (Ezra 8:33).

name: Noadiah
title: Noadiah (Nehemiah 6:14)
description: A false prophetess who assisted Tobiah and Sanballat against the Jews (Neh. 6:14). Being bribed by them, she tried to stir up discontent among the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and so to embarrass Nehemiah in his great work of rebuilding the ruined walls of the city.

name: Noah
description: Rest, (Heb. Noah) the grandson of Methuselah (Gen. 5:25-29), who was for two hundred and fifty years contemporary with Adam, and the son of Lamech, who was about fifty years old at the time of Adam’s death.

name: Noah
title: Noah (daughter of Zelophehad)
description: Rest, (Heb. Noah) the grandson of Methuselah (Gen. 5:25-29), who was for two hundred and fifty years contemporary with Adam, and the son of Lamech, who was about fifty years old at the time of Adam’s death.

name: Nogah
description: Splendour, one of David’s sons, born at Jerusalem (1 Chr. 3:7).

name: Nun
description: Beyond the fact that he was the father of Joshua nothing more is known of him (Ex. 33:11).

name: Obadiah
title: Obadiah (1 Kings 18:3)
description: An Israelite who was chief in the household of King Ahab (1 Kings 18:3). Amid great spiritual degeneracy he maintained his fidelity to God, and interposed to protect The Lord’s prophets, an hundred of whom he hid at great personal risk in a cave (4, 13).

name: Obadiah
title: Obadiah (son of Izrahiah)
description: A chief of the tribe of Issachar (1 Chr. 7:3).

name: Obadiah
title: Obadiah (son of Azel)
description: A descendant of Saul (1 Chr. 8:38).

name: Obadiah
title: Obadiah (son of Shemaiah)
description: A Levite, after the Captivity (1 Chr. 9:16).

name: Obadiah
title: Obadiah (1 Chronicles 12:9)
description: A Gadite who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:9).

name: Obadiah
title: Obadiah (father of Ishmaiah)
description: A prince of Zebulun in the time of David (1 Chr. 27:19).

name: Obadiah
title: Obadiah (2 Chronicles 17:7)
description: One of the princes sent by Jehoshaphat to instruct the people in the law (2 Chr. 17:7).

name: Obadiah
title: Obadiah (2 Chronicles 34:12)
description: A Levite who superintended the repairs of the temple under Josiah (2 Chr. 34:12).

name: Obadiah
title: Obadiah (son of Jehiel)
description: One who accompanied Ezra on the return from Babylon (Ezra 8:9).

name: Obed
title: Obed (son of Boaz)
description: A son of Boaz and Ruth (Ruth 4:21, 22), and the grandfather of David (Matt. 1:5).

name: Obil
description: A keeper of camels, an Ishmaelite who was “over the camels” in the time of David (1 Chr. 27:30).

name: Oded
title: Oded (2 Chronicles 28:9)
description: A prophet in the time of Ahaz and Pekah (2 Chr. 28:9-15).

name: Og
description: Gigantic, the king of Bashan, who was defeated by Moses in a pitched battle at Edrei, and was slain along with his sons (Deut. 1:4), and whose kingdom was given to the tribes of Reuben and Gad and half the tribe of Manasseh (Num. 21:32-35; Deut. 3:1-13).

name: Ohad
description: United, or power, the third son of Simeon (Gen. 46:10).

name: Ohel
description: A house; tent, the fourth son of Zerubbabel (1 Chr. 3:20).

name: Olympas
description: A Roman Christian whom Paul salutes (Rom. 16:15).

name: Omar
description: Eloquent, the son of Eliphaz, who was Esau’s eldest son (Gen. 36:11-15).

name: Omri
description: Servant of Jehovah. When Elah was murdered by Zimri at Tirzah (1 Kings 16:15-27), Omri, his captain, was made king (B.C. 931).

name: Onan
description: Strong, the second son of Judah (Gen. 38:4-10; comp. Deut. 25:5; Matt. 22:24). He died before the going down of Jacob and his family into Egypt.

name: Onesimus
description: Useful, a slave who, after robbing his master Philemon (q.v.) at Colosse, fled to Rome, where he was converted by the apostle Paul, who sent him back to his master with the epistle which bears his name.

name: Onesiphorus
description: Bringing profit, an Ephesian Christian who showed great kindness to Paul at Rome. He served him in many things, and had oft refreshed him.

name: Ophir
description: One of the sons of Joktan (Gen. 10:29).

name: Oreb
description: Raven, a prince of Midian, who, being defeated by Gideon and put to straits, was slain along with Zeeb (Judg. 7:20-25). Many of the Midianites perished along with him (Ps. 83:9; Isa. 10:26).

name: Oren
description: Ash or pine, the son of Jerahmeel (1 Chr. 2:25).

name: Ornan
description: Agile; also called Ornan 1 Chr. 21:15, a Jebusite who dwelt in Jerusalem before it was taken by the Israelites.

name: Orpah
description: Forelock or fawn, a Moabitess, the wife of Chilion (Ruth 1:4; 4:10). On the death of her husband she accompanied Naomi, her mother-in-law, part of the way to Bethlehem, and then returned to Moab.

name: Othni
description: A lion of Jehovah, a son of Shemaiah, and one of the temple porters in the time of David (1 Chr. 26:7). He was a “mighty man of valour.”

name: Othniel
description: Lion of God, the first of the judges. His wife Achsah was the daughter of Caleb (Josh. 15:16, 17; Judg. 1:13). He gained her hand as a reward for his bravery in leading a successful expedition against Debir (q.v.).

name: Ozem
title: Ozem (son of Jesse)
description: One of David’s brothers; the sixth son of Jesse (1 Chr. 2:15).

name: Ozem
title: Ozem (son of Jerahmeel)
description: A son of Jerahmeel (1 Chr. 2:25).

name: Ozni
description: Hearing, one of the sons of Gad; also called Ezbon (Gen. 46:16; Num. 26:16).

name: Paarai
description: Opening of the Lord, “the Arbite,” one of David’s heroes (2 Sam. 23:35); called also Naarai, 1 Chr. 11:37.

name: Pagiel
description: God allots, a prince of the tribe of Asher (Num. 1:13), in the wilderness.

name: Pahath-moab
title: Pahath-moab (father of Jeshua)
description: Governor of Moab, a person whose descendants returned from the Captivity and assisted in rebuilding Jerusalem (Ezra 2:6; 8:4; 10:30).

name: Pallu
description: Separated, the second son of Reuben (1 Chr. 5:3); called Phallu, Gen. 46:9. He was the father of the Phalluites (Ex. 6:14; Num. 26:5, 8).

name: Palti
description: Deliverance from the Lord, one of the spies representing the tribe of Benjamin (Num. 13:9).

name: Paltiel
description: Deliverance of God, the prince of Issachar who assisted “to divide the land by inheritance” (Num. 34:26).

name: Parmashta
description: Strong-fisted, a son of Haman, slain in Shushan (Esther 9:9).

name: Parmenas
description: Constant, one of the seven “deacons” (Acts 6:5).

name: Parshandatha
description: An interpreter of the law, the eldest of Haman’s sons, slain in Shushan (Esther 9:7).

name: Paruah
description: Flourishing, the father of Jehoshaphat, appointed to provide monthly supplies for Solomon from the tribe of Issachar (1 Kings 4:17).

name: Pasach
description: Clearing, one of the sons of Japhlet, of the tribe of Asher (1 Chr. 7:33).

name: Patrobas
description: A Christian at Rome to whom Paul sent salutations (Rom. 16:14).

name: Paul
description: Saul (q.v.) was born about the same time as our Lord. His circumcision-name was Saul, and probably the name Paul was also given to him in infancy “for use in the Gentile world,” as “Saul” would be his Hebrew home-name.

name: Pedahel
description: Redeemed of God, the son of Ammihud, a prince of Naphtali (Num. 34:28).

name: Pedahzur
description: Rock of redemption, the father of Gamaliel and prince of Manasseh at the time of the Exodus (Num. 1:10; 2:20).

name: Pedaiah
title: Pedaiah (father of Zebudah)
description: The father of Zebudah, who was the wife of Josiah and mother of king Jehoiakim (2 Kings 23:36).

name: Pedaiah
title: Pedaiah (son of Jehoiachin)
description: The father of Zerubbabel (1 Chr. 3:17-19).

name: Pedaiah
title: Pedaiah (father of Joel)
description: The father of Joel, ruler of the half-tribe of Manasseh (1 Chr. 27:20).

name: Pekah
description: Open-eyed, the son of Remaliah a captain in the army of Pekahiah, king of Israel, whom he slew, with the aid of a band of Gileadites, and succeeded (B.C. 758) on the throne (2 Kings 15:25).

name: Pekahiah
description: The Lord opened his eyes, the son and successor of Menahem on the throne of Israel. He was murdered in the royal palace of Samaria by Pekah, one of the captains of his army (2 Kings 15:23-26), after a reign of two years (B.C. 761-759).

name: Pelaiah
title: Pelaiah (son of Elioenai)
description: One of David’s posterity (1 Chr. 3:24).

name: Pelaiah
title: Pelaiah (Nehemiah 8:7)
description: A Levite who expounded the law (Neh. 8:7).

name: Pelatiah
title: Pelatiah (son of Hananiah)
description: A son of Hananiah and grandson of Zerubbabel (1 Chr. 3:21).

name: Pelatiah
title: Pelatiah (son of Benaiah)
description: One of the twenty-five princes of the people against whom Ezekiel prophesied on account of their wicked counsel (Ezek. 11:1-13).

name: Peleg
description: Division, one of the sons of Eber; so called because “in his days was the earth divided” (Gen. 10:25). Possibly he may have lived at the time of the dispersion from Babel.

name: Pelet
title: Pelet (son of Jahdai)
description: A descendant of Judah (1 Chr. 2:47).

name: Pelet
title: Pelet (son of Azmaveth)
description: A Benjamite who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:3).

name: Peleth
title: Peleth (father of On)
description: A Reubenite whose son was one of the conspirators against Moses and Aaron (Num. 16:1).

name: Peleth
title: Peleth (son of Jonathan)
description: One of the sons of Jonathan (1 Chr. 2:33).

name: Perida
description: One whose descendants returned with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:55); called also Perida (Neh. 7:57).

name: Persis
description: A female Christian at Rome whom Paul salutes (Rom. 16:12). She is spoken of as “beloved,” and as having “laboured much in the Lord.”

name: Simon
title: Simon Peter
description: Originally called Simon (=Simeon, i.e., “hearing”), a very common Jewish name in the New Testament. He was the son of Jona (Matt. 16:17).

name: Pethahiah
title: Pethahiah (1 Chronicles 24:16)
description: The chief of one of the priestly courses (the nineteenth) in the time of David (1 Chr. 24:16).

name: Pethahiah
title: Pethahiah (son of Meshezabeel)
description: A descendant of Judah who had some office at the court of Persia (Neh. 11:24).

name: Pethuel
description: Vision of God, the father of Joel the prophet (Joel 1:1).

name: Peulthai
description: Wages of the Lord, one of the sons of Obed-edom, a Levite porter (1 Chr. 26:5).

name: Phaltiel
description: Deliverance of the Lord, the son of Laish of Gallim (1 Sam. 25:44)= Phaltiel (2 Sam. 3:15). Michal, David’s wife, was given to him.

name: Phanuel
description: Face of God, father of the prophetess Anna (q.v.), Luke 2:36.

name: Pharaoh
title: Pharaoh (during Abraham's Journey)
description: The Pharaoh who was on the throne when Abram went down into Egypt (Gen. 12:10-20) was probably one of the Hyksos, or “shepherd kings.”

name: Pharaoh
title: Pharaoh (of Joseph)
description: The Pharaoh of Joseph’s days (Gen. 41) was probably Apopi, or Apopis, the last of the Hyksos kings.

name: Pharaoh
title: Pharaoh (father of Daughter of Pharaoh, Exodus 1:11)
description: The “new king who knew not Joseph” (Ex. 1:8-22) has been generally supposed to have been Aahmes I., or Amosis, as he is called by Josephus.

name: Pharaoh
title: Pharaoh (of the Exodus)
description: The Pharaoh of the Exodus was probably Menephtah I., the fourteenth and eldest surviving son of Rameses II. He resided at Zoan, where he had the various interviews with Moses and Aaron recorded in the book of Exodus.

name: Pharaoh
title: Pharaoh (father of Daughter of Pharaoh, 1 Kings 3:1)
description: The Pharaoh of 1 Kings 11:18-22.

name: Pharaoh
title: Pharaoh (2 Kings 18:21)
description: Pharaoh, in whom Hezekiah put his trust in his war against Sennacherib (2 Kings 18:21).

name: Pharaoh
title: Pharaoh (father of Bithiah)
description: The Pharaoh of 1 Chr. 4:18.

name: Pharez
description: Pharez, (q.v.), breach, the son of Judah (Neh. 11:4). “The chief of all the captains of the host for the first month” in the reign of David was taken from his family (1 Chr. 27:3).

name: Phebe
description: A “deaconess of the church at Cenchrea,” the port of Corinth. She was probably the bearer of Paul’s epistle to the Romans.

name: Phichol
description: Great, the chief captain of the army of Abimelech, the Philistine king of Gerar. He entered into an alliance with Abraham with reference to a certain well which, from this circumstance, was called Beersheba (q.v.), “the well of the oath” (Gen. 21:22, 32; 26:26).

name: Philemon
description: An inhabitant of Colosse, and apparently a person of some note among the citizens (Col. 4:9; Philemon 1:2). He was brought to a knowledge of the gospel through the instrumentality of Paul (19), and held a prominent place in the Christian community for his piety and beneficence (4-7).

name: Philetus
description: Amiable, with Hymenaeus, at Ephesus, said that the “resurrection was past already” (2 Tim. 2:17, 18). This was a Gnostic heresy held by the Nicolaitanes.

name: Philip
title: Phillip the Apostle
description: One of the twelve apostles; a native of Bethsaida, “the city of Andrew and Peter” (John 1:44). He readily responded to the call of Jesus when first addressed to him (43), and forthwith brought Nathanael also to Jesus (45, 46).

name: Philip
title: Philip (son of Herod, Matthew 14:3)
description: Mentioned only in connection with the imprisonment of John the Baptist (Matt. 14:3; Mark 6:17; Luke 3:19). He was the son of Herod the Great, and the first husband of Herodias, and the father of Salome. (See HEROD PHILIP I.)

name: Philip
title: Phillip the Evangelist
description: One of the “seven” (Acts 6:5), called also “the evangelist” (21:8, 9). He was one of those who were “scattered abroad” by the persecution that arose on the death of Stephen.

name: Phinehas
title: Phinehas (Levite)
description: Son of Eleazar, the high priest (Ex. 6:25).

name: Phinehas
title: Phinehas (son of Eli)
description: One of the sons of Eli, the high priest (1 Sam. 1:3; 2:12). He and his brother Hophni were guilty of great crimes, for which destruction came on the house of Eli (31).

name: Phlegon
description: Burning, a Roman Christian to whom Paul sent salutations (Rom. 16:14).

name: Phut
description: One of the sons of Ham (Gen. 10:6).

name: Phygellus
description: Fugitive, a Christian of Asia, who “turned away” from Paul during his second imprisonment at Rome (2 Tim. 1:15). Nothing more is known of him.

name: Pontius
title: Pontius Pilate
description: Probably connected with the Roman family of the Pontii, and called “Pilate” from the Latin pileatus, i.e., “wearing the pileus”, which was the “cap or badge of a manumitted slave,” as indicating that he was a “freedman,” or the descendant of one.

name: Portius
title: Portius Festus
description: The successor of Felix (A.D. 60) as procurator of Judea (Acts 24:27). A few weeks after he had entered on his office the case of Paul, then a prisoner at Caesarea, was reported to him.

name: Potiphar
description: Dedicated to Ra; i.e., to the sun-god, the Egyptian to whom the Ishmaelites sold Joseph (Gen. 39:1).

name: Priscilla
description: The wife of Aquila (Acts 18:2), who is never mentioned without her. Her name sometimes takes the precedence of his (Rom. 16:3; 2 Tim. 4:19).

name: Puah
title: Puah (Exodus 1:15)
description: One of the two midwives who feared God, and refused to kill the Hebrew male children at their birth (Ex. 1:15-21).

name: Puah
title: Puah (son of Dodo)
description: A descendant of Issachar (Judg. 10:1).

name: Publius
description: “the chief man of the island” of Malta (Acts 28:7), who courteously entertained Paul and his shipwrecked companions for three days, till they found a more permanent place of residence; for they remained on the island for three months, till the stormy season had passed.

name: Pudens
description: Bashful, a Christian at Rome, who sent his greetings to Timothy (2 Tim. 4:21).

name: Quartus
description: Fourth, a Corinthian Christian who sent by Paul his salutations to friends at Rome (Rom. 16:23).

name: Raamah
description: One of the sons of Cush (Gen. 10:7).

name: Rabsaris
description: Chief of the Heads, one of the three officers whom Sennacherib sent from Lachish with a threatening message to Jerusalem (2 Kings 18:17; Jer. 39:3, 13).

name: Rabshakeh
description: Chief of the princes, the name given to the chief cup-bearer or the vizier of the Assyrian court; one of Sennacherib’s messengers to Hezekiah.

name: Rachab
description: Rahab, a name found in the genealogy of our Lord (Matt. 1:5).

name: Rachel
description: Ewe, “the daughter”, “the somewhat petulant, peevish, and self-willed though beautiful younger daughter” of Laban, and one of Jacob’s wives (Gen. 29:6, 28).

name: Rahab
description: Insolence; pride, a poetical name applied to Egypt in Ps. 87:4; 89:10; Isa. 51:9, as “the proud one.” Rahab, (Heb. Rahab; i.e., “broad,” “large”).

name: Raham
description: Merciful, one of the descendants of Caleb, the son of Hezron (1 Chr. 2:44).

name: Ram
title: Ram (son of Hezron)
description: The son of Hezron, and one of the ancestors of the royal line (Ruth 4:19). The margin of 1 Chr. 2:9, also Matt. 1:3, 4 and Luke 3:33, have “Aram.”

name: Ram
title: Ram (son of Jerahmeel)
description: One of the sons of Jerahmeel (1 Chr. 2:25, 27).

name: Ram
title: Ram (Job 32:2)
description: A person mentioned in Job 32:2 as founder of a clan to which Elihu belonged. The same as Aram of Gen. 22:21.

name: Rapha
description: A Benjamite, the son of Binea (1 Chr. 8:2, 37), a descendant of Saul.

name: Raphu
description: Healed, a Benjamite, whose son Palti was one of the twelve spies (Num. 13:9).

name: Reba
description: Fourth, one of the Midianite chiefs slain by the Israelites in the wilderness (Num. 31:8; Josh. 13:21).

name: Rebekah
description: A noose, the daughter of Bethuel, and the wife of Isaac (Gen. 22:23; 24:67). The circumstances under which Abraham’s “steward” found her at the “city of Nahor,” in Padan-aram, are narrated in Gen. 24-27.

name: Rechab
title: Rechab (son of Rimmon)
description: One of Ishbosheth’s “captains of bands” or leaders of predatory troops (2 Sam. 4:2).

name: Rechab
title: Rechab (father of Jonadab)
description: The father of Jehonadab, who was the father of the Rechabites (2 Kings 10:15, 23; Jer. 35:6-19).

name: Reelaiah
description: Thunder of the Lord, one of the princes who returned from the Exile (Neh. 7:7); called also Reelaiah (Ezra 2:2).

name: Regem-melech
description: Friend of the king, one of the two messengers sent by the exiled Jews to Jerusalem in the time of Darius (Zech. 7:2) to make inquiries at the temple.

name: Rehabiah
description: Enlargement of the Lord, the son of Eliezer, and grandson of Moses (1 Chr. 23:17; 24:21).

name: Rehob
title: Rehob (father of Hadarezer)
description: The father of Hadadezer, king of Tobah (2 Sam. 8:3, 12).

name: Rehoboam
description: He enlarges the people, the successor of Solomon on the throne, and apparently his only son. He was the son of Naamah “the Ammonitess,” some well-known Ammonitish princess (1 Kings 14:21; 2 Chr. 12:13).

name: Rehum
title: Rehum (Ezra 2:2)
description: One of “the children of the province” who returned from the Captivity (Ezra 2:2); the same as “Nehum” (Neh. 7:7).

name: Rehum
title: Rehum (Ezra 4:8)
description: The “chancellor” of Artaxerxes, who sought to stir him up against the Jews (Ezra 4:8-24) and prevent the rebuilding of the walls and the temple of Jerusalem.

name: Rei
description: Friendly, one who maintained true allegiance to king David (1 Kings 1:8) when Adonijah rebelled.

name: Rekem
title: Rekem (Numbers 31:8)
description: One of the five Midianite kings whom the Israelites destroyed (Num. 31:8).

name: Rekem
title: Rekem (son of Hebron)
description: One of the sons of Hebron (1 Chr. 2:43, 44).

name: Remaliah
description: Adorned by the Lord, the father of Pekah, who conspired successfully against Pekahiah (2 Kings 15:25, 27, 30, 32, 37; Isa. 7:1, 4, 5, 9; 8:6).

name: Rephael
description: Healed of God, one of Shemaiah’s sons. He and his brethren, on account of their “strength for service,” formed one of the divisions of the temple porters (1 Chr. 26:7, 8).

name: Reuben
description: Behold a son!, the eldest son of Jacob and Leah (Gen. 29:32). His sinful conduct, referred to in Gen. 35:22, brought down upon him his dying father’s malediction (48:4).

name: Reuel
title: Reuel (son of Esau)
description: A son of Esau and Bashemath (Gen. 36:4, 10; 1 Chr. 1:35).

name: Rezin
title: Rezin (2 Kings 15:37)
description: Firm; a prince, a king of Syria, who joined Pekah (q.v.) in an invasion of the kingdom of Judah (2 Kings 15:37; 16:5-9; Isa. 7:1-8).

name: Rezon
description: Prince, son of Eliadah. Abandoning the service of Hadadezer, the king of Zobah, on the occasion of his being defeated by David, he became the “captain over a band” of marauders, and took Damascus, and became king of Syria (1 Kings 11:23-25; 2 Sam. 8:3-8).

name: Rhesa
description: Affection, son of Zorobabel, mentioned in the genealogy of our Lord (Luke 3:27).

name: Rhoda
description: A rose, the damsel in the house of Mary, the mother of John Mark. She came to hearken when Peter knocked at the door of the gate (Acts 12:12-15).

name: Rimmon
description: A man of Beeroth (2 Sam. 4:2), one of the four Gibeonite cities. (See Josh. 9:17.)

name: Riphath
description: A crusher, Gomer’s second son (Gen. 10:3), supposed to have been the ancestor of the Paphlagonians.

name: Rizpah
description: Coal; hot stone, the daughter of Aiah, and one of Saul’s concubines. She was the mother of Armoni and Mephibosheth (2 Sam. 3:7; 21:8, 10, 11).

name: Romamti-ezer
description: Elevation of help, one of the sons of Heman, “the king’s seer in the words of God, to lift up the horn.” He was head of the “four-and-twentieth” course of singers (1 Chr. 25:4, 31).

name: Ruth
description: A friend, a Moabitess, the wife of Mahlon, whose father, Elimelech, had settled in the land of Moab. On the death of Elimelech and Mahlon, Naomi came with Ruth, her daughter-in-law, who refused to leave her, to Bethlehem, the old home from which Elimelech had migrated.

name: Sabtah
description: Rest, the third son of Cush (Gen. 10:7; 1 Chr. 1:9).

name: Sabtecha
description: The fifth son of Cush.

name: Sacar
description: A son of Obed-edom the Gittite, and a temple porter (1 Chr. 26:4).

name: Sadoc
description: Just, mentioned in the genealogy of our Lord (Matt. 1:14).

name: Salah
description: A shoot, a descendant of Arphaxed (Luke 3:35, 36); called also Shelah (1 Chr. 1:18, 24).

name: Salathiel
description: Whom I asked of God, the son of Jeconiah (Matt. 1:12; 1 Chr. 3:17); also called the son of Neri (Luke 3:27).

name: Salmon
description: Shady; or Zalmon (q.v.), a hill covered with dark forests, south of Shechem, from which Abimelech and his men gathered wood to burn that city (Judg. 9:48).

name: Salome
description: The wife of Zebedee and mother of James and John (Mat. 27:56), and probably the sister of Mary, the mother of our Lord (John 19:25).

name: Samgar-nebo
description: Be gracious, O Nebo! or a cup-bearer of Nebo, probably the title of Nergal-sharezer, one of the princes of Babylon (Jer. 39:3).

name: Samson
description: Of the sun, the son of Manoah, born at Zorah. The narrative of his life is given in Judg. 13-16. He was a “Nazarite unto God” from his birth, the first Nazarite mentioned in Scripture (Judg. 13:3-5; comp. Num. 6:1-21).

name: Samuel
description: Heard of God. The peculiar circumstances connected with his birth are recorded in 1 Sam. 1:20. Hannah, one of the two wives of Elkanah, who came up to Shiloh to worship before the Lord, earnestly prayed to God that she might become the mother of a son.

name: Sanballat
description: Held some place of authority in Samaria when Nehemiah went up to Jerusalem to rebuild its ruined walls. He vainly attempted to hinder this work (Neh. 2:10, 19; 4:1-12; 6).

name: Sapphira
description: Beautiful, the wife of Ananias (q.v.). She was a partner in his guilt and also in his punishment (Acts 5:1-11).

name: Sarah
description: Princess, the wife and at the same time the half-sister of Abraham (Gen. 11:29; 20:12). This name was given to her at the time that it was announced to Abraham that she should be the mother of the promised child.

name: Satan
description: Adversary; accuser. When used as a proper name, the Hebrew word so rendered has the article “the adversary” (Job 1:6-12; 2:1-7).

name: Saul
description: The son of Kish (probably his only son, and a child of prayer, “asked for”), of the tribe of Benjamin, the first king of the Jewish nation.

name: Sceva
description: An implement, a Jew, chief of the priests at Ephesus (Acts 19:13-16); i.e., the head of one of the twenty-four courses of the house of Levi.

name: Seba
description: One of the sons of Cush (Gen. 10:7).

name: Secundus
description: Second, a Christian of Thessalonica who accompanied Paul into Asia (Acts 20:4).

name: Segub
title: Segub (son of Hiel)
description: The youngest son of Hiel the Bethelite. His death is recorded in 1 Kings 16:34 (comp. Josh. 6:26).

name: Segub
title: Segub (son of Hezron)
description: A descendant of Judah (1 Chr. 2:21, 22).

name: Seir
description: A Horite; one of the “dukes” of Edom (Gen. 36:20-30).

name: Semei
description: Mentioned in the genealogy of our Lord (Luke 3:26).

name: Sennacherib
description: Sin (the god) sends many brothers, son of Sargon, whom he succeeded on the throne of Assyria (B.C. 705), in the 23rd year of Hezekiah.

name: Seorim
description: Barley, the chief of the forth priestly course (1 Chr. 24:8).

name: Serah
description: Abundance; princess, the daughter of Asher and grand-daughter of Jacob (Gen. 46:17); called also Sarah (Num. 26:46; R.V., “Serah”).

name: Seraiah
title: Seraiah (son of Azariah)
description: A ruler of the temple (Neh. 11:11).

name: Seraiah
title: Seraiah (son of Kenaz)
description: The father of Joab (1 Chr. 4:13, 14).

name: Seraiah
title: Seraiah (son of Asiel)
description: The grandfather of Jehu (1 Chr. 4:35).

name: Seraiah
title: Seraiah (Ezra 2:2)
description: A priest of the days of Jehoiakim (Neh. 12:1, 12).

name: Seraiah
title: Seraiah (son of Neriah)
description: The son of Neriah. When Zedekiah made a journey to Babylon to do homage to Nebuchadnezzar, Seraiah had charge of the royal gifts to be presented on that occasion.

name: Sered
description: Fear, one of the sons of Zebulun (Gen. 46:14).

name: Sergius
title: Sergius Paulus
description: A “prudent man” (R.V., “man of understanding”), the deputy (R.V., “proconsul”) of Cyprus (Acts 13:6-13). He became a convert to Christianity under Paul, who visited this island on his first mission to the heathen.

name: Serug
description: Branch, the father of Nahor (Gen. 11:20-23); called Saruch in Luke 3:35.

name: Seth
description: Appointed; a substitute, the third son of Adam and Eve (Gen. 4:25; 5:3). His mother gave him this name, “for God,” said she, “hath appointed me [i.e., compensated me with] another seed instead of Abel, whom Cain slew.”

name: Sethur
description: Hidden, one of the spies sent to search the Promised Land. He was of the tribe of Asher (Num. 13:13).

name: Shaashgaz
description: Servant of the beautiful, a chief eunuch in the second house of the harem of king Ahasuerus (Esther 2:14).

name: Shadrach
description: Aku’s command, the Chaldean name given to Hananiah, one of the Hebrew youths whom Nebuchadnezzar carried captive to Babylon (Dan. 1:6, 7; 3:12-30).

name: Shallum
title: Shallum (son of Jabesh)
description: The son of Jabesh, otherwise unknown. He “conspired against Zachariah, and smote him before the people, and slew him, and reigned in his stead” (2 Kings 15:10).

name: Shallum
title: Shallum (son of Tikvah)
description: Keeper of the temple vestments in the reign of Josiah (2 Kings 22:14).

name: Shallum
title: Shallum (son of Sisamai)
description: One of the posterity of Judah (1 Chr. 2:40, 41).

name: Shallum
title: Shallum (son of Shaul)
description: A descendant of Simeon (1 Chr. 4:25).

name: Shallum
title: Shallum (son of Kore)
description: A keeper of the gate in the reign of David (1 Chr. 9:17).

name: Shallum
title: Shallum (father of Jehizkiah)
description: An Ephraimite chief (2 Chr. 28:12).

name: Shallum
title: Shallum (father of Hanameel)
description: The uncle of the prophet Jeremiah (Jer. 32:7).

name: Shalmaneser
description: An Assyrian king (Hos. 10:14), identified with Shalmaneser II. (Sayce) or IV. (Lenormant), the successor of Pul on the throne of Assyria (B.C. 728).

name: Shamer
title: Shamer (son of Heber)
description: A man of Asher (1 Chr. 7:32); called also Shamer (34).

name: Shamgar
description: The Philistines from the maritime plain had made incursions into the Hebrew upland for the purposes of plunder, when one of this name, the son of Anath, otherwise unknown, headed a rising for the purpose of freeing the land from this oppression.

name: Shamir
description: One of the sons of Michah (1 Chr. 24:24).

name: Shammah
title: Shammah (son of Reuel)
description: One of the “dukes” of Edom (Gen. 36:13, 17).

name: Shammah
title: Shammah (son of Agee)
description: One of David’s three mighty men (2 Sam. 23:11, 12).

name: Shammah
title: Shammah (2 Samuel 23:25)
description: One of David’s mighties (2 Sam. 23:25); called also Shammoth (1 Chr. 11:27) and Shamhuth (27:8).

name: Shammah
title: Shammah (son of Jesse)
description: One of the sons of Jesse (1 Sam. 16:9). He is also called Shimeah (2 Sam. 13:3) and Shimma (1 Chr. 2:13).

name: Shammua
title: Shammua (son of Zaccur)
description: One of the spies sent out by Moses to search the land (Num. 13:4). He represented the tribe of Reuben.

name: Shammua
title: Shammua (son of David)
description: One of David’s sons by Bathsheba (1 Chr. 3:5); called also Shammua (14:4).

name: Shaphan
description: A coney, a scribe or secretary of king Josiah (2 Kings 22:3-7). He consulted Huldah concerning the newly-discovered copy of the law which was delivered to him by Hilkiah the priest (8-14).

name: Shaphat
title: Shaphat (son of Hori)
description: One of the spies. He represented the tribe of Simeon (Num. 13:5).

name: Shaphat
title: Shaphat (father of Elisha)
description: The father of Elisha (1 Kings 19:16-19).

name: Shaphat
title: Shaphat (son of Adlai)
description: One of David’s chief herdsmen (1 Chr. 27:29).

name: Sharar
description: One of David’s heroes (1 Chr. 11:35); called also Sharar (2 Sam. 23:33).

name: Sharezer
description: (god) protect the king!, a son of Sennacherib, king of Assyria. He and his brother Adrammelech murdered their father, and then fled into the land of Armenia (2 Kings 19:37).

name: Shaul
title: Shaul (Genesis 36:37)
description: A king of Edom (Gen. 36:37, 38); called Shaul in 1 Chr. 1:48.

name: Shavsha
description: (“Seraiah,” 2 Sam. 8:17; “Shisha,” 1 Kings 4:3), one of David’s secretaries (1 Chr. 18:16).

name: Shealtiel
description: Asked for of God, father of Zerubbabel (Ezra 3:2, 8; Neh. 12:1).

name: Sheba
title: Sheba (son of Raamah)
description: Heb. shebha, the son of Raamah (Gen. 10:7), whose descendants settled with those of Dedan on the Persian Gulf.

name: Sheba
title: Sheba (son of Joktan)
description: Heb. id. A son of Joktan (Gen. 10:28), probably the founder of the Sabeans.

name: Sheba
title: Sheba (son of Jokshan)
description: Heb. id. A son of Jokshan, who was a son of Abraham by Keturah (Gen. 25:3).

name: Sheba
title: Sheba (son of Bichri)
description: Heb. id. A “son of Bichri,” of the family of Becher, the son of Benjamin, and thus of the stem from which Saul was descended (2 Sam. 20:1-22).

name: Shebaniah
title: Shebaniah (1 Chronicles 15:24)
description: A Levite appointed to blow the trumpet before the ark of God (1 Chr. 15:24).

name: Shebaniah
title: Shebaniah (Nehemiah 9:4)
description: Another Levite (Neh. 9:4, 5).

name: Shebaniah
title: Shebaniah (Nehemiah 10:4)
description: A priest who returned from the Captivity with Zerubbabel (Neh. 12:3; marg., or Shebaniah).

name: Shebna
title: Shebna (2 Kings 18:18)
description: Tender youth, “treasurer” over the house in the reign of Hezekiah, i.e., comptroller or governor of the palace. On account of his pride he was ejected from his office, and Eliakim was promoted to it (Isa. 22:15-25).

name: Shecaniah
title: Shecaniah (1 Chronicles 24:11)
description: A priest to whom the tenth lot came forth when David divided the priests (1 Chr. 24:11).

name: Shecaniah
title: Shecaniah (2 Chronicles 31:15)
description: One of the priests who were set “to give to their brethren by courses” of the daily portion (2 Chr. 31:15). Shechani’ah, id.

name: Shechaniah
title: Shechaniah (son of Hananiah)
description: A priest whose sons are mentioned in 1 Chr. 3:21, 22.

name: Shechaniah
title: Shechaniah (son of Jehiel)
description: The father of Shemaiah, who repaired the wall of Jerusalem (Neh. 3:29).

name: Shechaniah
title: Shechaniah (son of Arah)
description: The father-in-law of Tobiah (Neh. 6:18).

name: Shechem
description: The son of Hamor the Hivite (Gen. 33:19; 34).

name: Shechem
title: Shechem (son of Gilead)
description: A descendant of Manasseh (Num. 26:31; Josh. 17:2).

name: Shelah
description: Judah’s third son (Gen. 38:2, 5, 11, 14).

name: Shelemiah
title: Shelemiah (father of Hananiah)
description: The father of Hananiah (Neh. 3:30).

name: Shelemiah
title: Shelemiah (father of Jucal)
description: Father of one of those who accused Jeremiah to Zedekiah (Jer. 37:3; 38:1).

name: Shelemiah
title: Shelemiah (son of Hananiah)
description: Father of a captain of the ward (Jer. 37:13).

name: Shem
description: A name; renown, the first mentioned of the sons of Noah (Gen. 5:32; 6:10). He was probably the eldest of Noah’s sons. The words “brother of Japheth the elder” in Gen. 10:21 are more correctly rendered “the elder brother of Japheth,” as in the Revised Version.

name: Shema
title: Shema (Nehemiah 8:4)
description: One who stood by Ezra when he read the law (Neh. 8:4).

name: Shemaah
description: Rumour, a Benjamite whose sons “came to David to Ziklag” (1 Chr. 12:3).

name: Shemaiah
title: Shemaiah (1 Kings 12:22)
description: A prophet in the reign of Rehoboam (1 Kings 12:22-24).

name: Shemaiah
title: Shemaiah (1 Chronicles 15:8)
description: A Levite in the time of David, who with 200 of his brethren took part in the bringing up of the ark from Obed-edom to Hebron (1 Chr. 15:8).

name: Shemaiah
title: Shemaiah (son of Shimei)
description: The eldest son of Obed-edom (1 Chr. 26:4-8).

name: Shemaiah
title: Shemaiah (2 Chronicles 17:8)
description: One of the Levites whom Jehoshaphat appointed to teach the law (2 Chr. 17:8).

name: Shemaiah
title: Shemaiah (2 Chronicles 31:15)
description: A Levite appointed to “distribute the oblations of the Lord” (2 Chr. 31:15).

name: Shemaiah
title: Shemaiah (son of Delaiah)
description: A false prophet who hindered the rebuilding of Jerusalem (Neh. 6:10).

name: Shemaiah
title: Shemaiah (father of Urijah)
description: The father of Urijah the prophet (Jer. 26:20).

name: Shemaiah
title: Shemaiah (Jeremiah 29:24)
description: A false prophet who opposed Jeremiah (Jer. 29:24-32).

name: Shemaiah
title: Shemaiah (father of Delaiah)
description: The father of a prince in the reign of Jehoiakim (Jer. 36:12).

name: Shemariah
title: Shemariah (1 Chronicles 12:5)
description: One who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:5).

name: Shemeber
description: Soaring on high, the king of Zeboiim, who joined with the other kings in casting off the yoke of Chedorlaomer. After having been reconquered by him, he was rescued by Abraham (Gen. 14:2).

name: Shemiramoth
title: Shemiramoth (1 Chronicles 15:18)
description: A Levite in David’s time (1 Chr. 15:18, 20).

name: Shemiramoth
title: Shemiramoth (2 Chronicles 17:8)
description: A Levite in the reign of Jehoshaphat (2 Chr. 17:8).

name: Shemuel
title: Shemuel (son of Ammihud)
description: The son of Ammihud. He represented Simeon in the division of the land (Num. 34:20).

name: Shemuel
title: Shemuel (son of Tola)
description: A prince of the tribe of Issachar (1 Chr. 7:2).

name: Shephatiah
title: Shephatiah (1 Chronicles 12:5)
description: A Benjamite who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:5).

name: Shephatiah
title: Shephatiah (son of Maachah)
description: A Simeonite prince in David’s time (1 Chr. 27:16).

name: Shephatiah
title: Shephatiah (son of Jehoshaphat)
description: One of Jehoshaphat’s sons (2 Chr. 21:2).

name: Shephatiah
title: Shephatiah (son of Mattan)
description: One of the princes who urged the putting of Jeremiah to death (Jer. 38:1-4).

name: Sheresh
description: Root, a descendant of Manasseh (1 Chr. 7:16).

name: Sherezer
description: One of the messengers whom the children of the Captivity sent to Jerusalem “to pray for them before the Lord” (Zech. 7:2).

name: Shethar
description: A star, a prince at the court of Ahasuerus (Esther 1:14).

name: Shethar-boznai
description: Star of splendour, a Persian officer who vainly attempted to hinder the rebuilding of the temple (Ezra 5:3, 6; 6:6, 13).

name: Sheva
description: The son of Caleb (1 Chr. 2:49).

name: Shimea
title: Shimea (son of Uzza)
description: A Levite of the family of Merari (1 Chr. 6:30).

name: Shimea
title: Shimea (son of Michael)
description: Another Levite of the family of Gershon (1 Chr. 6:39).

name: Shimeah
description: A Benjamite, a descendant of Gibeon (1 Chr. 8:32); called also Shimeam (9:38).

name: Shimei
title: Shimei (son of Laadan)
description: A Levite of the family of Gershon (1 Chr. 6:42).

name: Shimei
title: Shimei (son of Gera)
description: A Benjamite of the house of Saul, who stoned and cursed David when he reached Bahurim in his flight from Jerusalem on the occasion of the rebellion of Absalom (2 Sam. 16:5-13).

name: Shimei
title: Shimei (son of Elah)
description: One of David’s mighty men who refused to acknowledge Adonijah as David’s successor (1 Kings 1:8). He is probably the same person who is called elsewhere (4:18) “the son of Elah.”

name: Shimei
title: Shimei (son of Pedaiah)
description: A son of Pedaiah, the brother of Zerubbabel (1 Chr. 3:19).

name: Shimei
title: Shimei (1 Chronicles 27:27)
description: A Ramathite who was “over the vineyards” of David (1 Chr. 27:27).

name: Shimei
title: Shimei (2 Chronicles 29:14)
description: One of the sons of Heman, who assisted in the purification of the temple (2 Chr. 29:14).

name: Shimhi
description: Famous, a Benjamite (1 Chr. 8:21).

name: Shimri
title: Shimri (father of Jediael)
description: The father of one of the “valiant men” of David’s armies (1 Chr. 11:45).

name: Shimri
title: Shimri (2 Chronicles 29:13)
description: Assisted at the purification of the temple in the time of Hezekiah (2 Chr. 29:13).

name: Shimrith
description: The mother of Jehozabad, who murdered Joash (2 Kings 12:21); called also Shimrith, a Moabitess (2 Chr. 24:26).

name: Shimron
description: Watchman, the fourth son of Issachar (Gen. 46:13; 1 Chr. 7:1; R.V., correctly, “Shimron”).

name: Shimshai
description: The shining one, or sunny, the secretary of Rehum the chancellor, who took part in opposing the rebuilding of the temple after the Captivity (Ezra 4:8, 9, 17-23).

name: Shinab
description: Cooling, the king of Adamah, in the valley of Siddim, who with his confederates was conquered by Chedorlaomer (Gen. 14:2).

name: Shiphrah
description: Beauty, one of the Egyptian midwives (Ex. 1:15).

name: Shiphtan
description: Judicial, an Ephraimite prince at the time of the division of Canaan (Num. 34:24).

name: Shishak
description: Sheshonk I., king of Egypt. His reign was one of great national success, and a record of his wars and conquests adorns the portico of what are called the “Bubastite kings” at Karnak, the ancient Thebes.

name: Shobab
title: Shobab (son of David)
description: One of David’s sons by Bathseheba (2 Sam. 5:14).

name: Shobab
title: Shobab (son of Caleb)
description: One of the sons of Caleb (1 Chr. 2:18), the son of Hezron.

name: Shobach
description: Poured out, the “captain of the host of Hadarezer” when he mustered his vassals and tributaries from beyond “the river Euphrates” (2 Sam. 10:15-18); called also Shophach (1 Chr. 19:16).

name: Shobal
title: Shobal (son of Seir)
description: The second son of Seir the Horite; one of the Horite “dukes” (Gen. 36:20).

name: Shobal
title: Shobal (son of Hur)
description: One of the sons of Caleb, and a descendant of Hur (1 Chr. 2:50, 52; 4:1, 2).

name: Shobi
description: Captor, son of Nahash of Rabbah, the Ammonite. He showed kindness to David when he fled from Jerusalem to Mahanaim (2 Sam. 17:27).

name: Shua
description: A daughter of Heber the Asherite (1 Chr. 7:32).

name: Shuah
title: Shuah (son of Abraham)
description: One of Abraham’s sons by Keturah (Gen. 25:2; Chr. 1:32).

name: Shuah
title: Shuah (father of Daughter of Shuah)
description: A Canaanite whose daughter was married to Judah (1 Chr. 2:3).

name: Shubael
title: Shubael (son of Gershom)
description: One of the descendants of Gershom, who had charge of the temple treasures in the time of David (1 Chr. 23:16; 26:24).

name: Shubael
title: Shubael (son of Heman)
description: One of the sons of Heman; one of those whose duty it was to “lift up the horn” in the temple service (1 Chr. 25:4, 5); called also Shubael (ver. 20).

name: Sibbechai
description: The Lord sustains, one of David’s heroes (1 Chr. 11:29), general of the eighth division of the army (27:11). He slew the giant Saph in the battle of Gob (2 Sam. 21:18; R.V., “Sibbechai”).

name: Sihon
description: Striking down. The whole country on the east of Jordan, from the Arnon to the Jabbok, was possessed by the Amorites, whose king, Sihon, refused to permit the Israelites to pass through his territory, and put his army in array against them.

name: Silas
description: Wood, a prominent member of the church at Jerusalem; also called Silvanus.

name: Simeon
description: The second son of Jacob by Leah (Gen. 29:33). He was associated with Levi in the terrible act of vengeance against Hamor and the Shechemites (34:25, 26).

name: Simeon
title: Simeon (son of Juda)
description: One of the ancestors of Joseph (Luke 3:30).

name: Simeon
title: Simeon (Acts 13:1)
description: Surnamed Niger, i.e., “black,” perhaps from his dark complexion, a teacher of some distinction in the church of Antioch (Acts 13:1-3).

name: Simon
title: Simon Zelotes
description: One of the twelve apostles, called the Canaanite (Matt. 10:4; Mark 3:18). This word “Canaanite” does not mean a native of Canaan, but is derived from the Syriac word Kanean or Kaneniah, which was the name of a Jewish sect.

name: Simon
title: Simon (son of Joseph)
description: One of the brothers of our Lord (Matt. 13:55; Mark 6:3).

name: Simon
title: Simon (Matthew 26:6)
description: A leper of Bethany, in whose house Mary anointed our Lord’s head with ointment “as he sat at meat” (Matt. 26:6-13; Mark 14:3-9).

name: Simon
title: Simon (father of Rufus)
description: A Jew of Cyrene, in North Africa, then a province of Libya. A hundred thousand Jews from Palestine had been settled in this province by Ptolemy Soter (B.C. 323-285), where by this time they had greatly increased in number.

name: Simon
description: The father of Judas Iscariot (John 6:71; 13:2, 26).

name: Simon
title: Simon the Sorcerer
description: A sorcerer of great repute for his magical arts among the Samaritans (Acts 8:9-11). He afterwards became a professed convert to the faith under the preaching of Philip the deacon and evangelist (12, 13).

name: Simon
title: Simon the Tanner
description: A Christian at Joppa, a tanner by trade, with whom Peter on one occasion lodged (Acts 9:43).

name: Simri
description: Watchman, a Levite of the family of Merari (1 Chr. 26:10).

name: Sinite
description: An inhabitant of Sin, near Arka (Gen. 10:17; 1 Chr. 1:15).

name: Sippai
description: Extension, the son of the giant whom Sibbechai slew (2 Sam. 21:18); called also Sippai (1 Chr. 20:4).

name: Sisera
title: Sisera (army captain)
description: The captain of Jabin’s army (Judg. 4:2), which was routed and destroyed by the army of Barak on the plain of Esdraelon. After all was lost he fled to the settlement of Heber the Kenite in the plain of Zaanaim.

name: Sisera
description: The ancestor of some of the Nethinim who returned with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:53; Neh. 7:55).

name: So
description: (Nubian, Sabako), an Ethiopian king who brought Egypt under his sway. He was bribed by Hoshea to help him against the Assyrian monarch Shalmaneser (2 Kings 17:4).

name: Solomon
description: Peaceful, (Heb. Shelomoh), David’s second son by Bathsheba, i.e., the first after their legal marriage (2 Sam. 12). He was probably born about B.C. 1035 (1 Chr. 22:5; 29:1).

name: Sopater
description: The father who saves, probably the same as Sosipater, a kinsman of Paul (Rom. 16:21), a Christian of the city of Berea who accompanied Paul into Asia (Acts 20:4-6).

name: Sosthenes
description: Safe in strength, the chief ruler of the synagogue at Corinth, who was seized and beaten by the mob in the presence of Gallio, the Roman governor, when he refused to proceed against Paul at the instigation of the Jews (Acts 18:12-17).

name: Stachys
description: Spike; an ear of corn, a convert at Rome whom Paul salutes (Rom. 16:9).

name: Stephanas
description: Crown, a member of the church at Corinth, whose family were among those the apostle had baptized (1 Cor. 1:16; 16:15, 17).

name: Stephen
description: One of the seven deacons, who became a preacher of the gospel. He was the first Christian martyr. His personal character and history are recorded in Acts 6.

name: Susanna
description: Lily, with other pious women, ministered to Jesus (Luke 8:3).

name: Susi
description: The father of Gaddi, who was one of the twelve spies (Num. 13:11).

name: Syntyche
description: Fortunate; affable, a female member of the church at Philippi, whom Paul beseeches to be of one mind with Euodias (Phil. 4:2, 3).

name: Tabbaoth
description: Impressions; rings, “the children of,” returned from the Captivity (Ezra 2:43).

name: Tabeal
description: Goodness of God, the father of one whom the kings of Syria and Samaria in vain attempted to place on the throne of Ahaz (Isa. 7:6).

name: Tabeel
description: A Persian governor of Samaria, who joined others in the attempt to prevent the rebuilding of Jerusalem (Ezra 4:7).

name: Tabrimon
description: Good is Rimmon, the father of Benhadad, king of Syria (1 Kings 15:18).

name: Tahpenes
description: The wife of Pharaoh, who gave her sister in marriage to Hadad the Edomite (1 Kings 11:19, 20).

name: Talmai
title: Talmai (son of Anak)
description: One of the Anakim of Hebron, who were slain by the men of Judah under Caleb (Num. 13:22; Josh. 15:14; Judg. 1:10).

name: Talmai
title: Talmai (son of Ammihud)
description: A king of Geshur, to whom Absalom fled after he had put Amnon to death (2 Sam. 3:3; 13:37). His daughter, Maachah, was one of David’s wives, and the mother of Absalom (1 Chr. 3:2).

name: Talmon
description: A Levite porter (1 Chr. 9:17; Neh. 11:19).

name: Tamar
title: Tamar (mother of Pharez)
description: The daughter-in-law of Judah, to whose eldest son, Er, she was married (Gen. 38:6). After her husband’s death, she was married to Onan, his brother (8), and on his death, Judah promised to her that his third son, Shelah, would become her husband.

name: Tamar
title: Tamar (daughter of David)
description: A daughter of David (2 Sam. 13:1-32; 1 Chr. 3:9), whom Amnon shamefully outraged and afterwards “hated exceedingly,” thereby illustrating the law of human nature noticed even by the heathen, “Proprium humani ingenii est odisse quem laeseris”, i.e., “It is the property of human nature to hate one…

name: Tamar
title: Tamar (daughter of Absalom)
description: A daughter of Absalom (2 Sam. 14:27).

name: Tanhumeth
description: Consolation, a Netophathite; one of the captains who supported Gedaliah (2 Kings 25:23; Jer. 40:8).

name: Tarshish
title: Tarshish (son of Javan)
description: One of the “sons” of Javan (Gen. 10:4; 1 Chr. 1:7).

name: Tartan
description: One of Sennacherib’s messengers to Hezekiah (2 Kings 18:17).

name: Tatnai
description: Gift, a Persian governor (Heb. pehah, i.e., “satrap;” modern “pasha”) “on this side the river”, i.e., of the whole tract on the west of the Euphrates.

name: Temeni
description: One of the sons of Ashur, the father of Tekoa (1 Chr. 4:6).

name: Terah
