description: The wanderer; loiterer, for some unknown reason emigrated with his family from his native mountains in the north to the plains of Mesopotamia.

name: Teresh
description: Severe, a eunuch or chamberlain in the palace of Ahasuerus, who conspired with another to murder him. The plot was detected by Mordecai, and the conspirators were put to death (Esther 2:21; 6:2).

name: Tertullus
description: A modification of “Tertius;” a Roman advocate, whom the Jews employed to state their case against Paul in the presence of Felix (Acts 24:1-9).

name: Thahash
description: A badger, a son of Nahor, Abraham’s brother (Gen. 22:24).

name: the giant in Gath
description: Heb. ‘Anakim (Deut. 2:10, 11, 21; Josh. 11:21, 22; 14:12, 15; called “sons of Anak,” Num. 13:33; “children of Anak,” 13:22; Josh. 15:14), a nomad race of giants descended from Arba (Josh. 14:15), the father of Anak, that dwelt in the south of Palestine near Hebron (Gen. 23:2; Josh. 15:13).

name: Theophilus
description: Lover of God, a Christian, probably a Roman, to whom Luke dedicated both his Gospel (Luke 1:3) and the Acts of the Apostles (1:1).

name: Theudas
description: Thanksgiving, referred to by Gamaliel in his speech before the council at Jerusalem (Acts 5:36). He headed an insurrection against the Roman authority.

name: Thomas
description: Twin, one of the twelve (Matt. 10:3; Mark 3:18, etc.). He was also called Didymus (John 11:16; 20:24), which is the Greek equivalent of the Hebrew name.

name: Tiberius
description: I.e., as known in Roman history, Tiberius Claudius Nero, only mentioned in Luke 3:1. He was the stepson of Augustus, whom he succeeded on the throne, A.D. 14.

name: Tibni
description: Building of Jehovah, the son of Ginath, a man of some position, whom a considerable number of the people chose as monarch. For the period of four years he contended for the throne with Omri (1 Kings 16:21, 22), who at length gained the mastery, and became sole monarch of Israel.

name: Tidal
description: (in the LXX. called “Thorgal”), styled the “king of nations” (Gen. 14:1-9). Mentioned as Tudkhula on Arioch’s brick (see facing page 139).

name: Tilgath-pilneser
description: An Assyrian king. It has been a question whether he was identical with Tiglath-pileser III. (q.v.), or was his predecessor.

name: Timaeus
description: Defiled, the father of blind Bartimaeus (Mark 10:46).

name: Timnah
description: A “duke” or sheik of Edom (Gen. 36:40).

name: Timon
description: Honouring, one of the seven deacons at Jerusalem (Acts 6:5). Nothing further is known of him.

name: Timotheus
description: Honouring God, a young disciple who was Paul’s companion in many of his journeyings. His mother, Eunice, and his grandmother, Lois, are mentioned as eminent for their piety (2 Tim. 1:5).

name: Tiras
description: The youngest of the sons of Japheth (Gen. 10:2; 1 Chr. 1:5).

name: Tirhakah
description: The last king of Egypt of the Ethiopian (the fifteenth) dynasty. He was the brother-in-law of So (q.v.). He probably ascended the throne about B.C. 692, having been previously king of Ethiopia (2 Kings 19:9; Isa. 37:9), which with Egypt now formed one nation.

name: Tirzah
description: The youngest of Zelophehad’s five daughters (Num. 26:33; Josh. 17:3).

name: Titus
description: Honourable, was with Paul and Barnabas at Antioch, and accompanied them to the council at Jerusalem (Gal. 2:1-3; Acts 15:2), although his name nowhere occurs in the Acts of the Apostles.

name: Tobadonijah
description: Good is Jehovah, my Lord, a Levite sent out by Jehoshaphat to instruct the people of Judah in the law (2 Chr. 17:8).

name: Tobiah
description: Pleasing to Jehovah, the “servant,” the “Ammonite,” who joined with those who opposed the rebuilding of Jerusalem after the Exile (Neh. 2:10).

name: Tobijah
title: Tobijah (2 Chronicles 17:8)
description: Id., a Levite sent out through Judah by Jehoshaphat to teach the people (2 Chr. 17:8).

name: Togarmah
description: A son of Gomer, and grandson of Japheth (Gen. 10:3).

name: Toi
description: A king of Hamath, who sent “Joram his son unto King David to salute him,” when he “heard that David had smitten all the host of Hadadezer” (2 Sam. 8:9, 10). Called Tou (1 Chr. 18:9, 10).

name: Tola
title: Tola (son of Issachar)
description: Eldest son of Issachar (Gen. 46:13).

name: Tola
title: Tola (son of Puah)
description: A judge of the tribe of Issachar who “judged” Israel twenty-three years (Judg. 10:1, 2), when he died, and was buried in Shamir. He was succeeded by Jair.

name: Trophimus
description: A foster-child, an Ephesian who accompanied Paul during a part of his third missionary journey (Acts 20:4; 21:29). He was with Paul in Jerusalem, and the Jews, supposing that the apostle had brought him with him into the temple, raised a tumult which resulted in Paul’s imprisonment.

name: Tubal
description: The fifth son of Japheth (Gen. 10:2).

name: Tubal-cain
description: The son of Lamech and Zillah, “an instructor of every artificer in brass and iron” (Gen. 4:22; R.V., “the forger of every cutting instrument of brass and iron”).

name: Tychicus
description: Chance, an Asiatic Christian, a “faithful minister in the Lord” (Eph. 6:21, 22), who, with Trophimus, accompanied Paul on a part of his journey from Macedonia to Jerusalem (Acts 20:4).

name: Tyrannus
description: Prince, a Greek rhetorician, in whose “school” at Ephesus Paul disputed daily for the space of two years with those who came to him (Acts 19:9). Some have supposed that he was a Jew, and that his “school” was a private synagogue.

name: Ucal
description: The name of a person to whom Agur’s words are addressed (Prov. 30:1).

name: Unni
title: Unni (1 Chronicles 15:18)
description: A Levite whom David appointed to take part in bringing the ark up to Jerusalem from the house of Obed-edom by playing the psaltery on that occasion (1 Chr. 15:18, 20).

name: Unni
title: Unni (Nehemiah 12:9)
description: A Levite who returned with Zerubbabel from the Captivity (Neh. 12:9).

name: Uriah
description: A Hittite, the husband of Bathsheba, whom David first seduced, and then after Uriah’s death married. He was one of the band of David’s “mighty men.”

name: Uriel
title: Uriel (son of Tahath)
description: A Kohathite ancestor of the prophet Samuel (1 Chr. 6:36).

name: Uriel
title: Uriel (1 Chronicles 15:5)
description: The chief of the Kohathites at the time when the ark was brought up to Jerusalem (1 Chr. 15:5, 11).

name: Uriel
title: Uriel (father of Maachah)
description: The father of Michaiah, one of Rehoboam’s wives, and mother of Abijah (2 Chr. 13:2).

name: Urijah
title: Urijah (son of Koz)
description: The father of Meremoth, mentioned in Ezra 8:33.

name: Urijah
title: Urijah (2 Kings 16:10)
description: A high priest in the time of Ahaz (2 Kings 16:10-16), at whose bidding he constructed an idolatrous altar like one the king had seen at Damascus, to be set up instead of the brazen altar.

name: Urijah
title: Urijah (Nehemiah 8:4)
description: One of the priests who stood at the right hand of Ezra’s pulpit when he read and expounded the law (Neh. 8:4).

name: Urijah
title: Urijah (son of Shemaiah)
description: A prophet of Kirjath-jearim in the reign of Jehoiakim, king of Judah (Jer. 26:20-23). He fled into Egypt from the cruelty of the king, but having been brought back he was beheaded and his body “cast into the graves of the common people.”

name: Uz
title: Uz (son of Aram)
description: The son of Aram, and grandson of Shem (Gen. 10:23; 1 Chr. 1:17).

name: Uz
title: Uz (son of Dishan)
description: One of the Horite “dukes” in the land of Edom (Gen. 36:28).

name: Uzal
description: A wanderer, a descendant of Joktan (Gen. 10:27; 1 Chr. 1:21), the founder apparently of one of the Arab tribes; the name also probably of the province they occupied and of their chief city.

name: Uzzah
description: Strength, a son of Abinadab, in whose house the men of Kirjath-jearim placed the ark when it was brought back from the land of the Philistines (1 Sam. 7:1).

name: Uzzi
title: Uzzi (son of Bukki)
description: The son of Bukki, and a descendant of Aaron (1 Chr. 6:5, 51; Ezra 7:4).

name: Uzzi
title: Uzzi (son of Tola)
description: A grandson of Issachar (1 Chr. 7:2, 3).

name: Uzzi
title: Uzzi (son of Bela)
description: A son of Bela, and grandson of Benjamin (1 Chr. 7:7).

name: Uzzi
title: Uzzi (son of Michri)
description: A Benjamite, a chief in the tribe (1 Chr. 9:8).

name: Uzzi
title: Uzzi (son of Bani)
description: A son of Bani. He had the oversight of the Levites after the return from captivity (Neh. 11:22).

name: Uzzi
title: Uzzi (Nehemiah 12:19)
description: The head of the house of Jedaiah, one of “the chief of the priests” (Neh. 12:19).

name: Uzzi
title: Uzzi (Nehemiah 12:42)
description: A priest who assisted in the dedication of the walls of Jerusalem (Neh. 12:42).

name: Uzziah
description: One of Amaziah’s sons, whom the people made king of Judah in his father’s stead (2 Kings 14:21; 2 Chr. 26:1). His long reign of about fifty-two years was “the most prosperous excepting that of Jehosaphat since the time of Solomon.”

name: Uzziah
title: Uzziah (father of Jehonathan)
description: The father of Jehonathan, one of David’s overseers (1 Chr. 27:25).

name: Uzziel
description: One of the sons of Kohath, and uncle of Aaron (Ex. 6:18; Lev. 10:4).

name: Uzziel
title: Uzziel (son of Bela)
description: A son of Bela, and grandson of Benjamin (1 Chr. 7:7).

name: Uzziel
title: Uzziel (son of Heman)
description: One of the sons of Heman (1 Chr. 25:4); called also Azareel (18).

name: Uzziel
title: Uzziel (2 Chronicles 29:14)
description: A son of Jeduthan (2 Chr. 29:14).

name: Uzziel
title: Uzziel (son of Harhaiah)
description: The son of Harhaiah (Neh. 3:8).

name: Vajezatha
description: Purity; worthy of honour, one of Haman’s sons, whom the Jews slew in the palace of Shushan (Esther 9:9).

name: Vashti
description: Beautiful, the queen of Ahasuerus, who was deposed from her royal dignity because she refused to obey the king when he desired her to appear in the banqueting hall of Shushan the palace (Esther 1:10-12).

name: Zabad
title: Zabad (son of Shimeath)
description: The son of Shemath. He conspired against Joash, king of Judah, and slew him (2 Chr. 24:25, 26). He is called also Jozachar (2 Kings 12:21).

name: Zabad
title: Zabad (son of Ahlai)
description: One of David’s valiant men (1 Chr. 11:41), the descendant of Ahlai, of the “children of Sheshan” (2:31).

name: Zabbai
title: Zabbai (father of Baruch)
description: The father of Baruch, who “earnestly repaired” part of the wall of Jerusalem (Neh. 3:20; marg., “Zaccai”).

name: Zabdi
title: Zabdi (son of Zerah)
description: An ancestor of Achan (Josh. 7:1, 17, 18). He is probably the “Zimri” of 1 Chr. 2:6.

name: Zabdi
title: Zabdi (1 Chronicles 27:27)
description: Called “the Shiphmite,” one of David’s officers, who had charge of his vineyards (1 Chr. 27:27).

name: Zabdiel
title: Zabdiel (father of Jashobeam)
description: The father of Jashobeam, who was one of David’s officers (1 Chr. 27:2).

name: Zabdiel
title: Zabdiel (Nehemiah 11:14)
description: An overseer of the priests after the Captivity (Neh. 11:14).

name: Zabud
description: Gift, the son of Nathan, who was “king’s friend” in the court of Solomon (1 Kings 4:5).

name: Zaccai
description: Pure, one whose “sons” returned with Zerubbabel to Jerusalem (Ezra 2:9; Neh. 7:14).

name: Zacchaeus
description: Pure, a superintendant of customs; a chief tax-gather (publicanus) at Jericho (Luke 19:1-10). “The collection of customs at Jericho, which at this time produced and exported a considerable quantity of balsam, was undoubtedly an important post, and would account for Zacchaeus being a rich man.”

name: Zaccur
title: Zaccur (father of Shammua)
description: Father of Shammua, who was one of the spies sent out by Moses (Num. 13:4).

name: Zaccur
title: Zaccur (son of Jaaziah)
description: A Merarite Levite (1 Chr. 24:27).

name: Zaccur
title: Zaccur (son of Asaph)
description: A son of Asaph, and chief of one of the courses of singers as arranged by David (1 Chr. 25:2, 10).

name: Zaccur
title: Zaccur (son of Imri)
description: Son of Imri (Neh. 3:2).

name: Zaccur
title: Zaccur (son of Mattaniah)
description: The son of Mattaniah (Neh. 13:13).

name: Zachariah
description: Son of Jeroboam II., king of Israel. On the death of his father there was an interregnum of ten years, at the end of which he succeeded to the throne, which he occupied only six months, having been put to death by Shallum, who usurped the throne.

name: Zacharias
title: Zacharias (father of John)
description: A priest of the course of Abia, the eighth of the twenty-four courses into which the priests had been originally divided by David (1 Chr. 23:1-19).

name: Zacharias
title: Zacharias (son of Jehoiada)
description: The son or grandson of Jehoiada, the high priest in the times of Ahaziah and Joash.

name: Zacher
description: Memorial, a son of Jehiel (1 Chr. 8:31; 9:35); called Zechariah (9:37).

name: Zadok
description: A son of Ahitub, of the line of Eleazer (2 Sam. 8:17; 1 Chr. 24:3), high priest in the time of David (2 Sam. 20:25) and Solomon (1 Kings 4:4).

name: Zadok
title: Zadok (father of Jerushah)
description: The father of Jerusha, who was wife of King Uzziah, and mother of King Jotham (2 Kings 15:33; 2 Chr. 27:1).

name: Zadok
title: Zadok (son of Baana)
description: The sons of Baana, one of those who assisted in rebuilding the wall of Jerusalem (Neh. 3:4).

name: Zadok
title: Zadok (Nehemiah 13:13)
description: “The scribe” set over the treasuries of the temple by Nehemiah along with a priest and a Levite (Neh. 13:13).

name: Zalmunna
description: One of the two kings of Midian whom the “Lord delivered” into the hands of Gideon. He was slain afterwards with Zebah (Judg. 8:5-21).

name: Zattu
description: Id., one whose descendants returned from the Captivity with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:8; Neh. 7:13); probably the same as Zatthu.

name: Zavan
description: Terror, one of the “dukes of Edom” (Gen. 36:27); called also Zavan (1 Chr. 1:42).

name: Zaza
description: Plenty, a descendant of Judah (1 Chr. 2:33).

name: Zebadiah
title: Zebadiah (son of Beriah)
description: A son of Beriah (1 Chr. 8:15).

name: Zebadiah
title: Zebadiah (son of Meshelemiah)
description: A Korhite porter of the Lord’s house (1 Chr. 26:2). Three or four others of this name are also mentioned.

name: Zebadiah
title: Zebadiah (son of Asahel)
description: A son of Asahel, Joab’s brother (1 Chr. 27:7).

name: Zebadiah
title: Zebadiah (2 Chronicles 17:8)
description: A Levite who took part as one of the teachers in the system of national education instituted by Jehoshaphat (2 Chr. 17:7, 8).

name: Zebadiah
title: Zebadiah (son of Ishmael)
description: The son of Ishmael, “the ruler of the house of Judah in all the king’s matters” (2 Chr. 19:8-11).

name: Zebah
description: Man-killer, or sacrifice, one of the two kings who led the vast host of the Midianites who invaded the land of Israel, and over whom Gideon gained a great and decisive victory (Judg. 8).

name: Zebedee
description: A Galilean fisherman, the husband of Salome (q.v.), and the father of James and John, two of our Lord’s disciples (Matt. 4:21; 27:56; Mark 15:40).

name: Zebudah
description: Given, the wife of Josiah and mother of Jehoiakim (2 Kings 23:36).

name: Zebul
description: Habitation, the governor of Shechem under Abimelech (Judg. 9:28, 30, 36). He informed his master of the intention of the people of Shechem to transfer their allegiance to the Hivite tribe of Hamor.

name: Zebulun
description: Dwelling, the sixth and youngest son of Jacob and Leah (Gen. 30:20). Little is known of his personal history. He had three sons (46:14).

name: Zechariah
title: Zechariah (father of Abijah)
description: The father of Abijah, who was the mother of Hezekiah (2 Chr. 29:1).

name: Zechariah
title: Zechariah (1 Chronicles 5:7)
description: One of the chiefs of the tribe of Reuben (1 Chr. 5:7).

name: Zechariah
title: Zechariah (son of Meshelemiah)
description: A Levite who assisted at the bringing up of the ark from the house of Obededom (1 Chr. 15:20-24).

name: Zechariah
title: Zechariah (son of Isshiah)
description: A Kohathite Levite (1 Chr. 24:25).

name: Zechariah
title: Zechariah (father of Iddo)
description: A Merarite Levite (1 Chr. 27:21).

name: Zechariah
title: Zechariah (2 Chronicles 17:7)
description: One who assisted in teaching the law to the people in the time of Jehoshaphat (2 Chr. 17:7).

name: Zechariah
title: Zechariah (son of Benaiah)
description: A Levite of the sons of Asaph (2 Chr. 20:14).

name: Zechariah
title: Zechariah (son of Jehoshaphat)
description: One of Jehoshaphat’s sons (2 Chr. 21:2).

name: Zechariah
title: Zechariah (2 Chronicles 26:5)
description: A prophet, who had “understanding in the seeing of God,” in the time of Uzziah, who was much indebted to him for his wise counsel (2 Chr. 26:5). Besides these, there is a large number of persons mentioned in Scripture bearing this name of whom nothing is known.

name: Zechariah
title: Zechariah (2 Chronicles 35:8)
description: One of the “rulers of the house of God” (2 Chr. 35:8).

name: Zechariah
title: Zechariah (son of Berechiah)
description: A prophet of Judah, the eleventh of the twelve minor prophets. Like Ezekiel, he was of priestly extraction. He describes himself (1:1) as “the son of Berechiah.”

name: Zedekiah
description: The last king of Judah. He was the third son of Josiah, and his mother’s name was Hamutal, the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah, and hence he was the brother of Jehoahaz (2 Kings 23:31; 24:17, 18).

name: Zedekiah
title: Zedekiah (son of Chenaanah)
description: The son of Chenaanah, a false prophet in the days of Ahab (1 Kings 22:11, 24; 2 Chr. 18:10, 23).

name: Zedekiah
title: Zedekiah (son of Hananiah)
description: The son of Hananiah, a prince of Judah in the days of Jehoiakim (Jer. 36:12).

name: Zeeb
description: The wolf, one of the two leaders of the great Midianite host which invaded Israel and was utterly routed by Gideon.

name: Zelek
description: Cleft, an Ammonite; one of David’s valiant men (2 Sam. 23:37).

name: Zelophehad
description: First-born, of the tribe of Manasseh, and of the family of Gilead; died in the wilderness.

name: Zemarite
description: The designation of one of the Phoenician tribes (Gen. 10:18) who inhabited the town of Sumra, at the western base of the Lebanon range. In the Amarna tablets (B.C. 1400) Zemar, or Zumur, was one of the most important of the Phoenician cities, but it afterwards almost disappears from history.

name: Zemira
description: Vine-dresser, a Benjamite; one of the sons of Becher (1 Chr. 7:8).

name: Zenas
description: A disciple called “the lawyer,” whom Paul wished Titus to bring with him (Titus 3:13). Nothing more is known of him.

name: Zephaniah
title: Zephaniah (son of Maaseiah)
description: The son of Maaseiah, the “second priest” in the reign of Zedekiah, often mentioned in Jeremiah as having been sent from the king to inquire (Jer. 21:1) regarding the coming woes which he had denounced, and to entreat the prophet’s intercession that the judgment threatened might be averted (Jer.…

name: Zephaniah
title: Zephaniah (father of Josiah)
description: The father of Josiah, the priest who dwelt in Jerusalem when Darius issued the decree that the temple should be rebuilt (Zech. 6:10).

name: Zerah
description: A son of Tamar (Gen. 38:30); called also Zara (Matt. 1:3).

name: Zerah
title: Zerah (son of Adaiah)
description: A Gershonite Levite (1 Chr. 6:21, 41).

name: Zerah
title: Zerah (2 Chronicles 14:9)
description: An “Ethiopian,” probably Osorkon II., the successor of Shishak on the throne of Egypt. With an enormous army, the largest we read of in Scripture, he invaded the kingdom of Judah in the days of Asa (2 Chr. 14:9-15).

name: Zerah
title: Zerah (son of Simeon)
description: One of the sons of Simeon (Gen. 46:10; Ex. 6:15).

name: Zeresh
description: Star of Venus, the wife of Haman, whom she instigated to prepare a gallows for Mordecai (Esther 5:10).

name: Zeruah
description: Stricken, mother of Jeroboam, the first king of the ten tribes (1 Kings 11:26).

name: Zerubbabel
description: The seed of Babylon, the son of Salathiel or Shealtiel (Hag. 1:1; Zorobabel, Matt. 1:12); called also the son of Pedaiah (1 Chr. 3:17-19), i.e., according to a frequent usage of the word “son;” the grandson or the nephew of Salathiel.

name: Zeruiah
description: Stricken of the Lord, David’s sister, and the mother of Abishai, Joab, and Asahel (1 Chr. 2:16), who were the three leading heroes of David’s army, and being his nephews, they were admitted to the closest companionship with him.

name: Zetham
description: Olive planter, a Levite (1 Chr. 23:8).

name: Zia
description: Fear, a Gadite (1 Chr. 5:13).

name: Ziba
description: Post; statue, “a servant of the house of Saul” (2 Sam. 9:2), who informed David that Mephibosheth, a son of Jonathan, was alive. He afterwards dealt treacherously toward Mephibosheth, whom he slanderously misrepresented to David.

name: Zibia
description: Gazelle, a Benjamite (1 Chr. 8:9).

name: Zibiah
description: The mother of King Joash (2 Kings 12:1; 2 Chr. 24:1).

name: Zichri
title: Zichri (son of Shimhi)
description: A Benjamite chief (1 Chr. 8:19).

name: Zichri
title: Zichri (son of Shashak)
description: Another of the same tribe (1 Chr. 8:23).

name: Zichri
title: Zichri (son of Asaph)
description: A Levite, one of the sons of Asaph (Neh. 11:17); probably the same as Zichri (1 Chr. 9:15), and Zaccur (Neh. 12:35).

name: Zidkijah
description: The Lord is righteous, one who sealed the covenant with Nehemiah (Neh. 10:1).

name: Zidon
description: A fishery, a town on the Mediterranean coast, about 25 miles north of Tyre. It received its name from the “first-born” of Canaan, the grandson of Noah (Gen. 10:15, 19).

name: Ziha
title: Ziha (Ezra 2:43)
description: The name of a family of Nethinim (Ezra 2:43; Neh. 7:46).

name: Ziha
title: Ziha (Nehemiah 11:21)
description: A ruler among the Nethinim (Neh. 11:21).

name: Zillah
description: Shadow, one of the wives of Lamech, of the line of Cain, and mother of Tubal-cain (Gen. 4:19, 22).

name: Zilpah
description: Drooping, Leah’s handmaid, and the mother of Gad and Asher (Gen. 30:9-13).

name: Zilthai
title: Zilthai (1 Chronicles 12:20)
description: One of the captains of the tribe of Manasseh who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:20).

name: Zimmah
title: Zimmah (son of Shimei)
description: A Gershonite Levite (1 Chr. 6:20).

name: Zimmah
title: Zimmah (father of Joah)
description: The father of Joah (2 Chr. 29:12).

name: Zimran
description: Vine-dressers; celebrated, one of the sons of Abraham by Keturah (Gen. 25:2).

name: Zimri
title: Zimri (1 Kings 16:9)
description: Murdered Elah at Tirzah, and succeeded him on the throne of Israel (1 Kings 16:8-10). He reigned only seven days, for Omri, whom the army elected as king, laid siege to Tirzah, whereupon Zimri set fire to the palace and perished amid its ruins (11-20).

name: Ziph
description: A son of Jehaleleel (1 Chr. 4:16).

name: Ziphah
description: A descendant of Judah (1 Chr. 4:16).

name: Zippor
description: A little bird, the father of Balak, king of Moab (Num. 22:2, 4).

name: Zipporah
description: A female bird. Reuel’s daughter, who became the wife of Moses (Ex. 2:21).

name: Zithri
description: The Lord protects, a Levite, son of Uzziel (Ex. 6:22).

name: Ziza
title: Ziza (son of Shiphi)
description: A Simeonite prince (1 Chr. 4:37-43).

name: Ziza
title: Ziza (son of Rehoboam)
description: A son of Rehoboam (2 Chr. 11:20).

name: Zizah
description: A Gershonite Levite (1 Chr. 23:11).

name: Zohar
description: The father of Ephron the Hittite (Gen. 23:8).

name: Zoheth
description: Snatching (?), one of the sons of Ishi (1 Chr. 4:20).

name: Zophah
description: Spreading out, a son of Helem (1 Chr. 7:35), a chief of Asher.

name: Zophar
description: Chirping, one of Job’s friends who came to condole with him in his distress (Job 2:11. The LXX. render here “king of the Mineans” = Ma’in, Maonites, Judg. 10:12, in Southern Arabia). He is called a Naamathite, or an inhabitant of some unknown place called Naamah.

name: Zuph
description: Honeycomb, a Kohathite Levite, ancestor of Elkanah and Samuel (1 Sam. 1:1); called also Zophai (1 Chr. 6:26).

name: Zur
title: Zur (Numbers 31:8)
description: One of the five Midianite kings whom the Israelites defeated and put to death (Num. 31:8).

name: Zuriel
description: Rock of God, chief of the family of the Merarites (Num. 3:35) at the time of the Exodus.

name: Zurishaddai
description: Rock of the Almighty, the father of Shelumiel, who was chief of the tribe of Simeon when Israel was encamped at Sinai (Num. 1:6; 2:12).
